01.1Chapter 1 — Understanding reasoning models

Defining reasoning in the context of LLMs

Is section me hum samjhenge ki LLM ke context me reasoning ka matlab kya hota hai — aur ek aam LLM aur ek reasoning model me asal farak kya hai.

Reasoning ka practical matlab

  • Is book me reasoning ka matlab koi philosophical definition nahi hai — ye ek practical engineering definition hai.
  • LLM ke context me reasoning ka matlab hai: model final answer dene se pehle intermediate steps generate kare.
  • Ye intermediate steps do tareekon se dikh sakte hain — ek visible step-by-step explanation ke roop me, ya <think>...</think> jaise special tags ke andar chhup kar.
  • Core idea ek hi hai: model seedha conclusion par jump karne ke bajay, problem solve karne ke liye tokens kharch kare — beech ke steps likhe.

Reasoning model kya hota hai?

  • Reasoning model ka matlab hai: ek aisa LLM jise training ya prompting techniques se improve kiya gaya ho, taaki wo aise intermediate steps produce kare.
  • Isse complex tasks par accuracy aksar badh jaati hai — jaise coding, logical puzzles aur math problems.
  • Ye steps dikhne se user ko ye bhi samajh aata hai ki model answer tak kaise pahuncha — sirf answer milna hi kaafi nahi hota.

Chain-of-thought (CoT)

  • Intermediate steps generate karne ki is style ko chain-of-thought (CoT) kehte hain.
  • Log aksar kehte hain ki model problem ko "step by step sochta hai" — matlab wo apni intermediate reasoning ko explicit aur follow karne layak bana deta hai.
  • Is book me reasoning aur thinking words isi common engineering sense me use hote hain.
  • Important: iska matlab ye nahi hai ki LLM waise hi sochta hai jaise insaan sochta hai. Ye sirf ek useful tarika hai us behaviour ko describe karne ka.

Do tarah ki soch — tez vs dheemi

  • Insaan ki soch ko do styles me baanta ja sakta hai: ek tez, automatic style — jaise pehchana hua chehra dekh kar turant naam yaad aana — aur ek dheemi, step-by-step style — jaise ek mushkil math problem ko stages me solve karna.
  • Ek aam LLM zyadatar pehle style jaisa behave karta hai: turant, pattern se, seedha answer.
  • Reasoning model dusre style ki taraf badhta hai: wo pehle steps likhta hai, phir answer deta hai — jaise dheemi soch me hota hai.
  • Lekin yaad rakho: LLM ke steps statistical prediction se bante hain, insaan ki tarah deliberate logic se nahi.

Reasoning deterministic nahi hota

  • Ek symbolic logic engine ya theorem prover strict, rule-based steps follow karta hai — har step fixed hota hai aur hamesha same result deta hai.
  • Analogy: recipe ko exactly follow karo to hamesha wahi dish banegi. Wahi deterministic reasoning hai.
  • Iske ulta, ek LLM apne reasoning steps ko autoregressively generate karta hai — matlab ek token at a time, training data ke statistical patterns ke basis par.
  • Isliye LLM ke reasoning steps convincing lag sakte hain, lekin unke logically sound hone ki koi guarantee nahi hoti.
  • Ye book isi liye fundamental techniques par focus karti hai jo LLM-based reasoning ko improve karti hain — taaki LLM complex tasks ko behtar handle kar sake.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Reasoning = final answer se pehle intermediate steps generate karna.
  • CoT = chain-of-thought, step-by-step reasoning ka sabse common naam.
  • Reasoning steps visible bhi ho sakte hain aur <think> tags me chhupe bhi.
  • LLM reasoning probabilistic hota hai, deterministic rule-based logic nahi.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 1

01.2Chapter 1 — Understanding reasoning models

Understanding the standard LLM training pipeline

Reasoning techniques ko samajhne se pehle, ye jaanna zaroori hai ki ek aam LLM train kaise hota hai — kyunki reasoning methods isi pipeline ke upar lagaye jaate hain.

Do stages: pre-training aur post-training

  • Ek conventional LLM ki training aam taur par do stages me hoti hai: pre-training aur post-training.
  • Kuch recent approaches beech me ek mid-training stage bhi batate hain — jaise code, math ya long-context data par training continue karna — lekin is book me use bhi pre-training ke andar hi count kiya gaya hai, taaki terminology simple rahe.

Stage 1 — Pre-training

  • Pre-training me model ko massive amounts of unlabeled text par train kiya jaata hai — aksar kai terabytes data, yaani trillions of tokens: books, websites, research articles aur bahut kuch.
  • Goal simple hai: next token predict karna — text me agla word (token) kya aayega.
  • Ye training bahut mehengi hoti hai: hazaaron GPUs, kai mahine, aur millions of dollars ka kharcha.
  • Iske baad model coherent, insaan jaisa text generate karne lagta hai — aur kuch emergent properties bhi dikhane lagta hai, matlab wo tasks bhi karne lagta hai jinke liye use explicitly train nahi kiya gaya tha, jaise translation aur code generation.

Token kya hota hai?

  • Token text ki ek chhoti unit hai jise language model process karta hai — ye ek poora word, word ka hissa, ya punctuation bhi ho sakta hai.
  • Example: sentence "An LLM can be useful." ko tokenizer is tarah tod sakta hai: "An", " L", "LM", " can", " be", " useful", "."
  • Ye tokens phir numerical IDs me convert hote hain, jinhe model ingest kar sakta hai.
  • Tokenizer khud LLM ka hissa nahi hota, lekin text processing aur generation pipeline ka ek critical component hai.

Stage 2 — Post-training

  • Pre-trained model sirf ek base model hota hai. Post-training me do key techniques use hoti hain:
  • Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) — jise instruction tuning bhi kehte hain. Ye model ko sikhata hai ki user ke instructions ko kaise follow kare — question-answering, summarizing, translating jaise tasks.
  • Preference tuning — ye responses ko human preferences ke hisaab se refine karta hai. Iska ek famous implementation hai Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF).
  • Short me: pre-training = "raw language prediction", post-training = task samajhna + pasand ke hisaab se style.

Ek example se samjho

  • Prompt: "sleep aur health ke relation ka summary do."
  • Pre-trained model: relevant lekin unfocused answer dega — instruction ko directly follow nahi karega.
  • Instruction-tuned model: concise aur accurate summary dega, prompt ke hisaab se.
  • Preference-tuned model: usi summary ko friendly tone aur engaging language me dega — zyada relatable aur user-centered.

Ek important nuance

  • Instruction-tuned model bhi abhi tak ek "chatbot" nahi hota.
  • Chat interface ek aur layer add karta hai: system prompt, conversation history management aur orchestration — jo multi-turn, interactive setting me responses ko guide karta hai.
  • Is book me hum already pre-trained aur post-trained model ko load karke shuru karte hain — taaki focus sirf reasoning methods par rahe, expensive training stages par nahi.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Pre-training: trillions of tokens par next-token prediction.
  • Post-training: instruction tuning (SFT) + preference tuning (jaise RLHF).
  • Token = word, subword ya punctuation — tokenizer text ko token IDs me badalta hai.
  • Reasoning methods inhi stages ke baad, base model ke upar apply hote hain.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 1

01.3Chapter 1 — Understanding reasoning models

Improving LLM reasoning with training and inference techniques

Reasoning LLMs public eye me tab aaye jab pehle reasoning model series launch hui — jisme model "respond karne se pehle zyada time sochta" tha. Uske baad open reasoning models ne poori field ko badal diya.

Timeline — do bade milestones

  • September 2024: pehli badi reasoning model series announce hui — aise models jo respond karne se pehle zyada time "sochte" hain.
  • Company ke hisaab se, ye enhanced reasoning capabilities khaas taur par useful hain science, coding aur math jaise complex problems ke liye.
  • January 2025: DeepSeek-R1 release hua — ek open model jisne proprietary reasoning model ke barabar (aur kuch mamlo me behtar) performance di.
  • Iske saath ek technical report bhi aayi jisme training methodology ka blueprint share kiya gaya — isliye isne bahut badi halchal machayi.
  • Is book ka goal hai: in methodologies ko khud implement karke samajhna.

Reasoning improve karne ke 3 tareeke

  • LLM ki reasoning capability improve karne ke approaches ko 3 broad categories me baanta ja sakta hai.
  • Ye teeno aam taur par conventional training stages (pre-training + post-training) ke baad apply hote hain — lekin inhe pre-trained base model par bhi apply kiya ja sakta hai.

1. Inference-time compute scaling

  • Isme model ke weights ko change kiye bina, inference time par (jab user prompt deta hai) zyada compute kharch karke reasoning improve ki jaati hai.
  • Core idea: zyada computational resources ke badle better performance — jaise chain-of-thought reasoning aur alag-alag sampling procedures.
  • Iske aur naam: inference-compute scaling, test-time scaling.
  • Ye chapters 4 aur 5 ka focus hai.

2. Reinforcement learning (RL)

  • RL training methods hain jo model ko un actions ke liye encourage karte hain jinse high reward milta hai.
  • Reward broad ho sakta hai — jaise task success ya heuristic score — ya narrow aur verifiable — jaise math problem ka sahi answer ya coding task ka pass hona.
  • Inference-time scaling se farak: RL model ke weights update karta hai training ke dauraan — model trial-and-error se reasoning strategies seekhta aur refine karta hai.
  • Ye chapters 6 aur 7 me detail me aayega.

3. Distillation

  • Distillation me ek strong, bade model ke complex reasoning patterns ko ek chhote ya zyada efficient model me transfer kiya jaata hai.
  • LLM context me iska matlab aam taur par hai: bade, capable model se generate kiye gaye high-quality labeled instruction datasets par supervised fine-tuning (SFT) karna.
  • Isse knowledge distillation bhi kehte hain — lekin ye traditional deep learning wali distillation se thoda alag hai, jisme chhota ("student") model bade ("teacher") model ke outputs ke saath-saath uske logits se bhi seekhta hai.
  • Ye chapter 8 ka topic hai.

RLHF vs reasoning ke liye RL — confusion mat karo

  • Dono me underlying process RL hi hai, lekin reward ka source alag hai.
  • RLHF (preference tuning): reward human judgments ya rankings se aata hai — model ko human-preferred behaviour ki taraf guide karta hai.
  • Reasoning RL: reward automated verifiers ya environment se aata hai — jaise math proof ki correctness. Ye zyada objective ho sakta hai, lekin human preferences se kam aligned bhi ho sakta hai.
  • Example: reasoning RL ek model ko math proofs me excel karne ke liye train karega — correctness ka explicit reward dekar. RLHF me human evaluators alag-alag responses ko rank karenge.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • 3 approaches: inference-time scaling (no weight change), RL (weights update hote hain), distillation (bade model se chhote model me transfer).
  • Inference-time scaling = zyada compute, same model. RL = training se behtar model.
  • Reasoning RL ka reward verifiable hota hai (math/code) — RLHF ka reward human judgment se aata hai.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 1

01.4Chapter 1 — Understanding reasoning models

Pattern matching versus logical reasoning

LLM fluent text generate karta hai — lekin kya wo sach me logic laga raha hota hai, ya sirf patterns match kar raha hota hai? Ye section isi farak ko ek concrete example se samjhata hai.

Pattern matching kya hai?

  • Pre-training me LLM vast amounts of text dekh kar next token predict karna seekhta hai — statistical associations ko identify aur reproduce karke.
  • Ye fluent aur coherent text generate kar sakta hai, lekin ye process fundamentally learned statistical regularities par based hai — explicit rules ya guaranteed logical inference par nahi.
  • Model prompts ka jawab aise text continuations se deta hai jo training me dekhe gaye patterns ke saath statistically consistent hote hain.
  • Isme kai premise-to-conclusion patterns bhi shamil hote hain jo logical inference jaise lagte hain — lekin model premises ko explicitly represent nahi karta aur formal rules apply nahi karta.

Example — "The capital of Germany is…"

  • Prompt: "The capital of Germany is…"
  • Response: "Berlin."
  • LLM ye answer logically deduce nahi kar raha — wo training data se seekhi gayi ek strong statistical association ko recall kar raha hai.
  • Yahi pattern matching hai: learned correlations ke basis par text complete karna, structured reasoning steps apply kiye bina.

Logical reasoning kya hai?

  • Logical reasoning me rules ka use karke systematically conclusions nikale jaate hain.
  • Ye intermediate reasoning steps par depend karta hai — aur contradictions ko pehchanne ya formal relationships se implications nikalne ki ability par.
  • Pattern matching se iska farak: yahan steps explicit hote hain aur unhe check kiya ja sakta hai.

Penguin wala example — contradiction ko pakdo

  • Prompt: "All birds can fly. A penguin is a bird. Can a penguin fly?"
  • Closed-world setting (sirf prompt ke facts): dono premises se valid answer hai "Yes, a penguin can fly."
  • Open-world setting (background knowledge bhi allowed): hum jaante hain ki penguins cannot fly — ye external fact premises se nikle conclusion se contradict karta hai.
  • Ek reasoning system ko ye inconsistency notice karni chahiye — ya to clarification maangni chahiye, ya pehla statement weaken karna chahiye, jaise "Most birds can fly, with exceptions such as penguins."
  • Ek statistical (pattern-matching) LLM contradictions ko explicitly track nahi karta — wo sirf learned text distributions se predict karta hai.
  • Agar training data me "All birds can fly" strongly reinforce hua ho, to model confidently jawab de sakta hai: "Yes, penguins can fly."

Rule-based systems popular kyun nahi?

  • Rule-based systems '80s aur '90s me widely use hote the — medical diagnosis, legal decisions, engineering me.
  • Aaj bhi critical domains (medicine, law, aerospace) me use hote hain, jahan explicit inference aur transparent decision processes chahiye.
  • Lekin inhe implement karna mushkil hai — ye zyadatar human-crafted heuristics par depend karte hain.
  • Heuristics ka matlab: simple decision rules jo jaldi ek good-enough answer de dein, optimal answer ki guarantee ke bina.
  • Deep neural networks, jinme LLMs bhi aate hain, hand-written rules implement nahi karte — wo data se decision patterns seekhte hain aur scale par train hone par highly flexible hote hain.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Pattern matching = statistical association se text complete karna.
  • Logical reasoning = rules se systematic conclusions, contradictions ko track karke.
  • LLM ka sahi answer aksar pattern matching hota hai — logic ka proof nahi.
  • Closed-world me premises se jo nikle wahi sahi; open-world me background knowledge contradiction create kar sakta hai.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 1

01.5Chapter 1 — Understanding reasoning models

Simulating reasoning without explicit rules

Ek aam LLM bina kisi explicit rule engine ke bhi logical reasoning jaisa jawab de sakta hai. Ye section batata hai ki ye "simulation" kaise kaam karti hai — aur kab ye fail ho jaati hai.

Penguin prompt par ek aam LLM ka jawab

  • Pichle section wala "All birds can fly..." prompt ek non-reasoning LLM (jaise GPT-4o) ko diya jaye to wo aksar sahi jawab deta hua lagta hai — wo contradiction ko point out kar deta hai.
  • Lekin iska matlab ye nahi hai ki model explicitly logically reason kar raha hai.
  • Model ke paas koi explicit contradiction-checking mechanism nahi hota — wo probability-weighted patterns se answer generate karta hai.
  • Ye isliye kaam karta hai kyunki training data me aise contradictions ko correct karne wale bahut saare instances hote hain — jaise text "penguins cannot fly".
  • Model "penguins" aur "not flying" ke beech ek statistical association seekh leta hai — aur is tarah bina rule-based logic ke bhi sahi jawab de deta hai.

Implicit recognition kaise hoti hai?

  • Model contradiction ko implicitly pehchan leta hai kyunki use training me ye exact reasoning scenario bahut baar mila hota hai.
  • Ye effectiveness poori tarah training data me reasoning-like patterns ke massive exposure par depend karti hai.
  • Matlab: model logic execute nahi kar raha — wo familiar pattern ko recognize kar raha hai.

Pattern-based reasoning kab fail hoti hai?

  • Is tarah ki pattern-based reasoning aam taur par do situations me struggle karti hai:
  • Scenario novel ho — jo training data me pehle kabhi encounter nahi hua.
  • Reasoning complexity high ho — jisme intricate, multi-step logical relationships hon.
  • In cases me sirf pattern matching kaafi nahi hota — yahi wahan hai jahan dedicated reasoning methods (inference-time scaling, RL) kaam aate hain.

Reasoning ek spectrum hai

  • Reasoning LLMs me spectrum par exist karta hai — ye on/off switch nahi hai.
  • Dedicated reasoning models (jaise o1, DeepSeek-R1) se pehle bhi LLMs reasoning behaviour simulate kar sakte the — jaise intermediate steps generate karke sahi conclusions par pahunchna.
  • Aaj jinhe hum "reasoning model" kehte hain, wo isi capability ka zyada refined version hai.
  • Ye improvement inference-compute scaling techniques (chapters 4 aur 5) aur targeted post-training methods jaise reinforcement learning (chapters 6 aur 7) se aati hai.
  • Important: ye sab bina kisi rule-based reasoning pipeline implement kiye hota hai — model inference aur training methodology change hone se apni reasoning capability seekhta ya improve karta hai.

Aaj ke popular reasoning models

  • OpenAI ke dedicated reasoning models me o1, o3, o4-mini aur GPT-5 shamil hain — jabki GPT-4o officially reasoning model ke roop me label nahi kiya gaya.
  • Dusri companies bhi explicit reasoning capabilities wale LLMs bana rahi hain — jaise Claude 4, Grok 4, Gemini 2.5, DeepSeek-R1 aur Qwen3.
  • In sab models me use hone wali techniques hi is book ka focus hain.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Ek aam LLM familiar scenarios me logical reasoning ko simulate kar sakta hai — bina explicit rules ke.
  • Ye simulation training data ke massive exposure par based hai, logic engine par nahi.
  • Novel scenarios aur high-complexity multi-step logic me pattern matching fail hone lagta hai.
  • Reasoning ek spectrum hai — dedicated reasoning models iska refined version hain.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 1

01.6Chapter 1 — Understanding reasoning models

Why build reasoning models from scratch?

Reasoning models ab AI ki sabse hot topic hain — lekin unhe khud scratch se banana kyun seekhein? Is section me cost, trade-offs aur poori book ka roadmap hai.

Reasoning models ki taraf bada shift

  • DeepSeek-R1 ke release (January 2025) ke baad se LLM reasoning improve karna AI ki sabse hot topics me se ek ban gaya hai.
  • Stronger reasoning se LLMs zyada complex problems tackle kar sakte hain — aur users ke kaam ke tasks me zyada capable hote hain.
  • Leading providers bhi isi taraf badh rahe hain: non-chain-of-thought models ko reasoning models ke saath unify karna — aise systems jo saare tools use kar sakein aur jaan sakein ki kab lamba sochna hai aur kab nahi.
  • Ye "kab lamba sochna hai" wala point ek important design consideration hai: reasoning hamesha zaroori ya desirable nahi hota.

Reasoning kab use karein, kab nahi?

  • Reasoning models complex tasks ke liye bane hain: puzzles solve karna, advanced math, challenging coding, aur agent systems me task decomposition, planning aur tool choice.
  • Simple tasks ke liye zaroori nahi: summarization, translation, ya knowledge-based question answering.
  • Har cheez ke liye reasoning model use karna inefficient aur expensive ho sakta hai — simple rule: task ke liye sahi tool use karo.
  • Reasoning models aksar zyada expensive, zyada verbose, aur kabhi-kabhi "overthinking" ki wajah se zyada error-prone bhi hote hain.

Reasoning models mehenge kyun hote hain?

  • Pehla reason — lambe outputs: intermediate steps ki wajah se answer lamba hota hai. LLM text ek token at a time generate karta hai aur har token ke liye ek full forward pass chahiye hota hai.
  • Agar reasoning model ka answer doguna lamba hai, to generation me lagbhag dogune forward passes lagenge — compute cost badh jaati hai.
  • Dusra reason — multiple calls: kai reasoning workflows me ek hi task ke liye model ko kai baar run karna padta hai — jaise multiple candidate solutions sample karna, tools call karna, ya verifier run karna.
  • Ye additional calls total tokens ko multiply kar dete hain aur cost ko aur badha dete hain.
  • Isi liye in models ko scratch se implement karna itna useful hai — jab hum samajhte hain ki wo kaise kaam karte hain, to hum in trade-offs ko bhi behtar samajhte hain.

Book ka roadmap — 4 stages

  • Stage 1 — Base model load karna: hum ek conventional LLM se shuru karte hain jo already pre-trained hai. Reasoning methods aam taur par existing base LLM par hi apply hote hain, scratch se train karke nahi.
  • Stage 2 — Evaluation: ye measure karne ke tools banate hain ki koi method asal me help karta hai ya nahi. Stages 3 aur 4 ke baad hum stage 2 par wapas aate hain — improvement ke baad dobara measure karte hain.
  • Stage 3 — Inference techniques: model ke weights change kiye bina, inference time par reasoning improve karna.
  • Stage 4 — Training techniques: additional training se model ko ek dedicated reasoning model me badalna.

Chapter-wise map

  • Chapter 2: base model introduce karta hai (text generation).
  • Chapter 3: evaluation methods establish karta hai.
  • Chapters 4 aur 5: do inference-time techniques.
  • Chapters 6 se 8: do training-time techniques (RL aur distillation).

Chapter 1 ka summary

  • Conventional LLM training: pre-training → instruction fine-tuning → preference tuning.
  • Reasoning = model explicitly intermediate steps (chain-of-thought) generate kare final answer se pehle — isse multi-step tasks par accuracy aksar badhti hai.
  • LLM reasoning rule-based reasoning se alag hai — aur insaani reasoning se bhi alag kaam karta hai; aam consensus hai ki ye statistical pattern matching par rely karta hai.
  • Reasoning improve karne ke 3 tareeke: inference-time compute scaling, reinforcement learning, aur supervised fine-tuning / distillation.
  • Scratch se banana = LLM ki capabilities, limitations aur computational trade-offs ki practical samajh.

02.1Chapter 2 — Generating text with a pre-trained LLM

Introduction to LLMs for text generation

Ye chapter setup chapter hai: hum ek pre-trained base model load karenge, tokenizer use karenge, aur text generate karna seekhenge — yehi foundation aage ke saare chapters me use hoga.

Is chapter me kya banega?

  • Reasoning techniques aam taur par ek conventional (base) LLM ke upar lagaye jaate hain — isliye pehle hum wahi base model load karte hain.
  • Important: ye ek pre-trained base model hai — instruction-tuned ya preference-tuned assistant nahi.
  • Base model se shuru karne ka fayda: ye clearly dikhta hai ki kaunsi capability reasoning methods se aayi hai, aur kaunsi pehle se thi.
  • Is chapter me hum seekhenge: coding environment setup, tokenizer se input prepare karna, pre-trained LLM load karna, aur text generation function implement karna.

Text generation pipeline — overview

  • Pipeline ke main components: input preparation (tokenizer), LLM (model), aur output generation (decode).
  • User query (input text) → tokenizer → token IDs → LLM → output token IDs → decode → response (output text).
  • Neural network diagrams me information ka flow aam taur par neeche se upar padha jaata hai — input neeche, output upar, arrows flow dikhate hain.
  • Ek base model bhi coherent text generate kar sakta hai aur kuch cases me basic instructions bhi follow kar sakta hai.

Internals kitne deep jaayenge?

  • Is chapter me hum LLM ke internals — jaise attention mechanism aur architecture components — me deep nahi jaayenge.
  • Wo topics is book ke scope se bahar hain; unhe samajhna is book ko follow karne ke liye zaroori nahi hai.
  • Is chapter ka focus practical hai: model ko load karo, text generate karo, aur inference ko fast banao.
  • Agar aapne pehle LLM code kar liya hai, tab bhi ye chapter useful hai — isme inference speed aur practical optimizations par naya material hai.

Coding environment setup — pip ya uv

  • Python 3.10 ya newer chahiye. Do tareeke hain environment setup karne ke:
  • pip: sabse straightforward — pip install -r requirements.txt, ya direct install.
  • uv: recommended Python package aur project manager — pip se significantly faster, dependency resolution zyada reliable, aur isolated environments automatically banata hai.
bash — pip setup
pip install torch>=2.10.0 tokenizers>=0.22.2 reasoning-from-scratch
  • torch = PyTorch, deep learning library neural networks banane aur train karne ke liye.
  • tokenizers = efficient tokenization algorithms ki library, LLM ke liye input data prepare karne ke liye.
  • reasoning-from-scratch = is book ke liye banayi gayi custom library — saare chapter code examples aur utility functions isme hain.
  • PyTorch install platform aur hardware ke hisaab se alag ho sakta hai — khaas taur par GPU acceleration ke liye. Sahi build ke liye official PyTorch website ka install selector use karo.

uv workflow — 4 steps

  1. Official website se apne OS ke liye uv install karo.
  2. Code repo clone karo: git clone --depth 1 se sirf latest version download hoti hai — faster aur kam space. (--depth 1 = shallow clone, poori history nahi.)
  3. Terminal me reasoning-from-scratch folder me jao.
  4. uv run jupyter lab chalao — ye JupyterLab launch karega. Virtual environment banane ya activate karne ki zaroorat nahi — uv khud .venv folder bana kar pyproject.toml se saari dependencies install kar deta hai.
  • Tip: Python script files ko uv run script-name.py se execute kar sakte ho. Extra package ke liye uv add packagename.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Ye chapter stage 1 hai: conventional base LLM load karo + text generation implement karo.
  • Base model = sirf pre-trained, instruction-tuned nahi — phir bhi coherent text generate karta hai.
  • Setup: pip (simple) ya uv (fast, recommended). Python 3.10+ chahiye.

02.2Chapter 2 — Generating text with a pre-trained LLM

Understanding hardware needs and recommendations

LLM train karna bahut mehenga hota hai — lekin is book ke liye hume poora model train nahi karna. Hum ek chhota, capable pre-trained model use karenge jo consumer hardware par chal sake.

Training kitni mehengi hoti hai?

  • Leading LLM companies ke liye ek naya base model train karne ka compute cost aam taur par 1–10 million dollars (chhote end par) se 50 million dollars se zyada (bade end par) tak hota hai — reasoning techniques add karne se pehle.
  • Example: DeepSeek V3 model — jo DeepSeek R1 reasoning system ka base checkpoint hai — 2,048 Nvidia H800 GPUs par lagbhag 11 weeks train hua, estimated cost 5.5 million USD.
  • Final training run me 14.8 million GPU-hours compute use hua. Energy usage lagbhag 620 MWh — jo ek average American household lagbhag 55 saal me use karta hai.
  • Ye resource requirement aur price tag ek individual ke liye LLM develop karna unfeasible bana deta hai.

Is book ka solution — chhota lekin capable model

  • Hum ek relatively small (lekin capable) pre-trained LLM use karenge, jiske upar reasoning techniques implement karenge.
  • Ye chhota LLM ek scaled-down version hai jo otherwise contemporary state-of-the-art models wali same architecture follow karta hai.
  • Reasoning methods jo hum apply karenge, wo wahi hain jo bade LLMs par use hote hain — farak sirf itna hai ki chhota model budget-friendly tareeke se explore karne deta hai.
  • Analogy: agar tumhe seekhna hai ki cars kaise kaam karti hain, to tum seedha expensive Ferrari nahi banate — pehle ek chhoti car (jaise Volkswagen Beetle) banate ho. Chhoti car par kaam karne se engine aur transmission behtar samajh aate hain, kyunki complicated refinements beech me nahi aate.

GPU chahiye ya CPU kaafi hai?

  • Chapters 2–5 reasonable time me CPU par bhi execute ho sakte hain.
  • Baad ke chapters (jaise 5–8) me GPU se fayda hoga — wahan compute zyada intensive hai.
  • Apne machine par PyTorch-supported GPU check karne ke liye:
python — GPU check
import torch

print(f"PyTorch version {torch.__version__}")

if torch.cuda.is_available():
    print(f"CUDA/ROCm GPU: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")
elif torch.backends.mps.is_available():
    print("Apple Silicon GPU")
else:
    print("Only CPU")
  • Code automatically NVIDIA GPU use karega agar available ho, warna CPU (ya Apple Silicon GPU) par chalega.
  • Debugging aur compatibility ke liye pehle CPU par run karna helpful hota hai — phir GPU par switch karo.
  • GPU acceleration chahiye to cloud options bhi hain — jaise Lightning AI Studio ya Google Colab.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Base model training = millions of dollars + hazaaron GPUs + mahine.
  • Is book me chhota model use hota hai — same architecture, same reasoning methods, budget-friendly.
  • Chapters 2–5 CPU par chal sakte hain; baad ke chapters me GPU helpful hai.

02.3Chapter 2 — Generating text with a pre-trained LLM

Preparing input texts for LLMs

Model text nahi, numbers samajhta hai. Is section me hum tokenizer ko samjhenge — wo component jo text ko token IDs me badalta hai aur wapas text me decode karta hai.

Tokenization pipeline

  • Har prompt, reasoning trace aur generated answer ko pehle token IDs me represent karna padta hai — tabhi model use process kar sakta hai.
  • Flow: user text → tokenizer encode → token IDs → LLM → output token IDs → tokenizer decode → human-readable text.
  • Tokenizer LLM ka direct hissa nahi hota, lekin input/output processing ka critical component hai.

Round-trip: encode phir decode

  • Pehle tokenizer file download hoti hai — Qwen3 0.6B base LLM ke liye tokenizer-base.json, lagbhag 6 MB.
  • Phir use Qwen3Tokenizer me load kiya jaata hai.
  • Encode karo, phir decode karo — original text wapas milna chahiye. Ise round-trip kehte hain.
python — tokenization round-trip
prompt = "Explain large language models."
input_token_ids_list = tokenizer.encode(prompt)

text = tokenizer.decode(input_token_ids_list)
print(text)
# 'Explain large language models.'

"Explain" do tokens me kyun toota?

  • Har token ID aur uska decoded string print karne par output ye milta hai:
output — token IDs
840   --> Ex
20772 --> plain
3460  --> large
4128  --> language
4119  --> models
13    --> .
  • "Explain" do tokens me toota: "Ex" aur "plain". Ye Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) ki wajah se hai — ek subword-based method.
  • BPE common aur rare dono tarah ke words ko represent kar sakta hai — full words aur subword units ke mix se.
  • Spaces bhi aksar tokens me shamil hote hain — jaise " large" — jo LLM ko word boundaries detect karne me help karta hai.
  • Qwen3Tokenizer ki vocabulary lagbhag 151,000 tokens ki hai — relatively badi. Comparison: GPT-2 ki lagbhag 50,000 aur Llama 3 ki lagbhag 128,000.

Badi vocabulary — trade-off

  • Badi vocabulary se model size badhta hai — embedding aur output layers ko zyada token representations store karne padte hain.
  • Per-token compute cost bhi badh sakti hai — next-token probabilities nikalne me.
  • Lekin fayda: zyada words single token me represent hote hain, sequence chhoti hoti hai.
  • Chhoti vocabulary me words zyada subwords me toot-te hain — sequence lambi hoti hai, processing time aur resource usage badhta hai.
  • Rough rule: sequence me tokens dogune ho jaayein to computational cost bhi lagbhag doguni ho jaati hai.

Exercise — unknown words

  • Tokenizer ke saath experiment karo: aise words banao jo exist hi nahi karte — dekho tokenizer unhe kaise handle karta hai.
  • Agar tum multiple languages bolte ho, to English ke alawa kisi aur language ke words encode karke dekho.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Encode = text → token IDs; decode = token IDs → text.
  • BPE = subword tokenization — "Explain" → "Ex" + "plain".
  • Vocabulary ~151,000 tokens — badi vocab = chhoti sequences, lekin bada model.
  • Har prompt aur har generated answer pehle token IDs se guzarta hai.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 2

02.4Chapter 2 — Generating text with a pre-trained LLM

Loading pre-trained models

Tokenizer ke baad ab hum LLM ko load karte hain — is book ka base model: Qwen3 0.6B. "0.6B" ka matlab hai lagbhag 0.6 billion weight parameters.

Qwen3 0.6B kyun chuna?

  • Ye ek chhota lekin capable open-weight model hai — open-weight ka matlab, trained weights publicly downloadable hain.
  • Consumer hardware par chal sakta hai.
  • Qwen3 ke do variants hain: ek base model (hamara focus — reasoning development yahin se shuru hoti hai) aur ek official reasoning variant jise hum evaluation ke liye reference ke roop me use kar sakte hain.
  • Note: "Qwen3" ki canonical spelling me space nahi hota — jabki "Llama 3" me hota hai.

From-scratch reimplementation

  • Is book me Qwen3 ka ek custom reimplementation use hota hai — pure PyTorch me likha gaya, external LLM libraries se fully independent.
  • Emphasis code readability aur tweakability par hai — taaki tum apne experiments ke liye use modify kar sako.
  • Ye implementation original pre-trained Qwen3 model weights ke saath fully compatible hai.
  • Ye reimplementation poori tarah locally chalta hai — koi server-side component nahi, koi external API call nahi. Tumhara data tumhare device par hi rehta hai.
  • Book me Qwen3 ke code implementation ki depth me coverage nahi hai — wo topic akele ek alag book bhar ka hai.

Device select karna

  • Model load karne se pehle device specify karte hain — CPU ya GPU. get_device() function best-available device automatically select karta hai: CUDA → Apple Silicon (MPS) → Intel (XPU) → CPU.
  • Modern NVIDIA GPU (Ampere ya newer) par Tensor Cores automatically enable ho jaate hain — matrix multiplications fast hote hain, results par noticeable farak nahi padta.
  • Debugging ke liye pehle CPU par run karo — device = torch.device("cpu") se override kar sakte ho — phir GPU par switch karo.

Weights download aur load

  • Weights download karne ke liye wahi function use hota hai jo tokenizer ke liye use hua tha — bas tokenizer_only=False set karo taaki model weights bhi download hon.
  • File: qwen3-0.6B-base.pth — lagbhag 1,433 MB.
  • Phir Qwen3Model banakar load_state_dict se weights load kiye jaate hain aur model ko device par move kiya jaata hai.
python — model load karna
download_qwen3_small(kind="base", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir="qwen3")

model = Qwen3Model(QWEN_CONFIG_06_B)
model.load_state_dict(torch.load("qwen3/qwen3-0.6B-base.pth"))
model.to(device)

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Qwen3 0.6B = ~0.6 billion parameters, open-weight, consumer hardware par chalta hai.
  • Base model = reasoning development ka starting point; official reasoning variant = reference ke liye.
  • Model poori tarah local chalta hai — pure PyTorch reimplementation, no external API.

02.5Chapter 2 — Generating text with a pre-trained LLM

Understanding the sequential LLM text generation process

LLM text kaise generate karta hai? Ek token at a time — har step me poori sequence ko dekh kar agla token predict karna. Ise autoregressive generation kehte hain.

Autoregressive generation — step by step

  • Har iteration me model input prompt + ab tak generate kiye gaye saare tokens ko lekar ek naya token generate karta hai.
  • Naya token sequence me append ho jaata hai aur agle step ka input ban jaata hai.
  • Ye process tab tak chalti hai jab tak stopping condition meet na ho — jaise max tokens ya end-of-text token.
  • Chat interface bhi isi mechanism ko wrap karta hai — sirf poori dialogue history ko wapas feed karta hai taaki har naya reply context-aware lage. Is book me focus single-turn conversations par hai.

Ek forward pass me kya hota hai?

  • Model poori input sequence ko ek forward pass me process karta hai aur har input position ke liye ek prediction deta hai.
  • Example: 6 input tokens ho to output ek 6 × 151,936 matrix hoti hai — 6 = input tokens, 151,936 = vocabulary size.
  • Har row me 151,936 values hoti hain — har possible next token ke liye ek score (logit). Sabse bada score = sabse likely agla token.
  • Text generation ke liye sirf last position ki prediction use hoti hai — wahi batati hai ki kaunsa naya token append karna hai.
  • Output tensor ka shape: torch.Size([6, 151936]) — 6 input tokens ke liye.

Logits se token tak — argmax

  • Last row se token nikalne ke liye torch.argmax use karte hain — jo sabse bade value ka index deta hai.
  • Example: prompt "Explain large language models." par last token ka argmax 20286 aaya — decode karne par ye " Large" banta hai.
  • Scores bfloat16 format me store hote hain — ek reduced-precision format jo memory usage kam karta hai aur inference efficiency badhata hai.
  • torch.max() sabse badi value deta hai; torch.argmax() us value ka index deta hai. Example: tensor [-2, 1, 3, 1] par max = 3, argmax = 2.
  • torch.inference_mode() me model run karte hain — PyTorch ko gradients track karne ki zaroorat nahi hoti, isse memory kam aur speed zyada milti hai.

Tensors ko reshape karna — squeeze aur unsqueeze

  • PyTorch ke kai functions ko specific dimensions chahiye hote hain — isliye dimensions add ya remove karna important hai.
  • .unsqueeze(0) size-1 ki dimension add karta hai: 1D tensor [1, 2, 3] → 2D tensor [[1, 2, 3]].
  • .squeeze(0) size-1 ki dimension remove karta hai: [[1, 2, 3]] → [1, 2, 3].
  • Model ko batch dimension chahiye hoti hai — isliye input token list ko pehle tensor me convert karke unsqueeze(0) karte hain.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Generation = ek token at a time, har step me poori sequence + naya token.
  • Har forward pass har position ke liye logits deta hai; sirf last position use hoti hai.
  • argmax = greedy decoding — hamesha sabse zyada score wala token chunna.
  • inference_mode = no gradients = kam memory + zyada speed.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 2
← Previous02.4 · Loading pre-trained models→ Next02.6 · Coding a minimal text generation function
02.6Chapter 2 — Generating text with a pre-trained LLM

Coding a minimal text generation function

Ab hum ek minimal text generation function code karenge — aur phir use do techniques se fast karenge: KV caching aur model compilation. Speed yahan se 5 tokens/sec se 68 tokens/sec tak jaati hai.

Basic generation function

  • generate_text_basic_stream function ye karti hai: prompt ko token IDs me convert karo → model se next token predict karo (argmax) → sequence me append karo → repeat karo.
  • Ye ek generator hai — har token generate hote hi yield kar deta hai, taaki tokens live stream hote hue dikhein.
  • model.eval() model ko evaluation mode me daalta hai — deterministic behaviour ke liye best practice.
  • @torch.inference_mode() gradient tracking band kar deta hai — speed aur memory efficiency ke liye.
python — basic text generation (simplified)
@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_basic_stream(model, token_ids, max_new_tokens,
                               eos_token_id=None):
    model.eval()
    for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
        out = model(token_ids)[:, -1]              # last position ke logits
        next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        if eos_token_id is not None and torch.all(next_token == eos_token_id):
            break                                  # stop token mil gaya
        yield next_token
        token_ids = torch.cat([token_ids, next_token], dim=1)

EOS token — kab rukna hai?

  • Base model kabhi-kabhi instruction follow karne ke baad bhi off-topic text generate karta rehta hai — special token <|endoftext|> ke baad bhi.
  • Ye token training me document ka end mark karne ke liye use hota hai. Iska token ID hai 151643.
  • Inference me hum chahte hain ki model is token par ruk jaaye — isliye eos_token_id pass karte hain (tokenizer.eos_token_id se milta hai).
  • Example prompt "Explain large language models in a single sentence." par model ek clear sentence deta hai — lekin EOS ke bina uske baad bhi text chalu rehta hai.
  • Tip: pehle token me leading space (" Large") expected hai — kai tokenizers words ko preceding space ke saath encode karte hain.

Speed-up 1 — KV caching

  • Basic function slow thi: Mac Mini M4 CPU par sirf 5 tokens/sec.
  • Problem: har step me poori sequence dobara process hoti thi — jabki purane tokens ke results same hi rehte hain.
  • KV cache attention mechanism ke keys aur values ko store karke reuse karta hai — har step me sirf naya token process hota hai.
  • Rough complexity: bina KV cache ke n naye tokens generate karna lagbhag O(n²) kaam hai; KV cache ke saath lagbhag O(n) — total kaam output length ke proportional.
  • Result: 5 → 29 tokens/sec — aur generated text bilkul same rehta hai (important sanity check).
  • Code me farak chhota hai: pehle round me poori sequence + cache, uske baad sirf model(next_token, cache=cache).

Speed-up 2 — PyTorch model compilation

  • torch.compile(model) model ke computation graph ko analyze karke operations ko zyada optimized kernels me badal deta hai — Python overhead kam hota hai.
  • Ye khaas taur par helpful hota hai jab same model code ko loop me baar-baar call kiya jaata hai — jaise text generation me.
  • Result (M4 CPU): KV cache + compiled = 68 tokens/sec — uncompiled KV cache (29) se 2x se zyada fast.
  • Agar improvement na dikhe to mode="max-autotune" try karo.
  • PyTorch 2.8+ me ek setting chahiye hoti hai taaki model baar-baar recompile na ho: torch._dynamo.config.allow_unspec_int_on_nn_module = True.

Speed table — Mac Mini M4 CPU

  • Regular: 5 tokens/sec
  • Regular + compiled: 6 tokens/sec
  • KV cache: 28–29 tokens/sec
  • KV cache + compiled: 68 tokens/sec
  • NVIDIA H100 GPU par: regular 51 → compiled 164 → KV cache + compiled 141 tokens/sec. GPU gains is setup me utne bade nahi hain kyunki model chhota hai aur implementation memory-friendly (KV cache on-demand grow karta hai, pre-allocate nahi karta).
  • Batched inference (multiple inputs ek saath) evaluation ko aur fast karta hai — appendix me discuss hai.

Chapter 2 ka summary

  • Text generation ke steps: environment setup → pre-trained base LLM (Qwen3 0.6B) load karo → tokenizer se text prepare karo → autoregressive generation.
  • Generation sequential hoti hai — ek token at a time, argmax (greedy) se.
  • Speed: KV caching (intermediate states reuse karo) + torch.compile (graph optimize karo).
  • Ye chapter aage ki reasoning capabilities ki technical foundation hai.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 2

02.7Chapter 2 — Generating text with a pre-trained LLM

Chapter 2 — poora code

Is chapter ka poora code — official GitHub repo se, bilkul waisa ka waisa. Har file ko kholo aur GitHub link se repo me bhi dekh sakte ho. Code hi hai; outputs nahi dikhaye gaye hain.

ch02/03_optimized-LLM/compare_inference.py · 164 lines · GitHub par dekho
ch02/03_optimized-LLM/compare_inference.py164 lines
# Copyright (c) [Name] under Apache License 2.0 (see LICENSE.txt)
# Source for "Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch)": https://mng.bz/lZ5B
# Code repository: https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch


import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import time
import torch

from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import (
    get_device,
    generate_stats
)
from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import (
    download_qwen3_small,
    Qwen3Tokenizer,
    QWEN_CONFIG_06_B
)


############################
# Parse command-line args
############################
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter, description="Run Qwen3 text generation")
parser.add_argument(
    "--device",
    type=str,
    default=None,
    help="Device to run on (e.g. 'cpu', 'cuda', 'mps'). "
         "If not provided, will auto-detect with get_device()."
)
parser.add_argument(
    "--cache",
    action="store_true",
    help="Use KV cache during generation."
)

parser.add_argument(
    "--compile",
    action="store_true",
    help="Compile PyTorch model."
)

parser.add_argument(
    "--reasoning",
    action="store_true",
    help="Use reasoning model variant."
)

parser.add_argument(
    "--optimized",
    action="store_true",
    help="Use reasoning model variant."
)


args = parser.parse_args()

if args.optimized:
    from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3_optimized import Qwen3Model
else:
    from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import Qwen3Model


if args.cache:
    if args.optimized:
        from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3_optimized import generate_text_basic_cache as generate_text
        is_streaming_generate = False
    else:
        from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import generate_text_basic_stream_cache as generate_text
        is_streaming_generate = True

else:
    from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import generate_text_basic_stream as generate_text
    is_streaming_generate = True

device = torch.device(args.device) if args.device else get_device()

#########################
# Model + tokenizer setup
#########################

if args.reasoning:
    download_qwen3_small(kind="reasoning", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir="qwen3")
    tokenizer_path = Path("qwen3") / "tokenizer-reasoning.json"
    model_path = Path("qwen3") / "qwen3-0.6B-reasoning.pth"
    tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(
        tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path,
        apply_chat_template=True,
        add_generation_prompt=True,
        add_thinking=True
    )

else:
    download_qwen3_small(kind="base", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir="qwen3")
    tokenizer_path = Path("qwen3") / "tokenizer-base.json"
    model_path = Path("qwen3") / "qwen3-0.6B-base.pth"
    tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path)

model = Qwen3Model(QWEN_CONFIG_06_B)
model.load_state_dict(torch.load(model_path, map_location=device))

model.to(device)

if args.compile:
    major, minor = map(int, torch.__version__.split(".")[:2])
    if (major, minor) >= (2, 8):
        # This avoids retriggering model recompilations
        # in PyTorch 2.8 and newer
        # if the model contains code like self.pos = self.pos + 1
        torch._dynamo.config.allow_unspec_int_on_nn_module = True
    model = torch.compile(model)

#########################
# Prompt + generation
#########################

if args.reasoning:
    prompt = "Find all c in Z_3 such that Z_3[x]/(x^2 + c) is a field."
else:
    prompt = "Explain large language models in a single sentence."

input_token_ids_tensor = torch.tensor(
    tokenizer.encode(prompt),
    device=device
).unsqueeze(0)

max_new_tokens = 2048


for iteration in range(1, 4):
    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"Iteration : {iteration}")
    print(f"optimized : {args.optimized}")
    print(f"torch     : {torch.__version__}")
    print(f"device    : {device}")
    print(f"cache     : {args.cache}")
    print(f"compile   : {args.compile}")
    print(f"reasoning : {args.reasoning}")
    print("=" * 60)

    start_time = time.time()
    if is_streaming_generate:
        generated_ids = []
        for token in generate_text(
            model=model,
            token_ids=input_token_ids_tensor,
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
            eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id,
        ):
            generated_ids.append(token.squeeze(0).item())
        output_token_ids_tensor = torch.tensor(generated_ids, device=device)
    else:
        output_token_ids_tensor = generate_text(
            model=model,
            token_ids=input_token_ids_tensor,
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
            eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id,
        )
    end_time = time.time()

    print(f"Output length: {output_token_ids_tensor.numel()}")
    generate_stats(output_token_ids_tensor, tokenizer, start_time, end_time)

# Runs the model similar to chapter 2 and 3 in streaming mode with the least
# amount of bells and whistles. Uses KV caching by default.
# Interactive REPL (Read, Evaluate, Print, Loop) with multiturn memory.

import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import time
import torch

from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import (
    get_device,
    generate_stats
)
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import (
    generate_text_basic_stream_cache
)
from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import (
    download_qwen3_small,
    Qwen3Model,
    Qwen3Tokenizer,
    QWEN_CONFIG_06_B
)

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter, description="Run Qwen3 text generation (interactive REPL)")
parser.add_argument(
    "--device",
    type=str,
    default=None,
    help="Device to run on (e.g. 'cpu', 'cuda', 'mps'). "
         "If not provided, will auto-detect with get_device()."
)
parser.add_argument(
    "--max_new_tokens",
    type=int,
    default=2048,
    help="Maximum number of new tokens to generate in each turn."
)
parser.add_argument(
    "--compile",
    action="store_true",
    help="Compile PyTorch model."
)
parser.add_argument(
    "--reasoning",
    action="store_true",
    help="Use reasoning model variant."
)

args = parser.parse_args()
device = torch.device(args.device) if args.device else get_device()

if args.reasoning:
    download_qwen3_small(kind="reasoning", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir="qwen3")
    tokenizer_path = Path("qwen3") / "tokenizer-reasoning.json"
    model_path = Path("qwen3") / "qwen3-0.6B-reasoning.pth"
else:
    download_qwen3_small(kind="base", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir="qwen3")
    tokenizer_path = Path("qwen3") / "tokenizer-base.json"
    model_path = Path("qwen3") / "qwen3-0.6B-base.pth"

# We will apply the chat template manually later
tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(
    tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path,
    apply_chat_template=False
)

model = Qwen3Model(QWEN_CONFIG_06_B)
state = torch.load(model_path, map_location=device)
model.load_state_dict(state)
model.to(device)
model.eval()

if args.compile:
    model = torch.compile(model)

# The reasoning model may emit <|im_end|>; base may emit <|endoftext|>.
EOS_TOKEN_IDS = (
    tokenizer.encode("<|im_end|>")[0],
    tokenizer.encode("<|endoftext|>")[0]
)

print()
print("=" * 60)
print(f"torch     : {torch.__version__}")
print(f"device    : {device}")
print("cache     : True")
print(f"compile   : {args.compile}")
print(f"reasoning : {args.reasoning}")
print("memory    : True")
print(f"max_new_tokens (per turn): {args.max_new_tokens}")
print(f"context_length: {model.cfg['context_length']}")
print("=" * 60)
print()
print("Interactive REPL with memory. Type '\\exit' or '\\quit' to quit.")
print("Commands: \\clear (forget memory), \\history (show turn count)\n")

# Multi-turn memory as a list of role-content dicts
# Example: {"role": "system"|"user"|"assistant", "content": str}
history = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."}
]


def build_prompt_from_history(history, add_assistant_header=True):
    """
    history: [{"role": "system"|"user"|"assistant", "content": str}, ...]
    """
    parts = []
    for m in history:
        role = m["role"]
        content = m["content"]
        parts.append(f"<|im_start|>{role}\n{content}<|im_end|>\n")

    if add_assistant_header:
        parts.append("<|im_start|>assistant\n")
    return "".join(parts)


def trim_input_tensor(input_ids_tensor, context_len, max_new_tokens):
    if max_new_tokens > context_len:
        raise ValueError("max_new_tokens must not exceed context_len.")
    # The last generated token does not need another forward pass.
    keep_len = max(1, context_len - max(0, max_new_tokens - 1))

    # If the prompt is too long, left-truncate to keep_len
    if input_ids_tensor.shape[1] > keep_len:
        input_ids_tensor = input_ids_tensor[:, -keep_len:]

    return input_ids_tensor


def run_generate(user_text):
    # Add user prompt to history
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_text})

    # Encode full history
    prompt = build_prompt_from_history(history, add_assistant_header=True)
    input_ids = tokenizer.encode(prompt)
    input_token_ids_tensor = torch.tensor(input_ids, device=device).unsqueeze(0)

    # Left-tuncate (to make space for generation)
    input_token_ids_tensor = trim_input_tensor(
        input_ids_tensor=input_token_ids_tensor,
        context_len=model.cfg["context_length"],
        max_new_tokens=args.max_new_tokens
    )

    start_time = time.time()
    all_token_ids = []

    print("[Model]\n", end="", flush=True)
    for tok in generate_text_basic_stream_cache(
        model=model,
        token_ids=input_token_ids_tensor,
        max_new_tokens=args.max_new_tokens,
        # eos_token_id=TOKENIZER.eos_token_id
    ):
        token_id = tok.squeeze(0)
        if token_id in EOS_TOKEN_IDS:  # Manually break at stop tokens
            break
        piece = tokenizer.decode(token_id.tolist())
        print(piece, end="", flush=True)
        all_token_ids.append(token_id.item())

    end_time = time.time()
    print("\n")

    print("[Stats]")
    generate_stats(
        torch.tensor(all_token_ids),
        tokenizer,
        start_time,
        end_time
    )
    print("-" * 60)

    # Add model reply to history
    assistant_text = tokenizer.decode(all_token_ids)
    history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": assistant_text})
    return assistant_text


# Interactive REPL (Read, Evaluate, Print, Loop)
try:
    while True:
        try:
            user_in = input(">> ").strip()
        except EOFError:
            print("")
            break

        low = user_in.lower()
        if low in {r"\exit", r"\quit"}:
            break
        if low == r"\clear":
            # Reset history but keep the system prompt
            system_entries = [m for m in history if m["role"] == "system"]
            history.clear()
            if system_entries:
                history.extend(system_entries)
            else:
                history.append({"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."})
            print("(memory cleared)\n")
            continue
        if low == r"\history":
            # Count assistant turns as the number of model replies so far
            assistant_turns = sum(1 for m in history if m["role"] == "assistant")
            print(f"(stored turns: {assistant_turns})\n")
            continue
        if not user_in:
            continue

        print("\n" + "-" * 60)
        print("[User]")
        print(user_in + "\n")
        run_generate(user_in)

except KeyboardInterrupt:
    print("\nInterrupted by user.")

# Copyright (c) [Name] under Apache License 2.0 (see LICENSE.txt)
# Source for "Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch)": https://mng.bz/lZ5B
# Code repository: https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch

from .qwen3 import KVCache
import warnings
import torch


def get_device(enable_tensor_cores=True):
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        device = torch.device("cuda")
        print("Using NVIDIA CUDA GPU")

        if enable_tensor_cores:
            major, minor = map(int, torch.__version__.split(".")[:2])
            # PyTorch 2.9 and 2.10 still read the legacy TF32 setting in torch.compile.
            # See https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/166387
            # and https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/issues/256
            if (major, minor) >= (2, 11):
                torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = "tf32"
                torch.backends.cudnn.conv.fp32_precision = "tf32"
            else:
                torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True
                torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = True

    elif torch.backends.mps.is_available():
        device = torch.device("mps")
        print("Using Apple Silicon GPU (MPS)")

    elif torch.xpu.is_available():
        device = torch.device("xpu")
        print("Using Intel GPU")

    else:
        device = torch.device("cpu")
        print("Using CPU")

    return device


@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_basic(model, token_ids, max_new_tokens, eos_token_id=None):
    input_length = token_ids.shape[1]
    model.eval()

    for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
        out = model(token_ids)[:, -1]
        next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        # Stop if all sequences in the batch have generated EOS
        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and next_token.item() == eos_token_id):
            break

        token_ids = torch.cat([token_ids, next_token], dim=1)
    return token_ids[:, input_length:]


# Previously, chapter 2 used a non-streaming function, and the
# *_stream functions were introduced in the exercises
# While the simpler generate_text_basic_cache is not used anymore
# it is kept here for backwards compatibility reasons
@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_basic_cache(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens,
    eos_token_id=None
):
    input_length = token_ids.shape[1]
    model.eval()
    cache = KVCache(n_layers=model.cfg["n_layers"])
    model.reset_kv_cache()
    out = model(token_ids, cache=cache)[:, -1]
    generated_tokens = []

    for step in range(max_new_tokens):
        next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and next_token.item() == eos_token_id):
            break

        generated_tokens.append(next_token)
        if step + 1 < max_new_tokens:  # Skips the forward pass after the last token is generated
            out = model(next_token, cache=cache)[:, -1]

    if generated_tokens:
        return torch.cat(generated_tokens, dim=1)
    return token_ids[:, input_length:]


@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_basic_stream(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens,
    eos_token_id=None
):
    model.eval()

    for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
        out = model(token_ids)[:, -1]
        next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and torch.all(next_token == eos_token_id)):
            break

        yield next_token

        token_ids = torch.cat([token_ids, next_token], dim=1)


@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_basic_stream_cache(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens,
    eos_token_id=None
):
    # input_length = token_ids.shape[1]
    model.eval()
    cache = KVCache(n_layers=model.cfg["n_layers"])
    model.reset_kv_cache()

    out = model(token_ids, cache=cache)[:, -1]
    for step in range(max_new_tokens):
        next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and torch.all(next_token == eos_token_id)):
            break

        yield next_token  # New: Yield each token as it's generated
        # token_ids = torch.cat([token_ids, next_token], dim=1)
        if step + 1 < max_new_tokens:  # Skips the forward pass after the last token is generated
            out = model(next_token, cache=cache)[:, -1]

    # return token_ids[:, input_length:]


def _print_peak_memory_stats(device):
    device = torch.device(device)
    backend = getattr(torch, device.type, None)
    if backend is None or not hasattr(backend, "is_available"):
        return
    if not backend.is_available():
        return

    sync_fn = getattr(backend, "synchronize", None)
    if callable(sync_fn):
        try:
            sync_fn(device=device)
        except TypeError:
            sync_fn()

    try:
        max_mem_bytes = backend.max_memory_allocated(device=device)
    except TypeError:
        max_mem_bytes = backend.max_memory_allocated()

    max_mem_gb = max_mem_bytes / (1024 ** 3)
    print(f"Max {device.type.upper()} memory allocated: {max_mem_gb:.2f} GB")

    try:
        backend.reset_peak_memory_stats(device=device)
    except TypeError:
        backend.reset_peak_memory_stats()


def generate_stats(output_token_ids, tokenizer, start_time,
                   end_time):
    # tokenizer is currently unused but retained for backward compatibility
    total_time = end_time - start_time
    print(f"\n\nTime: {total_time:.2f} sec")
    print(f"{int(output_token_ids.numel() / total_time)} tokens/sec")

    for name, backend in (("CUDA", getattr(torch, "cuda", None)),
                          ("XPU", getattr(torch, "xpu", None))):
        if backend is not None and backend.is_available():

            # Check whether we are actually using this backend
            device_type = output_token_ids.device.type
            if device_type != name.lower():
                warnings.warn(
                    f"{name} is available but tensors are on "
                    f"{device_type}. Memory stats may be 0."
                )

            # Synchronize if supported (important for async backends)
            if hasattr(backend, "synchronize"):
                backend.synchronize()

            max_mem_bytes = backend.max_memory_allocated()
            max_mem_gb = max_mem_bytes / (1024 ** 3)
            print(f"Max {name} memory allocated: {max_mem_gb:.2f} GB")
            backend.reset_peak_memory_stats()

def get_device(enable_tensor_cores=True):
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        device = torch.device("cuda")
        print("Using NVIDIA CUDA GPU")
        
        if enable_tensor_cores:
            major, minor = map(int, torch.__version__.split(".")[:2])
            # PyTorch 2.9 and 2.10 still read the legacy TF32 setting in torch.compile.
            # See https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/166387
            # and https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/issues/256
            if (major, minor) >= (2, 11):
                torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = "tf32"
                torch.backends.cudnn.conv.fp32_precision = "tf32"
            else:
                torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True
                torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = True

    elif torch.backends.mps.is_available():
        device = torch.device("mps")
        print("Using Apple Silicon GPU (MPS)")

    elif torch.xpu.is_available():
        device = torch.device("xpu")
        print("Using Intel GPU")

    else:
        device = torch.device("cpu")
        print("Using CPU")

    return device

# ---- notebook cell 75 ----
@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_basic_stream(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens, 
    eos_token_id=None
):
    model.eval()

    for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
        out = model(token_ids)[:, -1]
        next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        # Stop if we encounter an end-of-sequence token
        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and torch.all(next_token == eos_token_id)):
            break

        yield next_token  # Yield each token as it's generated
        
        token_ids = torch.cat([token_ids, next_token], dim=1)

# ---- notebook cell 86 ----
import warnings

def generate_stats(output_token_ids, tokenizer, start_time,
                   end_time):
    # tokenizer is currently unused but retained for backward compatibility
    total_time = end_time - start_time
    print(f"\n\nTime: {total_time:.2f} sec")
    print(f"{int(output_token_ids.numel() / total_time)} tokens/sec")

    for name, backend in (("CUDA", getattr(torch, "cuda", None)),
                          ("XPU", getattr(torch, "xpu", None))):
        if backend is not None and backend.is_available():

            # Check whether we are actually using this backend
            device_type = output_token_ids.device.type
            if device_type != name.lower():
                warnings.warn(
                    f"{name} is available but tensors are on "
                    f"{device_type}. Memory stats may be 0."
                )
    
            # Synchronize if supported (important for async backends)
            if hasattr(backend, "synchronize"):
                backend.synchronize()
            
            max_mem_bytes = backend.max_memory_allocated()
            max_mem_gb = max_mem_bytes / (1024 ** 3)
            print(f"Max {name} memory allocated: {max_mem_gb:.2f} GB")
            backend.reset_peak_memory_stats()

# ---- notebook cell 93 ----
from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import KVCache

@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_basic_stream_cache(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens,
    eos_token_id=None
):
    model.eval()
    cache = KVCache(n_layers=model.cfg["n_layers"])  # New
    model.reset_kv_cache()                           # New

    out = model(token_ids, cache=cache)[:, -1]
    for step in range(max_new_tokens):
        next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and torch.all(next_token == eos_token_id)):
            break

        yield next_token
        if step + 1 < max_new_tokens:  # Skips the forward pass after the last token is generated
            out = model(next_token, cache=cache)[:, -1]

from pathlib import Path
import sys
import requests
from urllib.parse import urlparse


def _download_error_message(filename, url, primary_error, backup_url=None, backup_error=None):
    details = [f"Failed to download {filename}."]

    if primary_error is not None:
        details.append(
            f"Primary URL failed ({url}): "
            f"{type(primary_error).__name__}: {primary_error}"
        )

    if backup_url and backup_error is not None:
        details.append(
            f"Backup URL failed ({backup_url}): "
            f"{type(backup_error).__name__}: {backup_error}"
        )

    cert_or_proxy_issue = any(
        isinstance(err, (requests.exceptions.ProxyError, requests.exceptions.SSLError))
        for err in (primary_error, backup_error)
        if err is not None
    )
    if not cert_or_proxy_issue:
        lowered = " ".join(
            str(err).lower() for err in (primary_error, backup_error) if err is not None
        )
        cert_or_proxy_issue = any(
            keyword in lowered for keyword in ("certificate", "ssl", "tls", "proxy")
        )

    if cert_or_proxy_issue:
        details.append(
            "This can happen on work or school machines where a VPN, proxy, or "
            "antivirus tool intercepts HTTPS certificates."
        )

    details.append(
        "See the troubleshooting guide: "
        "https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/main/troubleshooting.md "
        "(especially the 'File Download Issues' section)."
    )
    return "\n".join(details)


def download_file(url, out_dir=".", backup_url=None):
    out_dir = Path(out_dir)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    filename = Path(urlparse(url).path).name
    dest = out_dir / filename

    def try_download(u):
        try:
            with requests.get(u, stream=True, timeout=30) as r:
                r.raise_for_status()
                size_remote = int(r.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))

                # Skip download if already complete
                if dest.exists() and size_remote and dest.stat().st_size == size_remote:
                    print(f"✓ {dest} already up-to-date")
                    return True, None

                # Download in 1 MiB chunks with progress display
                block = 1024 * 1024
                downloaded = 0
                with open(dest, "wb") as f:
                    for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=block):
                        if not chunk:
                            continue
                        f.write(chunk)
                        downloaded += len(chunk)
                        if size_remote:
                            pct = downloaded * 100 // size_remote
                            sys.stdout.write(
                                f"\r{filename}: {pct:3d}% "
                                f"({downloaded // (1024*1024)} MiB / "
                                f"{size_remote // (1024*1024)} MiB)"
                            )
                            sys.stdout.flush()
                if size_remote:
                    sys.stdout.write("\n")
            return True, None
        except requests.RequestException as exc:
            return False, exc

    # Try main URL first
    success, primary_error = try_download(url)
    if success:
        return dest

    # Try backup URL if provided
    backup_error = None
    if backup_url:
        print(f"Primary URL ({url}) failed.\nTrying backup URL ({backup_url})...")
        success, backup_error = try_download(backup_url)
        if success:
            return dest

    message = _download_error_message(
        filename=filename,
        url=url,
        primary_error=primary_error,
        backup_url=backup_url,
        backup_error=backup_error,
    )
    raise RuntimeError(message) from (backup_error or primary_error)

03.1Chapter 3 — Evaluating reasoning models

Building a math verifier

Evaluation se pata chalta hai ki kaunsa LLM sirf convincing lagta hai aur kaunsa asal me problems sahi solve karta hai. Is chapter me hum ek math verifier banayenge — jo answers ko automatically check karega.

Evaluation ke 4 common tareeke

  • Trained LLMs ko evaluate karne ke 4 common tareeke hain: multiple choice, verifiers, leaderboards, aur LLM judges.
  • Inhe do broad types me baanta ja sakta hai: benchmark-based evaluation (zyada quantitative) aur judgment-based evaluation (zyada qualitative judgments par based).
  • Ye saare methods alag contexts me useful hain — lekin reasoning models ke liye verifiers khaas taur par relevant hain.

Math problems verifier ke liye perfect kyun hain?

  • Math problems ko solve karne ke liye step-by-step reasoning chahiye hoti hai — lekin evaluation straightforward hai, kyunki final answer ko correct answer se check kiya ja sakta hai.
  • Verifier approach ek simple aur reliable tareeka deta hai ye measure karne ka ki model ke reasoning steps sahi outcome tak le jaate hain ya nahi.
  • Math problems programmatically unlimited variations me generate bhi kiye ja sakte hain — isliye ye reasoning model evaluation aur development ka cornerstone ban gaya hai.

Verifier kaise kaam karta hai?

  • Model ek free-form answer generate karta hai (kai steps ke saath) aur final answer ek boxed form me likhta hai — jaise \boxed{14/3}.
  • Verifier boxed answer ko extract karta hai aur use dataset ke reference solution (ground truth) se compare karta hai — aksar external tools jaise code interpreters ya calculator programs ki help se.
  • Is chapter me "evaluate" ka matlab hai: model ko kai examples par quantitatively test karna aur uske outputs ko reference answers ke against score karna.

Verifier ke fayde aur limits

  • Fayda: verifier sirf evaluation ke liye nahi hai — ye chapter 6 me reinforcement learning ke liye verifiable reward signal ki foundation bhi hai.
  • Limit: verifier methods sirf un domains par apply ho sakte hain jinhe aasani se (aur ideally deterministically) verify kiya ja sake — jaise math aur code.
  • Ye approach extra complexity aur dependencies bhi add kar sakta hai — evaluation ka kuch burden model se hat kar external tool par shift ho jaata hai.

Math verifier banane ke 8 steps

  1. Pre-trained LLM load karo.
  2. Text generate karo (answers).
  3. Final answer box extract karo.
  4. Extracted answer ko normalize karo.
  5. Mathematical equivalence verify karo.
  6. Answers grade karo.
  7. Evaluation dataset (MATH-500) load karo.
  8. Poori dataset par evaluation run karo.
  • Is chapter me hum in 8 steps ko ek-ek karke implement karenge — har step ek function banega, aur aakhir me saare pieces ek full pipeline me jud jaayenge.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • 4 eval methods: multiple choice, verifiers, leaderboards, LLM judges.
  • Verifier = free-form answer → boxed answer extract karo → ground truth se compare karo.
  • Math is liye chuna gaya: reasoning chahiye, lekin checking easy hai — aur yehi verifier baad me RL reward banega.

03.2Chapter 3 — Evaluating reasoning models

Loading a pre-trained model to generate text

Verifier ke steps 1 aur 2: pehle wahi pre-trained LLM load karo jo chapter 2 me use hua tha — aur use aise wrap karo ki aage ke chapters me bhi reuse ho sake.

Reusable loader — load_model_and_tokenizer

  • Model loading logic ko ek function me wrap kiya gaya hai — load_model_and_tokenizer — taaki baad ke chapters me reuse ho sake.
  • Ye function do models load kar sakta hai: "base" (default — wahi Qwen3 0.6B base model) aur "reasoning" (official Qwen3 reasoning variant).
  • Reasoning variant wo custom reasoning model nahi hai jo hum baad me khud banayenge — ye sirf ek reference point hai, jisse hum apne results compare kar sakein.
  • Reasoning variant ke liye tokenizer alag settings ke saath load hota hai: chat template apply hota hai, generation prompt add hota hai, aur thinking add hoti hai.
  • Optional: use_compile=True se model compilation enable ho jaati hai (chapter 2 wali speed-up).

Text generation wrapper

  • Model load karne ke baad, chapter 2 ka text generation function use karke answers generate karte hain.
  • Iske liye ek wrapper function hai — generate_text_stream_concat — jo streaming generation ko wrap karke poora decoded text ek string me return karta hai.
  • Wrapper ka fayda: har jagah same prompt-handling, streaming aur decoding code repeat nahi karna padta — aur aage ke chapters me generation function ko swap karna easy ho jaata hai.

Example — algebra problem

  • Prompt: "If a+b=3 and ab=13/6, what is the value of a²+b²?"
  • Base model ne step-by-step solution diya — identity use ki: a²+b² = (a+b)² − 2ab — aur final answer diya: \boxed{14/3}.
  • Ye dikhata hai ki ek base model bhi kabhi-kabhi achha step-by-step answer de sakta hai — lekin ye consistent nahi hota.
  • Model ne boxed format khud use kiya — humne enforce nahi kiya tha. Ye isliye hota hai kyunki boxed answers math benchmarks aur training data me common convention hain.
  • Fair assumption: training ke time internet par available koi bhi information training data ka hissa ho sakti hai.
  • MATH-500 evaluation me hum ek specific prompt add karenge jo model ko boxed form me answer dene ko kehta hai — taaki extraction consistent rahe.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Ek hi loader dono models ke liye — base (default) aur official reasoning variant (reference).
  • Wrapper function generation ko simple banata hai: prompt do, poora text lo.
  • Boxed answers training data ki common convention hain — isliye model khud bhi use karta hai.
