03.3Chapter 3 — Evaluating reasoning models

Extracting the final answer box

Model ka answer lamba text hota hai — usme se final answer nikalna ek mechanical lekin zaroori step hai. Yahan hum \boxed{...} se answer extract karna seekhenge.

Problem — answer text ke andar chhupa hai

  • Model ka response explanation + final answer ka mix hota hai. Automatic checking ke liye hume sirf final answer chahiye.
  • Convention: final answer \boxed{...} me likha jaata hai — jaise \boxed{\dfrac{14}{3}}.
  • Ye step mechanical hai, lekin baar-baar kaam aayega — jab bhi model response ko automatically score karna hoga.
  • Note: hum code me raw strings (r"...") use karte hain — taaki backslash (\) characters ko escape sequence na samjha jaaye.

get_last_boxed — aakhri box nikalo

  • get_last_boxed(text) function text me aakhri \boxed dhoondti hai.
  • Phir whitespace skip karti hai, opening brace { check karti hai, aur brace nesting ko handle karte hue content extract karti hai.
  • Agar braces unbalanced hon ya box na mile to None return karti hai.
  • Example: model answer se ye \dfrac{14}{3} extract karti hai — wahi boxed answer jo hum chahte the.
  • Aakhri box kyun? Kyunki model beech me bhi boxes likh sakta hai — final answer aam taur par aakhri box hota hai.

extract_final_candidate — fallback ke saath

  • Asli duniya me model hamesha boxed answer nahi deta — box missing ya incomplete bhi ho sakta hai. Isliye ek robust function chahiye.
  • extract_final_candidate(text, fallback="number_then_full") pehle boxed expression try karta hai.
  • Agar box na mile to fallback settings kaam aati hain:
  • "number_then_full" (default): text ka aakhri number lo, warna poora text return karo.
  • "number_only": aakhri number lo, warna empty string.
  • "none": sirf boxed content lo, warna empty string.

Regex — numbers dhoondna

  • Fallback ke liye Python ki re library se regular expressions (regex) use hote hain — text me patterns search karne ka tareeka.
  • Regex pattern numbers ko pehchanta hai — fractions, decimals aur scientific notation bhi.
  • Examples: extract_final_candidate(r"\boxed{ 14/3. }") → "14/3." (extra whitespace strip ho jaati hai, punctuation rehta hai — use equality check handle karega).
  • extract_final_candidate("abc < > 14/3 abc") → "14/3" (fallback se aakhri number mila).
  • Regex syntax intimidating lag sakta hai — exact syntax yaad rakhna zaroori nahi; important ye hai ki ye ek reliable tool hai aakhri numeric candidate nikalne ke liye.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • get_last_boxed = aakhri \boxed{...} ka content nikalo, nesting handle karke.
  • extract_final_candidate = box pehle, warna fallback (aakhri number ya poora text).
  • Extraction deterministic code se hoti hai — iske liye dusra LLM use karne ki zaroorat nahi.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 3
← Previous03.2 · Loading a pre-trained model to generate text→ Next03.4 · Normalizing the extracted answer
03.4Chapter 3 — Evaluating reasoning models

Normalizing the extracted answer

Ek hi value kai tareekon se likhi ja sakti hai — \frac{14}{3}, 14/3, $14/3$, (14)/(3). Compare karne se pehle in sab ko ek canonical form me laana padta hai. Ise normalization kehte hain.

Normalize kyun zaroori hai?

  • Extract kiya hua answer \dfrac{14}{3} ho sakta hai — lekin model use \frac{14}{3}, 14/3, $14/3$ ya (14)/(3) bhi likh sakta hai.
  • Robust checking ke liye pehle ek consistent comparison method chahiye — isliye normalization (canonicalization) pass lagate hain.
  • Ye verifier pipeline ka step 4 hai: extract karo → normalize karo → phir verify karo.

normalize_text kya-kya karta hai?

  • Special tokens hatata hai — jaise <|endoftext|>.
  • LaTeX formatting saaf karta hai: \left, \right, \,, \; jaise commands remove karta hai.
  • \dfrac aur \tfrac ko \frac me badalta hai; \cdot ko * me.
  • \frac{a}{b} ko (a)/(b) me convert karta hai — taaki symbolic parser use samajh sake.
  • \sqrt{...} ko sqrt(...) me badalta hai.
  • Dollar signs ($) aur percent signs hatata hai; \text{...} se andar ka text nikalta hai.
  • Superscripts convert karta hai — jaise ² → **2 — taaki "x²" aur "x**2" same samjhe jaayein.
  • Degree symbols aur ^\circ hatata hai.

Example

  • Input: \dfrac{14}{3} → normalized: (14)/(3)
  • Input: 14/3 → normalized: 14/3 — ab dono ko compare kiya ja sakta hai.
  • Normalization ke baad bhi "14/3" aur "(14)/(3)" strings ke roop me alag dikhte hain — isliye agle step me symbolic comparison chahiye hoti hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Same value, kai formats — normalization sab ko ek canonical form me laata hai.
  • LaTeX commands, dollar signs, special tokens — sab strip hote hain.
  • Normalization ke baad bhi exact string match kaafi nahi — symbolic check chahiye (agla section).
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 3
← Previous03.3 · Extracting the final answer box→ Next03.5 · Verifying mathematical equivalence
03.5Chapter 3 — Evaluating reasoning models

Verifying mathematical equivalence

Normalize karne ke baad bhi "14/3" aur "28/6" strings ke roop me alag hain — lekin mathematically same hain. Is section me hum SymPy se symbolic equivalence check karenge, aur phir answers grade karenge.

Direct == comparison kyun kaafi nahi?

  • Python ka == operator sirf exact string match karta hai.
  • "14/3" aur "(14)/(3)" match nahi karenge — aur equivalent lekin unnormalized fractions jaise "(28)/(6)" aur "(14)/(3)" bhi unequal treat honge.
  • Isliye equality check se pehle ek intermediate step chahiye: extracted aur normalized answer ko ek symbolic math engine se parse karna.

SymPy parser

  • Hum SymPy open-source math library use karte hain — jo do decades se develop ho rahi hai aur scientific computing me staple hai.
  • sympy_parser(expr) expression ko SymPy object me convert karta hai — taaki use reliably compare kiya ja sake.
  • Ye SymPy ke standard parsing rules apply karta hai, implicit multiplication support karta hai (jaise 2y → 2*y), aur basic arithmetic simplify karta hai (jaise 2+3 → 5).
  • Safety: agar expression 2000 characters se lamba ho ya parse na ho, to None return karta hai — taaki lamba garbage response code ko crash na kare.
  • Examples: sympy_parser("28/6") → 14/3. sympy_parser("(14)/(3)") → 14/3.

equality_check — difference zero hai?

  • equality_check(expr_gtruth, expr_pred) pehle exact string match check karta hai — sabse simple case.
  • Agar strings alag hon to dono expressions ko SymPy objects me parse karta hai.
  • Phir check karta hai: simplify(gtruth - pred) == 0? Agar difference zero simplify hota hai, to dono mathematically equivalent hain.
  • Examples: "13/4." vs "(13)/(4)" → True. "0.5" vs "(1)/(2)" → True. "14/3" vs "15/3" → False.

Tuple wale answers — ek limitation

  • Ek tricky case: (14/3, 2/3) vs (14/3, 4/6). 2/3 aur 4/6 mathematically equivalent hain, to result True hona chahiye — lekin equality_check False deta hai.
  • Reason: ye function sirf simple expressions handle karta hai, tuples nahi.
  • Is limitation ko agle step me fix karte hain.

Grading answers — grade_answer

  • split_into_parts(text) tuple-like expressions ko parts me todta hai: (14/3, 2/3) → ['14/3', '2/3'].
  • Agar input (a, b) ya [a, b] jaisa dikhe to commas par split karta hai; empty string ho to empty list return karta hai.
  • grade_answer(pred_text, gt_text) dono sides ko normalize karta hai, parts me split karta hai, aur phir har part ko equality_check se compare karta hai.
  • Result True tabhi milta hai jab saare parts match karein aur dono sides me parts ki count same ho.
  • Default outcome False hota hai — sirf tab True milta hai jab saare checks pass hon.
  • Ab tuple example sahi grade hota hai: (14/3, 2/3) vs (14/3, 4/6) → True.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • == sirf strings compare karta hai — math equivalence ke liye SymPy chahiye.
  • SymPy parse karta hai, simplify karta hai, difference zero ho to equivalent.
  • grade_answer = normalize + split (tuples) + har part equality_check → sab pass to True.
  • Yehi verifier chapter 6 me verifiable reward signal banega.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 3
← Previous03.4 · Normalizing the extracted answer→ Next03.6 · Loading the evaluation dataset
03.6Chapter 3 — Evaluating reasoning models

Loading the evaluation dataset

Verifier ke pieces ready hain — ab hume ek benchmark dataset chahiye jiss par poori pipeline run karein. Iske liye hum MATH-500 use karenge: 500 curated math problems.

MATH-500 kyun?

  • MATH-500 ek widely used benchmark hai reasoning models ke liye — original MATH dataset se sample kiye gaye 500 problems ka curated collection.
  • Is choice ke 3 practical reasons hain:
  • Size sahi hai: 500 problems meaningful hone ke liye kaafi bade hain, lekin repeated evaluations ke liye manage bhi kiye ja sakte hain — poora MATH dataset har baar run karna bahut slow hota.
  • Clean reference: baad ke chapters me hum original MATH dataset se ek non-overlapping training subset use karenge — MATH-500 ko held-out evaluation set rakhne se clean reference point milta hai.
  • Standard benchmark: reasoning-model literature me common hai — isse is book ke results ko prior work se compare karna easy ho jaata hai.
  • GSM8K jaise simpler datasets ke bajay MATH-500 is liye prefer kiya gaya — ye modern reasoning models ke liye zyada challenging hai aur hamare multi-step symbolic verification pipeline se behtar match karta hai.

Dataset load karna

  • Dataset ko code repository se ek JSON file ke roop me load kiya jaata hai — taaki reproducibility bani rahe, agar external sources change bhi ho jaayein to.
  • load_math500_test() pehle local copy check karta hai, warna URL se download karke local save kar leta hai.
  • Result: Number of entries: 500
  • Optional: Hugging Face Hub se bhi load kar sakte hain — dataset HuggingFaceH4/MATH-500, split "test".

Ek entry kaisi dikhti hai?

  • Har entry me hota hai: problem (question text), answer (reference answer), level (difficulty), type (jaise Algebra, Geometry) aur solution.
  • Example pehli entry ka answer: \left( 3, \frac{\pi}{2} \right) — ek tuple jaisa answer, isiliye grade_answer me tuple handling zaroori thi.

Full evaluation pipeline — evaluate_math500_stream

  • Har problem ke liye ye 4 steps repeat hote hain: prompt template apply karo → model se response generate karo → answer extract karo → grade karo.
  • Results ek .jsonl file me save hote hain — har row ek JSON entry: index, problem, ground-truth answer, generated text, extracted answer, correct (True/False).
  • Progress ke saath ETA bhi print hoti hai — kitne problems ho gaye, kitna time bacha hai.
  • Pehle ek mini demo se test karte hain: "Compute 1/2 + 1/6." — ground truth 2/3, model ne 1/3 predict kiya → Correct: False. Extraction sahi thi, answer galat tha.

Prompt template ka asar

  • Evaluation prompt template: "You are a helpful math assistant. Answer the question and write the final result on a new line as: \boxed{ANSWER}" — phir "Question:" aur "Answer:".
  • Template se model ko boxed format follow karne ki zyada likelihood hoti hai — extraction consistent rehta hai.
  • Lekin prompt template se accuracy par bada asar padta hai: koi template na use karne se base model ki performance 50% boost hoti hai, lekin reasoning model ki accuracy 40% drop hoti hai.
  • Standard MATH-500 prompt ("Question:" ki jagah "Problem:") se base model ki accuracy lagbhag 20% badhti hai — shayad kyunki ye memorized training data se behtar match karta hai — lekin reasoning model ki accuracy 30% drop hoti hai.
  • Lesson: chhote base models prompt phrasing ke prati bahut sensitive hote hain.

Results — MATH-500 accuracy

  • 10-sample subset par: base model 30.0% (3/10), reasoning model 90%.
  • Poore 500-sample dataset par (CUDA): base model 15.3%, reasoning model 50.8%.
  • Reasoning model ki accuracy drastically behtar hai — lekin runtime bhi bahut zyada: 10 samples par 0.4 min (base) vs 7 min (reasoning); 500 samples par H100 par 13.3 min vs 185.4 min.
  • Yehi reasoning models ka core trade-off hai: zyada accuracy ke badle zyada compute aur zyada time.
  • Batched evaluation se speed badhti hai: batch size 128 par base model 13.3 min → 3.3 min, reasoning model 185.4 min → 14.6 min (H100).

Chapter 3 ka summary

  • 4 eval methods: multiple choice, verifiers, leaderboards, LLM judges.
  • Math verifier pipeline: load → generate → extract (boxed) → normalize → SymPy se verify → grade → MATH-500 par evaluate.
  • Prompt templates performance par bahut asar daalte hain.
  • Reasoning model base se zyada accurate hai — lekin bahut zyada runtime ke saath.
  • Yehi verifier chapter 6 me RL ke liye verifiable reward banega.

# Copyright (c) [Name] under Apache License 2.0 (see LICENSE.txt)
# Source for "Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch)": https://mng.bz/lZ5B
# Code repository: https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import (
    extract_final_candidate,
    grade_answer,
)


def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--json_path",
        type=str,
        required=True,
        help="Path to the records file (.json or .jsonl).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--gtruth_answer",
        type=str,
        default="gtruth_answer",
        help="Key name for the ground-truth answer",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--generated_text",
        type=str,
        default="generated_text",
        help="Key name for generated model output",
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


def load_records(json_path):
    path = Path(json_path)
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Input file not found: {path}")

    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        try:
            parsed = json.load(f)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            f.seek(0)
            records = []
            for line_num, line in enumerate(f, start=1):
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                try:
                    records.append(json.loads(line))
                except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Invalid JSON on line {line_num} in {path}: {exc}"
                    ) from exc
            return records

    if isinstance(parsed, list):
        return parsed
    if isinstance(parsed, dict):
        if "records" in parsed and isinstance(parsed["records"], list):
            return parsed["records"]
        return [parsed]

    raise ValueError(
        f"Unsupported JSON root type in {path}: {type(parsed).__name__}"
    )


def evaluate_records(records, gtruth_key, generated_text_key):
    num_examples = len(records)
    num_correct = 0

    for idx, record in enumerate(records, start=1):
        if not isinstance(record, dict):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Record {idx} is not a JSON object: {type(record).__name__}"
            )

        if gtruth_key not in record:
            raise KeyError(f"Record {idx} is missing key: {gtruth_key}")
        if generated_text_key not in record:
            raise KeyError(f"Record {idx} is missing key: {generated_text_key}")

        extracted = extract_final_candidate(record[generated_text_key])
        is_correct = grade_answer(extracted, record[gtruth_key])
        num_correct += int(is_correct)

    acc = num_correct / num_examples if num_examples else 0.0
    return num_correct, num_examples, acc


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = parse_args()
    records = load_records(args.json_path)
    num_correct, num_examples, acc = evaluate_records(
        records=records,
        gtruth_key=args.gtruth_answer,
        generated_text_key=args.generated_text,
    )
    print(f"Accuracy: {acc*100:.1f}% ({num_correct}/{num_examples})")

# Copyright (c) [Name] under Apache License 2.0 (see LICENSE.txt)
# Source for "Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch)": https://mng.bz/lZ5B
# Code repository: https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch

import argparse
import torch

from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import (
    Qwen3Model,
    QWEN_CONFIG_06_B
)
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import get_device
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import (
    load_math500_test,
    evaluate_math500_stream,
    load_model_and_tokenizer,
    load_tokenizer_only
)


def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--device",
        type=str,
        default="auto",
        help="Device to use: 'auto', or any torch device string like 'cpu', 'cuda', 'cuda:0', 'mps'.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--which_model",
        type=str,
        default="base",
        choices=["base", "reasoning", "instruct"],
        help="Model variant to load",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dataset_size",
        type=int,
        default=10,
        help="Number of MATH-500 examples to evaluate",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max_new_tokens",
        type=int,
        default=2048,
        help="Max new tokens for generation",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--compile",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable torch.compile for the model.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--checkpoint_path",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Optional path to a .pth checkpoint to load model weights from.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        help="Print per-sample correctness while evaluating.",
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = parse_args()

    if args.device == "auto":
        device = get_device()
    else:
        device = torch.device(args.device)

    which_model = args.which_model
    dataset_size = args.dataset_size
    max_new_tokens = args.max_new_tokens
    use_compile = args.compile

    print("Model:", which_model)
    print("Device:", device)
    dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")

    math_data = load_math500_test()

    if args.which_model == "instruct":
        which_model = "reasoning"
    else:
        which_model = args.which_model

    if args.checkpoint_path:
        # To load the saved RL checkpoint files from chapter 6
        tokenizer = load_tokenizer_only(which_model=which_model)
        model = Qwen3Model(QWEN_CONFIG_06_B)
        state_dict = torch.load(args.checkpoint_path, map_location="cpu")
        model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
        model.to(device)
        if args.compile:
            torch._dynamo.config.allow_unspec_int_on_nn_module = True
            model = torch.compile(model)
    else:
        model, tokenizer = load_model_and_tokenizer(
            which_model=which_model,
            device=device,
            use_compile=args.compile
        )

    if args.which_model == "instruct":
        tokenizer.add_thinking = False

    model.eval()
    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("high")

    num_correct, num_examples, acc = evaluate_math500_stream(
        model=model,
        out_path=f"math500_{which_model}-{dev_name}-evaluate-script.jsonl",
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        device=device,
        math_data=math_data[:dataset_size],
        max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
        verbose=args.verbose,
    )

# Batched MATH-500 evaluator

import argparse
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3_batched import (
    Qwen3Model,
    QWEN_CONFIG_06_B
)
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import get_device
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import (
    load_math500_test,
    render_prompt,
    extract_final_candidate,
    grade_answer,
    eta_progress_message,
    load_tokenizer_only
)
from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3_batched import (
    load_model_and_tokenizer,
)


def evaluate_math500_batched(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    device,
    math_data,
    out_path=None,
    max_new_tokens=512,
    verbose=False,
    batch_size=4,
    show_eta=False,
):
    model.eval()

    # Default output path like the streaming variant
    if out_path is None:
        dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")  # Make filename compatible with Windows
        out_path = Path(f"math500-{dev_name}.jsonl")

    num_examples = len(math_data)
    num_correct = 0

    start_time = time.time()

    eos_id = getattr(tokenizer, "eos_token_id", None)
    pad_id = getattr(tokenizer, "pad_token_id", None)

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        # Batched loop
        for start in range(0, num_examples, batch_size):
            batch = math_data[start:start + batch_size]

            prompts = [render_prompt(row["problem"]) for row in batch]

            # Encode and left-pad
            tokenized = [tokenizer.encode(p) for p in prompts]
            max_len = max(len(t) for t in tokenized)
            left_padded = [
                ([pad_id] * (max_len - len(t)) + t) if pad_id is not None else t
                for t in tokenized
            ]
            input_ids = torch.tensor(left_padded, device=device, dtype=torch.long)

            # Generate (batched)
            gen = generate_text_basic_batched_cache(
                model,
                token_ids=input_ids,
                max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
                eos_token_id=eos_id,
                pad_id=pad_id,
            )  # shape: (B, T_new)

            # Process each row
            B = gen.size(0)
            for b_idx in range(B):
                # Match the variable names used by evaluate_math500_stream
                i = start + b_idx + 1
                row = batch[b_idx]

                row_tokens = gen[b_idx]
                # Cut at first EOS if present
                if eos_id is not None:
                    eos_pos = (row_tokens == eos_id).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                    if len(eos_pos) > 0:
                        row_tokens = row_tokens[: eos_pos[0]]

                gen_text = tokenizer.decode(row_tokens.tolist())
                extracted = extract_final_candidate(gen_text)
                is_correct = grade_answer(extracted, row["answer"])
                num_correct += int(is_correct)

                record = {  # Record to be saved for inspection
                    "index": i,
                    "problem": row["problem"],
                    "gtruth_answer": row["answer"],
                    "generated_text": gen_text,
                    "extracted": extracted,
                    "correct": bool(is_correct),
                }
                f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

                progress_msg = eta_progress_message(
                    processed=i,
                    total=num_examples,
                    start_time=start_time,
                    show_eta=show_eta,
                    label="MATH-500",
                )
                print(progress_msg, end="\r", flush=True)
                if verbose:  # Print responses during the generation process
                    print(
                        f"\n\n{'='*50}\n{progress_msg}\n"
                        f"{'='*50}\nExtracted: {extracted}\n"
                        f"Expected:  {row['answer']}\n"
                        f"Correct so far: {num_correct}\n{'-'*50}"
                    )

    # Print summary information
    seconds_elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    acc = num_correct / num_examples if num_examples else 0.0
    print(f"\nAccuracy: {acc*100:.1f}% ({num_correct}/{num_examples})")
    print(f"Total time: {seconds_elapsed/60:.1f} min")
    print(f"Logs written to: {out_path}")
    return num_correct, num_examples, acc


def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--device",
        type=str,
        default="auto",
        help="Device to use: 'auto', or any torch device string like 'cpu', 'cuda', 'cuda:0', 'mps'.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--which_model",
        type=str,
        default="base",
        choices=["base", "reasoning", "instruct"],
        help="Model variant to load",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dataset_size",
        type=int,
        default=10,
        help="Number of MATH-500 examples to evaluate",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max_new_tokens",
        type=int,
        default=2048,
        help="Max new tokens for generation",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--compile",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable torch.compile for the model.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--checkpoint_path",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Optional path to a .pth checkpoint to load model weights from.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--batch_size",
        type=int,
        default=4,
        help="Batch size for batched generation",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        help="Print per-sample correctness while evaluating.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--disable_efficient_mode",
        action="store_true",
        help="Uses an alternative implementation of batched inference that is simpler but more memory and compute intense.",
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = parse_args()

    if args.disable_efficient_mode:
        from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3_batched import (
            generate_text_basic_batched_cache,
        )
    else:
        from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3_batched import (
            generate_text_basic_batched_cache_stop as generate_text_basic_batched_cache,
        )
    if args.device == "auto":
        device = get_device()
    else:
        device = torch.device(args.device)

    which_model = args.which_model
    dataset_size = args.dataset_size
    max_new_tokens = args.max_new_tokens
    batch_size = args.batch_size

    print("Model:", which_model)
    print("Device:", device)
    dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")
    print("Batch size:", batch_size)

    math_data = load_math500_test()[:dataset_size]
    if args.which_model == "instruct":
        which_model = "reasoning"
    else:
        which_model = args.which_model

    if args.checkpoint_path:
        # To load the saved RL checkpoint files from chapter 6
        tokenizer = load_tokenizer_only(which_model=which_model)
        model = Qwen3Model(QWEN_CONFIG_06_B)
        model.to(device)
        state_dict = torch.load(args.checkpoint_path, map_location=device)
        model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
        if args.compile:
            torch._dynamo.config.allow_unspec_int_on_nn_module = True
            model = torch.compile(model)
    else:
        model, tokenizer = load_model_and_tokenizer(
            which_model=which_model,
            device=device,
            use_compile=args.compile
        )
    if args.which_model == "instruct":
        tokenizer.add_thinking = False

    out_path = f"math500_{which_model}-{dev_name}-batched-bs{batch_size}.jsonl"
    num_correct, num_examples, acc = evaluate_math500_batched(
        model=model,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        device=device,
        math_data=math_data,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
        out_path=out_path,
        verbose=args.verbose,
        show_eta=True,
    )

def evaluate_math500_stream_hybrid(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    device,
    math_data,
    out_path=None,
    max_new_tokens=512,
    verbose=False,
):
    if out_path is None:
        dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")
        out_path = Path(f"math500-{dev_name}.jsonl")

    num_examples = len(math_data)
    num_correct = 0
    total_len = 0
    start_time = time.time()

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for i, row in enumerate(math_data, start=1):
            prompt = render_prompt(row["problem"])
            gen_text = generate_text_stream_concat(
                model,
                tokenizer,
                prompt,
                device,
                max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
                verbose=verbose,
            )
            total_len += len(tokenizer.encode(gen_text))

            extracted = extract_final_candidate(gen_text)
            pred = bonus.normalize_text_hybrid(extracted)
            gold = bonus.normalize_text_hybrid(row["answer"])
            is_correct = pred == gold
            num_correct += int(is_correct)

            record = {
                "index": i,
                "problem": row["problem"],
                "gtruth_answer": row["answer"],
                "generated_text": gen_text,
                "extracted": extracted,
                "pred_normalized_hybrid": pred,
                "gold_normalized_hybrid": gold,
                "correct": bool(is_correct),
            }
            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

            progress_msg = eta_progress_message(
                processed=i,
                total=num_examples,
                start_time=start_time,
                show_eta=True,
                label="MATH-500",
            )
            print(progress_msg, end="\r", flush=True)
            if verbose:
                print(
                    f"\n\n{'='*50}\n{progress_msg}\n"
                    f"{'='*50}\nExtracted: {extracted}\n"
                    f"Expected:  {row['answer']}\n"
                    f"Correct so far: {num_correct}\n{'-'*50}"
                )

    seconds_elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    acc = num_correct / num_examples if num_examples else 0.0
    print(f"\nAccuracy: {acc*100:.1f}% ({num_correct}/{num_examples})")
    print(f"Total time: {seconds_elapsed/60:.1f} min")
    avg_len = total_len / num_examples
    print(f"Average response length: {avg_len:.2f} tokens")
    print(f"Logs written to: {out_path}")
    return num_correct, num_examples, acc


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = parse_args()

    if args.device == "auto":
        device = get_device()
    else:
        device = torch.device(args.device)

    which_model = args.which_model
    dataset_size = args.dataset_size
    max_new_tokens = args.max_new_tokens

    print("Model:", which_model)
    print("Device:", device)
    dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")

    math_data = load_math500_test()

    if args.which_model == "instruct":
        which_model = "reasoning"
    else:
        which_model = args.which_model

    if args.checkpoint_path:
        # To load the saved RL checkpoint files from chapter 6
        tokenizer = load_tokenizer_only(which_model=which_model)
        model = Qwen3Model(QWEN_CONFIG_06_B)
        state_dict = torch.load(args.checkpoint_path, map_location="cpu")
        model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
        model.to(device)
        if args.compile:
            torch._dynamo.config.allow_unspec_int_on_nn_module = True
            model = torch.compile(model)
    else:
        model, tokenizer = load_model_and_tokenizer(
            which_model=which_model,
            device=device,
            use_compile=args.compile
        )

    if args.which_model == "instruct":
        tokenizer.add_thinking = False

    model.eval()
    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("high")

    if args.hybrid_parser:
        backend_ok = bonus.normalize_text_hybrid(r"\frac{1}{2}") == "1/2"
        print("LaTeX backend ready:", backend_ok)
        if not backend_ok:
            print('Suggestion: uv pip install "antlr4-python3-runtime==4.11.*"')

            verbose=args.verbose,
        )

from pathlib import Path
import json
import re
import time

import requests
from sympy import simplify
from sympy.parsing import sympy_parser as spp
from sympy.core.sympify import SympifyError
from sympy.polys.polyerrors import PolynomialError
from tokenize import TokenError
import torch

from .qwen3 import (
    download_qwen3_small,
    Qwen3Tokenizer,
    Qwen3Model,
    QWEN_CONFIG_06_B
)
from .ch02 import (
    generate_text_basic_stream_cache
)

RE_NUMBER = re.compile(
    r"-?(?:\d+/\d+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?)"
)

LATEX_FIXES = [  # Latex formatting to be replaced
    (r"\\left\s*", ""),
    (r"\\right\s*", ""),
    (r"\\,|\\!|\\;|\\:", ""),
    (r"\\cdot", "*"),
    (r"\u00B7|\u00D7", "*"),
    (r"\\\^\\circ", ""),
    (r"\\dfrac", r"\\frac"),
    (r"\\tfrac", r"\\frac"),
    (r"°", ""),
]

RE_SPECIAL = re.compile(r"<\|[^>]+?\|>")  # strip chat special tokens like <|assistant|>
SUPERSCRIPT_MAP = {
    "⁰": "0", "¹": "1", "²": "2", "³": "3", "⁴": "4",
    "⁵": "5", "⁶": "6", "⁷": "7", "⁸": "8", "⁹": "9",
    "⁺": "+", "⁻": "-", "⁽": "(", "⁾": ")",
}


def load_model_and_tokenizer(which_model, device, use_compile, local_dir="qwen3"):
    if which_model == "base":

        download_qwen3_small(
            kind="base", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir=local_dir
        )

        tokenizer_path = Path(local_dir) / "tokenizer-base.json"
        model_path = Path(local_dir) / "qwen3-0.6B-base.pth"
        tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path)

    elif which_model == "reasoning":

        download_qwen3_small(
            kind="reasoning", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir=local_dir
        )

        tokenizer_path = Path(local_dir) / "tokenizer-reasoning.json"
        model_path = Path(local_dir) / "qwen3-0.6B-reasoning.pth"
        tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(
            tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path,
            apply_chat_template=True,
            add_generation_prompt=True,
            add_thinking=True,
        )

    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid choice: which_model={which_model}")

    model = Qwen3Model(QWEN_CONFIG_06_B)
    model.load_state_dict(torch.load(model_path))

    model.to(device)

    if use_compile:
        torch._dynamo.config.allow_unspec_int_on_nn_module = True
        model = torch.compile(model)

    return model, tokenizer


def load_tokenizer_only(which_model, local_dir="qwen3"):
    if which_model == "base":
        download_qwen3_small(
            kind="base", tokenizer_only=True, out_dir=local_dir
        )

        tokenizer_path = Path(local_dir) / "tokenizer-base.json"
        tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path)

    elif which_model == "reasoning":
        download_qwen3_small(
            kind="reasoning", tokenizer_only=True, out_dir=local_dir
        )

        tokenizer_path = Path(local_dir) / "tokenizer-reasoning.json"
        tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(
            tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path,
            apply_chat_template=True,
            add_generation_prompt=True,
            add_thinking=True,
        )

    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid choice: which_model={which_model}")

    return tokenizer


def generate_text_stream_concat(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device, max_new_tokens,
    verbose=False,
):
    input_ids = torch.tensor(
        tokenizer.encode(prompt), device=device
        ).unsqueeze(0)

    generated_ids = []
    for token in generate_text_basic_stream_cache(
        model=model,
        token_ids=input_ids,
        max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
        eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id,
    ):
        next_token_id = token.squeeze(0)
        generated_ids.append(next_token_id.item())

        if verbose:
            print(
                tokenizer.decode(next_token_id.tolist()),
                end="",
                flush=True
            )
    return tokenizer.decode(generated_ids)


def get_last_boxed(text):
    # Find the last occurrence of "\boxed"
    boxed_start_idx = text.rfind(r"\boxed")
    if boxed_start_idx == -1:
        return None

    # Get position after "\boxed"
    current_idx = boxed_start_idx + len(r"\boxed")

    # Skip any whitespace after "\boxed"
    while current_idx < len(text) and text[current_idx].isspace():
        current_idx += 1

    # Expect an opening brace "{"
    if current_idx >= len(text) or text[current_idx] != "{":
        return None

    # Parse the braces with nesting
    current_idx += 1
    brace_depth = 1
    content_start_idx = current_idx

    while current_idx < len(text) and brace_depth > 0:
        char = text[current_idx]
        if char == "{":
            brace_depth += 1
        elif char == "}":
            brace_depth -= 1
        current_idx += 1

    # Account for unbalanced braces
    if brace_depth != 0:
        return None

    # Extract content inside the outermost braces
    return text[content_start_idx:current_idx-1]


def extract_final_candidate(text, fallback="number_then_full"):
    # Default return value if nothing matches
    result = ""

    if text:
        # Prefer the last boxed expression if present
        boxed = get_last_boxed(text.strip())
        if boxed:
            result = boxed.strip().strip("$ ")

        # If no boxed expression, try fallback
        elif fallback in ("number_then_full", "number_only"):
            m = RE_NUMBER.findall(text)
            if m:
                # Use last number
                result = m[-1]
            elif fallback == "number_then_full":
                # Else return full text if no number found
                result = text
    return result


def normalize_text(text):
    if not text:
        return ""
    text = RE_SPECIAL.sub("", text).strip()

    # Strip leading multiple-choice labels
    # E.g., like "c. 3" -> 3, or "b: 2" -> 2
    match = re.match(r"^[A-Za-z]\s*[.:]\s*(.+)$", text)
    if match:
        text = match.group(1)

    # Remove angle-degree markers
    text = re.sub(r"\^\s*\{\s*\\circ\s*\}", "", text)   # ^{\circ}
    text = re.sub(r"\^\s*\\circ", "", text)             # ^\circ
    text = text.replace("°", "")                        # Unicode degree

    # unwrap \text{...} if the whole string is wrapped
    match = re.match(r"^\\text\{(?P<x>.+?)\}$", text)
    if match:
        text = match.group("x")

    # strip inline/display math wrappers \( \) \[ \]
    text = re.sub(r"\\\(|\\\)|\\\[|\\\]", "", text)

    # light LaTeX canonicalization
    for pat, rep in LATEX_FIXES:
        text = re.sub(pat, rep, text)

    # convert unicode superscripts into exponent form (e.g., 2² -> 2**2)
    def convert_superscripts(s, base=None):
        converted = "".join(
            SUPERSCRIPT_MAP[ch] if ch in SUPERSCRIPT_MAP else ch
            for ch in s
        )
        if base is None:
            return converted
        return f"{base}**{converted}"

    text = re.sub(
        r"([0-9A-Za-z\)\]\}])([⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹⁺⁻]+)",
        lambda m: convert_superscripts(m.group(2), base=m.group(1)),
        text,
    )
    text = convert_superscripts(text)

    # numbers/roots
    text = text.replace("\\%", "%").replace("$", "").replace("%", "")
    text = re.sub(
        r"\\sqrt\s*\{([^}]*)\}",
        lambda match: f"sqrt({match.group(1)})",
        text,
    )
    text = re.sub(
        r"\\sqrt\s+([^\\\s{}]+)",
        lambda match: f"sqrt({match.group(1)})",
        text,
    )

    # fractions
    text = re.sub(
        r"\\frac\s*\{([^{}]+)\}\s*\{([^{}]+)\}",
        lambda match: f"({match.group(1)})/({match.group(2)})",
        text,
    )
    text = re.sub(
        r"\\frac\s+([^\s{}]+)\s+([^\s{}]+)",
        lambda match: f"({match.group(1)})/({match.group(2)})",
        text,
    )

    # exponent and mixed numbers
    text = text.replace("^", "**")
    text = re.sub(
        r"(?<=\d)\s+(\d+/\d+)",
        lambda match: "+" + match.group(1),
        text,
    )

    # 1,234 -> 1234
    text = re.sub(
        r"(?<=\d),(?=\d\d\d(\D|$))",
        "",
        text,
    )

    return text.replace("{", "").replace("}", "").strip().lower()


def sympy_parser(expr):
    # To avoid crashing on long garbage responses
    # that some badly trained models (chapter 6) may emit
    if expr is None or len(expr) > 2000:
        return None
    try:
        return spp.parse_expr(
            expr,
            transformations=(
                # Standard transformations like handling parentheses
                *spp.standard_transformations,

                # Allow omitted multiplication symbols (e.g., "2x" -> 2*x")
                spp.implicit_multiplication_application,
            ),

            # Evaluate during parsing so simple constants simplify (e.g., 2+3 -> 5)
            evaluate=True,
        )
    except (SympifyError, SyntaxError, TypeError, AttributeError,
            IndexError, TokenError, ValueError, PolynomialError):
        return None


def equality_check(expr_gtruth, expr_pred):
    # First, check if the two expressions are exactly the same string
    if expr_gtruth == expr_pred:
        return True

    # Parse both expressions into SymPy objects (returns None if parsing fails)
    gtruth, pred = sympy_parser(expr_gtruth), sympy_parser(expr_pred)

    # If both expressions were parsed successfully, try symbolic comparison
    if gtruth is not None and pred is not None:
        try:
            # If the difference is 0, they are equivalent
            return simplify(gtruth - pred) == 0
        except (SympifyError, TypeError):
            pass

    return False


def split_into_parts(text):
    result = [text]

    if text:
        # Check if text looks like a tuple or list, e.g. "(a, b)" or "[a, b]"
        if (
            len(text) >= 2
            and text[0] in "([" and text[-1] in ")]"
            and "," in text[1:-1]
        ):
            # Split on commas inside brackets and strip whitespace
            items = [p.strip() for p in text[1:-1].split(",")]
            if all(items):
                result = items
    else:
        # If text is empty, return an empty list
        result = []

    return result


def grade_answer(pred_text, gt_text):
    result = False  # Default outcome if checks fail

    # Only continue if both inputs are non-empty strings
    if pred_text is not None and gt_text is not None:
        gt_parts = split_into_parts(
            normalize_text(gt_text)
        )  # Break ground truth into comparable parts

        pred_parts = split_into_parts(
            normalize_text(pred_text)
        )  # Break prediction into comparable parts

        # Ensure both sides have same number of valid parts
        if (gt_parts and pred_parts
           and len(gt_parts) == len(pred_parts)):
            result = all(
                equality_check(gt, pred)
                for gt, pred in zip(gt_parts, pred_parts)
            )  # Check each part for mathematical equivalence

    return result  # True only if all checks passed


def run_demos_table(tests):
    header = ("Test", "Expect", "Got", "Status")
    rows = []
    for name, pred, gtruth, expect in tests:
        got = grade_answer(pred, gtruth)  # Run equality check
        status = "PASS" if got == expect else "FAIL"
        rows.append((name, str(expect), str(got), status))

    data = [header] + rows

    # Compute max width for each column to align table nicely
    col_widths = [
        max(len(row[i]) for row in data)
        for i in range(len(header))
    ]

    # Print table row by row
    for row in data:
        line = " | ".join(
            row[i].ljust(col_widths[i])
            for i in range(len(header))
        )
        print(line)

    # Print summary of passed tests
    passed = sum(r[3] == "PASS" for r in rows)
    print(f"\nPassed {passed}/{len(rows)}")


def render_prompt(prompt):
    template = (
        "You are a helpful math assistant.\n"
        "Answer the question and write the final result on a new line as:\n"
        "\\boxed{ANSWER}\n\n"
        f"Question:\n{prompt}\n\nAnswer:"
    )
    return template


def load_math500_test(local_path="math500_test.json", save_copy=True):
    local_path = Path(local_path)
    url = (
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/"
        "main/ch03/01_main-chapter-code/math500_test.json"
    )

    if local_path.exists():
        with local_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    else:
        r = requests.get(url, timeout=30)
        r.raise_for_status()
        data = r.json()

        if save_copy:  # Saves a local copy
            with local_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(data, f, indent=2)

    return data


def mini_eval_demo(model, tokenizer, device):
    ex = {  # Test example with "problem" and "answer" fields
        "problem": "Compute 1/2 + 1/6.",
        "answer": "2/3"
    }
    prompt = render_prompt(ex["problem"])     # 1. Apply prompt template
    gen_text = generate_text_stream_concat(   # 2. Generate response
        model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
        max_new_tokens=64,
    )
    pred_answer = extract_final_candidate(gen_text)  # 3. Extract and normalize answer
    is_correct = grade_answer(                       # 4. Grade answer
        pred_answer, ex["answer"]
    )
    print(f"Device: {device}")
    print(f"Prediction: {pred_answer}")
    print(f"Ground truth: {ex['answer']}")
    print(f"Correct: {is_correct}")


def eta_progress_message(
    processed,
    total,
    start_time,
    show_eta=False,
    label="Progress",
):
    progress = f"{label}: {processed}/{total}"
    pad_width = len(f"{label}: {total}/{total} | ETA: 00h 00m 00s")
    if not show_eta or processed <= 0:
        return progress.ljust(pad_width)

    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    if elapsed <= 0:
        return progress.ljust(pad_width)

    remaining = max(total - processed, 0)

    if processed:
        avg_time = elapsed / processed
        eta_seconds = avg_time * remaining
    else:
        eta_seconds = 0

    eta_seconds = max(int(round(eta_seconds)), 0)
    minutes, rem_seconds = divmod(eta_seconds, 60)
    hours, minutes = divmod(minutes, 60)
    if hours:
        eta = f"{hours}h {minutes:02d}m {rem_seconds:02d}s"
    elif minutes:
        eta = f"{minutes:02d}m {rem_seconds:02d}s"
    else:
        eta = f"{rem_seconds:02d}s"

    message = f"{progress} | ETA: {eta}"
    return message.ljust(pad_width)


def evaluate_math500_stream(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    device,
    math_data,
    out_path=None,
    max_new_tokens=512,
    verbose=False,
):

    if out_path is None:
        dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")  # Make filename compatible with Windows
        out_path = Path(f"math500-{dev_name}.jsonl")

    num_examples = len(math_data)
    num_correct = 0
    total_len = 0  # Calculates the average response length (see exercise 3.2)
    start_time = time.time()

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:  # Save results for inspection
        for i, row in enumerate(math_data, start=1):
            prompt = render_prompt(row["problem"])    # 1. Apply prompt template
            gen_text = generate_text_stream_concat(   # 2. Generate response
                model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
                max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
                verbose=verbose,
            )
            total_len += len(tokenizer.encode(gen_text))

            extracted = extract_final_candidate(  # 3. Extract and normalize answer
                gen_text
            )
            is_correct = grade_answer(            # 4. Grade answer
                extracted, row["answer"]
            )
            num_correct += int(is_correct)

            record = {  # Record to be saved for inspection
                "index": i,
                "problem": row["problem"],
                "gtruth_answer": row["answer"],
                "generated_text": gen_text,
                "extracted": extracted,
                "correct": bool(is_correct),
            }
            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

            progress_msg = eta_progress_message(
                processed=i,
                total=num_examples,
                start_time=start_time,
                show_eta=True,
                label="MATH-500",
            )
            print(progress_msg, end="\r", flush=True)
            if verbose:  # Print responses during the generation process
                print(
                    f"\n\n{'='*50}\n{progress_msg}\n"
                    f"{'='*50}\nExtracted: {extracted}\n"
                    f"Expected:  {row['answer']}\n"
                    f"Correct so far: {num_correct}\n{'-'*50}"
                )

    # Print summary information
    seconds_elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    acc = num_correct / num_examples if num_examples else 0.0
    print(f"\nAccuracy: {acc*100:.1f}% ({num_correct}/{num_examples})")
    print(f"Total time: {seconds_elapsed/60:.1f} min")
    avg_len = total_len / num_examples
    print(f"Average response length: {avg_len:.2f} tokens")
    print(f"Logs written to: {out_path}")
    return num_correct, num_examples, acc

from pathlib import Path
import torch


from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import (
    download_qwen3_small,
    Qwen3Tokenizer,
    Qwen3Model,
    QWEN_CONFIG_06_B
)


def load_model_and_tokenizer(
    which_model, device, use_compile, local_dir="qwen3"
):
    if which_model == "base":

        download_qwen3_small(
            kind="base", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir=local_dir
        )

        tokenizer_path = Path(local_dir) / "tokenizer-base.json"
        model_path = Path(local_dir) / "qwen3-0.6B-base.pth"
        tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path)

    elif which_model == "reasoning":

        download_qwen3_small(
            kind="reasoning", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir=local_dir
        )

        tokenizer_path = Path(local_dir) / "tokenizer-reasoning.json"
        model_path = Path(local_dir) / "qwen3-0.6B-reasoning.pth"
        tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(
            tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path,
            apply_chat_template=True,
            add_generation_prompt=True,
            add_thinking=True,
        )

    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid choice: which_model={which_model}")

    model = Qwen3Model(QWEN_CONFIG_06_B)
    model.load_state_dict(torch.load(model_path))

    model.to(device)

    if use_compile:
        torch._dynamo.config.allow_unspec_int_on_nn_module = True
        model = torch.compile(model)

    return model, tokenizer

def generate_text_stream_concat(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device, max_new_tokens,
    verbose=False,
):
    input_ids = torch.tensor(
        tokenizer.encode(prompt), device=device
        ).unsqueeze(0)

    generated_ids = []
    for token in generate_text_basic_stream_cache(
        model=model,
        token_ids=input_ids,
        max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
        eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id,
    ):
        next_token_id = token.squeeze(0)
        generated_ids.append(next_token_id.item())

        if verbose:
            print(
                tokenizer.decode(next_token_id.tolist()),
                end="",
                flush=True
            )
    return tokenizer.decode(generated_ids)

# ---- notebook cell 28 ----
def get_last_boxed(text):
    # Find the last occurrence of "\boxed"
    boxed_start_idx = text.rfind(r"\boxed")
    if boxed_start_idx == -1:
        return None

    # Get position after "\boxed"
    current_idx = boxed_start_idx + len(r"\boxed")

    # Skip any whitespace after "\boxed"
    while current_idx < len(text) and text[current_idx].isspace():
        current_idx += 1

    # Expect an opening brace "{"
    if current_idx >= len(text) or text[current_idx] != "{":
        return None

    # Parse the braces with nesting
    current_idx += 1
    brace_depth = 1
    content_start_idx = current_idx

    while current_idx < len(text) and brace_depth > 0:
        char = text[current_idx]
        if char == "{":
            brace_depth += 1
        elif char == "}":
            brace_depth -= 1
        current_idx += 1

    # Account for unbalanced braces
    if brace_depth != 0:
        return None

    # Extract content inside the outermost braces
    return text[content_start_idx:current_idx-1]

import re

RE_NUMBER = re.compile(
    r"-?(?:\d+/\d+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?)"
)

def extract_final_candidate(text, fallback="number_then_full"):
    # Default return value if nothing matches
    result = ""

    if text:
        # Prefer the last boxed expression if present
        boxed = get_last_boxed(text.strip())
        if boxed:
            result = boxed.strip().strip("$ ")

        # If no boxed expression, try fallback
        elif fallback in ("number_then_full", "number_only"):
            m = RE_NUMBER.findall(text)
            if m:
                # Use last number
                result = m[-1]
            elif fallback == "number_then_full":
                # Else return full text if no number found
                result = text
    return result

# ---- notebook cell 39 ----
LATEX_FIXES = [  # Latex formatting to be replaced
    (r"\\left\s*", ""),
    (r"\\right\s*", ""),
    (r"\\,|\\!|\\;|\\:", ""),
    (r"\\cdot", "*"),
    (r"\u00B7|\u00D7", "*"),
    (r"\\\^\\circ", ""),
    (r"\\dfrac", r"\\frac"),
    (r"\\tfrac", r"\\frac"),
    (r"°", ""),
]

RE_SPECIAL = re.compile(r"<\|[^>]+?\|>")  # strip chat special tokens like <|assistant|>

def normalize_text(text):
    if not text:
        return ""
    text = RE_SPECIAL.sub("", text).strip()
    SUPERSCRIPT_MAP = {
        "⁰": "0", "¹": "1", "²": "2", "³": "3", "⁴": "4",
        "⁵": "5", "⁶": "6", "⁷": "7", "⁸": "8", "⁹": "9",
        "⁺": "+", "⁻": "-", "⁽": "(", "⁾": ")",
    }

    # Strip leading multiple-choice labels
    # E.g., like "c. 3" -> 3, or "b: 2" -> 2
    match = re.match(r"^[A-Za-z]\s*[.:]\s*(.+)$", text)
    if match:
        text = match.group(1)
        
    # Remove angle-degree markers
    text = re.sub(r"\^\s*\{\s*\\circ\s*\}", "", text)   # ^{\circ}
    text = re.sub(r"\^\s*\\circ", "", text)             # ^\circ
    text = text.replace("°", "")                        # Unicode degree

    # unwrap \text{...} if the whole string is wrapped
    match = re.match(r"^\\text\{(?P<x>.+?)\}$", text)
    if match:
        text = match.group("x")

    # strip inline/display math wrappers \( \) \[ \]
    text = re.sub(r"\\\(|\\\)|\\\[|\\\]", "", text)

    # light LaTeX canonicalization
    for pat, rep in LATEX_FIXES:
        text = re.sub(pat, rep, text)

    def convert_superscripts(s, base=None):
        converted = "".join(
            SUPERSCRIPT_MAP[ch] if ch in SUPERSCRIPT_MAP else ch
            for ch in s
        )
        if base is None:
            return converted
        return f"{base}**{converted}"

    # convert unicode superscripts into exponent form (e.g., 2² -> 2**2)m
    text = re.sub(
        r"([0-9A-Za-z\)\]\}])([⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹⁺⁻]+)",
        lambda m: convert_superscripts(m.group(2), base=m.group(1)),
        text,
    )
    text = convert_superscripts(text)
    
    # numbers/roots
    text = text.replace("\\%", "%").replace("$", "").replace("%", "")
    text = re.sub(
        r"\\sqrt\s*\{([^}]*)\}",
        lambda match: f"sqrt({match.group(1)})",
        text,
    )
    text = re.sub(
        r"\\sqrt\s+([^\\\s{}]+)",
        lambda match: f"sqrt({match.group(1)})",
        text,
    )

    # fractions
    text = re.sub(
        r"\\frac\s*\{([^{}]+)\}\s*\{([^{}]+)\}",
        lambda match: f"({match.group(1)})/({match.group(2)})",
        text,
    )
    text = re.sub(
        r"\\frac\s+([^\s{}]+)\s+([^\s{}]+)",
        lambda match: f"({match.group(1)})/({match.group(2)})",
        text,
    )

    # exponent and mixed numbers
    text = text.replace("^", "**")
    text = re.sub(
        r"(?<=\d)\s+(\d+/\d+)",
        lambda match: "+" + match.group(1),
        text,
    )

    # 1,234 -> 1234
    text = re.sub(
        r"(?<=\d),(?=\d\d\d(\D|$))",
        "",
        text,
    )

    return text.replace("{", "").replace("}", "").strip().lower()

from sympy.parsing import sympy_parser as spp
from sympy.core.sympify import SympifyError
from tokenize import TokenError
from sympy.polys.polyerrors import PolynomialError

def sympy_parser(expr):
    # To avoid crashing on long garbage responses 
    # that some badly trained models (chapter 6) may emit
    if expr is None or len(expr) > 2000:
        return None
    try:
        return spp.parse_expr(
            expr,
            transformations=(
                # Standard transformations like handling parentheses
                *spp.standard_transformations,

                # Allow omitted multiplication symbols (e.g., "2x" -> 2*x")
                spp.implicit_multiplication_application,
            ),

            # Evaluate during parsing so simple constants simplify (e.g., 2+3 -> 5)
            evaluate=True,
        )
    except (SympifyError, SyntaxError, TypeError, AttributeError,
            IndexError, TokenError, ValueError, PolynomialError):
        return None

)))

# ---- notebook cell 51 ----
from sympy import simplify

def equality_check(expr_gtruth, expr_pred):
    # First, check if the two expressions are exactly the same string
    if expr_gtruth == expr_pred:
        return True

    # Parse both expressions into SymPy objects (returns None if parsing fails)
    gtruth, pred = sympy_parser(expr_gtruth), sympy_parser(expr_pred)

    # If both expressions were parsed successfully, try symbolic comparison
    if gtruth is not None and pred is not None:
        try:
            # If the difference is 0, they are equivalent
            return simplify(gtruth - pred) == 0
        except (SympifyError, TypeError):
            pass

    return False

))

# ---- notebook cell 57 ----
def split_into_parts(text):
    result = [text]

    if text:
        # Check if text looks like a tuple or list, e.g. "(a, b)" or "[a, b]"
        if (
            len(text) >= 2
            and text[0] in "([" and text[-1] in ")]"
            and "," in text[1:-1]
        ):
            # Split on commas inside brackets and strip whitespace
            items = [p.strip() for p in text[1:-1].split(",")]
            if all(items):
                result = items
    else:
        # If text is empty, return an empty list
        result = []

    return result

# ---- notebook cell 58 ----
split_into_parts(normalize_text(r"(14/3, 2/3)"))

# ---- notebook cell 59 ----
def grade_answer(pred_text, gt_text):
    result = False  # Default outcome if checks fail

    # Only continue if both inputs are non-empty strings
    if pred_text is not None and gt_text is not None:
        gt_parts = split_into_parts(
            normalize_text(gt_text)
        )  # Break ground truth into comparable parts

        pred_parts = split_into_parts(
            normalize_text(pred_text)
        )  # Break prediction into comparable parts

        # Ensure both sides have same number of valid parts
        if (gt_parts and pred_parts
           and len(gt_parts) == len(pred_parts)):
            result = all(
                equality_check(gt, pred)
                for gt, pred in zip(gt_parts, pred_parts)
            )  # Check each part for mathematical equivalence

    return result  # True only if all checks passed

        ("check_6", "(2, 1)", "(1, 2)", False),
        ("check_7", "(1, 2, 3)", "(1, 2)", False),
        ("check_8", "0.5", "1/2", True),
        ("check_9", "0.3333333333", "1/3", False),
        ("check_10", "1,234/2", "617", True),
        ("check_11", r"\text{2/3}", "2/3", True),
        ("check_12", "50%", "1/2", False),
        ("check_13", r"2\cdot 3/4", "3/2", True),
        ("check_14", r"90^\circ", "90", True),
        ("check_15", r"\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)", "3/4", True),
        ("check_16", r"2²", "2**2", True),
    ]


def run_demos_table(tests):
    header = ("Test", "Expect", "Got", "Status")
    rows = []
    for name, pred, gtruth, expect in tests:
        got = grade_answer(pred, gtruth)  # Run equality check
        status = "PASS" if got == expect else "FAIL"
        rows.append((name, str(expect), str(got), status))

    data = [header] + rows
    
    # Compute max width for each column to align table nicely
    col_widths = [
        max(len(row[i]) for row in data)
        for i in range(len(header))
    ]

    # Print table row by row
    for row in data:
        line = " | ".join(
            row[i].ljust(col_widths[i])
            for i in range(len(header))
        )
        print(line)

    # Print summary of passed tests
    passed = sum(r[3] == "PASS" for r in rows)
    print(f"\nPassed {passed}/{len(rows)}")

# ---- notebook cell 63 ----
run_demos_table(tests)

import json
import requests

def load_math500_test(local_path="math500_test.json", save_copy=True):
    local_path = Path(local_path)
    url = (
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/"
        "main/ch03/01_main-chapter-code/math500_test.json"
    )

    if local_path.exists():
        with local_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    else:
        r = requests.get(url, timeout=30)
        r.raise_for_status()
        data = r.json()

        if save_copy:  # Saves a local copy
            with local_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(data, f, indent=2)

    return data

# ---- notebook cell 80 ----
import time


# Helper function to calculate remaining time
def eta_progress_message(
    processed,
    total,
    start_time,
    show_eta=False,
    label="Progress",
):
    progress = f"{label}: {processed}/{total}"
    pad_width = len(f"{label}: {total}/{total} | ETA: 00h 00m 00s")
    if not show_eta or processed <= 0:
        return progress.ljust(pad_width)

    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    if elapsed <= 0:
        return progress.ljust(pad_width)

    remaining = max(total - processed, 0)

    if processed:
        avg_time = elapsed / processed
        eta_seconds = avg_time * remaining
    else:
        eta_seconds = 0

    eta_seconds = max(int(round(eta_seconds)), 0)
    minutes, rem_seconds = divmod(eta_seconds, 60)
    hours, minutes = divmod(minutes, 60)
    if hours:
        eta = f"{hours}h {minutes:02d}m {rem_seconds:02d}s"
    elif minutes:
        eta = f"{minutes:02d}m {rem_seconds:02d}s"
    else:
        eta = f"{rem_seconds:02d}s"

    message = f"{progress} | ETA: {eta}"
    return message.ljust(pad_width)

def evaluate_math500_stream(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    device,
    math_data,
    out_path=None,
    max_new_tokens=512,
    verbose=False,
):

    if out_path is None:
        dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")  # Make filename compatible with Windows
        out_path = Path(f"math500-{dev_name}.jsonl")

    num_examples = len(math_data)
    num_correct = 0
    start_time = time.time()

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:  # Save results for inspection
        for i, row in enumerate(math_data, start=1):
            prompt = render_prompt(row["problem"])    # 1. Apply prompt template
            gen_text = generate_text_stream_concat(   # 2. Generate response
                model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
                max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
                verbose=verbose,
            )

            extracted = extract_final_candidate(  # 3. Extract and normalize answer
                gen_text
            )
            is_correct = grade_answer(            # 4. Grade answer
                extracted, row["answer"]
            )
            num_correct += int(is_correct)

            record = {  # Record to be saved for inspection
                "index": i,
                "problem": row["problem"],
                "gtruth_answer": row["answer"],
                "generated_text": gen_text,
                "extracted": extracted,
                "correct": bool(is_correct),
            }
            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

            progress_msg = eta_progress_message(
                processed=i,
                total=num_examples,
                start_time=start_time,
                show_eta=True,
                label="MATH-500",
            )
            print(progress_msg, end="\r", flush=True)
            if verbose:  # Print responses during the generation process
                print(
                    f"\n\n{'='*50}\n{progress_msg}\n"
                    f"{'='*50}\nExtracted: {extracted}\n"
                    f"Expected:  {row['answer']}\n"
                    f"Correct so far: {num_correct}\n{'-'*50}"
                )

    # Print summary information
    seconds_elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    acc = num_correct / num_examples if num_examples else 0.0
    print(f"\nAccuracy: {acc*100:.1f}% ({num_correct}/{num_examples})")
    print(f"Total time: {seconds_elapsed/60:.1f} min")
    print(f"Logs written to: {out_path}")
    return num_correct, num_examples, acc

# ---- notebook cell 82 ----
print("Model:", WHICH_MODEL)
print("Device:", device)
num_correct, num_examples, acc = evaluate_math500_stream(
    model, tokenizer, device, 
    math_data=math_data[:10],
    max_new_tokens=2048,
    verbose=False
)

04.1Chapter 4 — Improving reasoning with inference-time scaling

Introduction to inference-time scaling

Is chapter me hum model ko dobara train kiye bina, sirf inference ke time zyada compute kharch karke, reasoning aur accuracy improve karna seekhenge. Yehi hai inference-time scaling — jise test-time scaling bhi kehte hain.

Reasoning improve karne ke do tareeke

  • Training-time scaling: training ke dauran zyada compute lagao — bada model, zyada data, zyada training steps. Ye mehenga hai aur ek baar training ho jaye to wapas nahi badalta.
  • Inference-time scaling: model train hone ke baad, har jawab generate karte time zyada compute lagao. Model ke weights bilkul same rehte hain — sirf generation ke time zyada kaam hota hai.
  • Dono ko combine bhi kiya jata hai: pehle achhi training, phir inference par extra compute. Is book me pehle inference-time tareeke aate hain (chapter 4 aur 5), phir training-time tareeke (chapter 6 se aage).

Inference-time scaling ka matlab kya hai, practically?

Model ko ek sawal ka jawab dene ke liye zyada tokens generate karne do, ya ek hi sawal ke kai jawab generate karke unme se best chuno, ya ek jawab ko baar-baar sudhaaro. Har tareeke me compute badhta hai — aur aksar accuracy bhi.

  • Zyada tokens generate karna = model "zyada der sochta hai" — jaise step-by-step reasoning likhna.
  • Kai jawab generate karna = alag-alag raaste try karke dekhna, phir vote se best chunnna.
  • Jawab ko refine karna = pehle draft likho, phir uski galtiyaan pakdo aur sudhaaro (ye chapter 5 ka topic hai).

Is chapter ke teen tareeke

  • Method 1 — Chain-of-thought prompting: prompt me "Explain step by step." jod do, taaki model final answer se pehle apni reasoning likhe.
  • Method 2 — Self-consistency sampling: ek hi prompt ke kai jawab sample karo aur majority vote se sabse frequent jawab chuno.
  • Method 3 — Self-refinement: model apna jawab khud review karke sudhaare. Ye agle chapter me detail me aayega.
Yaad rakho: Inference-time scaling accuracy badhata hai, lekin free me nahi — har jawab ke liye zyada tokens, zyada time aur zyada cost lagti hai. Ye trade-off poore chapter ka central theme hai.

Setup: base model load karna aur flexible wrapper

Is chapter me hum wahi base model use karte hain jo chapter 3 me tha — 0.6B parameters wala base model — aur chapter 3 wala generation wrapper thoda flexible banate hain.

  • Chapter me pehli baar CPU par chalane ki salah di gayi hai, kyunki GPU par results thode alag aa sakte hain.
  • Naya wrapper generate_text_stream_concat_flex generation function ko argument ke roop me leta hai — isse hum sirf generation logic badal kar alag-alag tareeke fairly compare kar sakte hain, bina prompt handling ya decoding code dobara likhe.
  • Default roop me ye wahi purana cached generation function use karta hai — isliye pehle jaisa behaviour same rehta hai.
python
def generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device, max_new_tokens,
    verbose=False,
    generate_func=None,   # generation function argument ke roop me
    **generate_kwargs
):
    if generate_func is None:
        generate_func = generate_text_basic_stream_cache
    # ... prompt encode karo, generate_func se tokens lo, decode karo ...

Ek chhota sa demo — greedy decoding galat jawab deta hai

Chapter ka running example ek MATH-500 problem hai: "Half the value of 3x - 9 is x + 37. What is the value of x?" Sahi jawab hai 83.

  • Seedha greedy decoding (hamesha sabse probable token chuno) sirf \boxed{20} deta hai — galat.
  • Yehi woh starting point hai jise is chapter ke tareeke sudhaarte hain — pehle chain-of-thought prompting se, phir sampling aur voting se.
  • Baseline yaad rakho: chapter 3 ke hisab se base model ki MATH-500 accuracy sirf 15.2% thi, jabki reasoning variant ki 48.2% thi.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Inference-time scaling = weights badle bina, generation ke time zyada compute.
  • Training-time scaling = training ke time zyada compute; dono combine hote hain.
  • Is chapter ke do tareeke: chain-of-thought prompting aur self-consistency; teesra (self-refinement) agle chapter me.
  • Flexible wrapper se hum generation function swap karke tareeke compare kar sakte hain.

04.2Chapter 4 — Improving reasoning with inference-time scaling

Generating better responses with chain-of-thought prompting

Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting is chapter ka pehla aur sabse simple inference-time tareeka hai — prompt me ek chhoti si line jod do, aur model khud step-by-step reasoning likhne lagta hai.

CoT prompting kaise kaam karta hai?

Model ko seedha final answer maangne ke bajay, hum prompt ke end me ye instruction jod dete hain: "Explain step by step." Bas itna sa change — aur model pehle apni reasoning likhta hai, phir final answer deta hai.

  • Ye ek sequential tareeka hai: model zyada tokens generate karta hai, ek ke baad ek, reasoning chain ke roop me.
  • Isse "zero-shot chain-of-thought" bhi kehte hain, kyunki hum koi example nahi dete — sirf instruction dete hain.
  • Alag-alag phrasing bhi hoti hai — jaise "Let's think step by step." — aur kaun si phrasing best hai, ye model aur task par depend karta hai. Is chapter me "Explain step by step." isliye chuni gayi, kyunki experiments me ye achhi chali.
python
prompt_cot = prompt + " \n\nExplain step by step."

response_cot = generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
    model, tokenizer, prompt_cot, device,
    max_new_tokens=2048, verbose=True,
)

Wahi example, ab sahi jawab

Ussi problem par — "Half the value of 3x - 9 is x + 37" — CoT prompt ke saath model pehle equation ko step by step solve karta hai: dono taraf 2 se multiply karo, 2x subtract karo, 9 add karo — aur ant me sahi jawab deta hai: \boxed{83}.

  • Bina CoT ke jawab tha 20 (galat). CoT ke saath jawab hai 83 (sahi).
  • Poori MATH-500 dataset par base model ki accuracy 15.2% se badh kar 40.6% ho gayi — sirf ek prompt line se.
  • Lekin time bhi badha: lagbhag 10 minute se lagbhag 85 minute. Lambi reasoning ka matlab hai zyada tokens, aur har token ke liye ek forward pass.

CoT accuracy kyun badhata hai?

  • Khud ko correct karne ka mauka: steps likhte time model beech me galti pakad sakta hai aur aage sahi raasta le sakta hai.
  • Training data se match: bade math aur logic datasets me detailed solutions hote hain — step-by-step maangna model ko usi pattern par le aata hai jo usne training me dekha tha.
  • Naya knowledge nahi: CoT model ko nayi jaankari nahi deta — ye sirf uske existing knowledge ko use karne ka tareeka badalta hai. Isi liye ye itna effective hai.

Kab CoT nuksaan bhi pahuncha sakta hai?

  • Overthinking: bahut simple problem par lambi reasoning likhna kabhi-kabhi model ko bhatka deta hai — woh galat explanation likh kar khud ko hi mislead kar leta hai.
  • Galat reasoning: step-by-step likhna sahi hone ki guarantee nahi hai — reasoning galat bhi ho sakti hai, aur phir final answer bhi galat hoga.
  • Trained reasoning models ko zaroorat nahi: jo model pehle se reasoning likhne ke liye train hua hai, use CoT prompt se zyada fayda nahi hota — woh waise bhi explanation likhta hai.
Rule of thumb: Multi-step problems — math, code, logic — par CoT aksar madad karta hai. Ek-line ke simple sawal par seedha jawab hi behtar hota hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • CoT = prompt me "Explain step by step." jodna; model pehle reasoning likhta hai, phir answer.
  • MATH-500 par base model: 15.2% se 40.6% — lekin runtime 10 se 85 minute.
  • CoT naya knowledge nahi deta, existing knowledge ko behtar use karwata hai.
  • Simple problem par overthinking nuksaan bhi kar sakta hai.

04.3Chapter 4 — Improving reasoning with inference-time scaling

Controlling output diversity with temperature scaling

Chain-of-thought se model lambi reasoning likhta hai. Ab hume ek aur cheez chahiye: ek hi prompt ke kai alag-alag jawab — taaki hum unme se best chunn sakein. Iske liye pehle samajhna hoga ki model agla token kaise chunta hai, aur temperature us choice ko kaise badalta hai.

Pehle: agla token kaise chuna jata hai?

Prompt "The capital of Germany is" par model ka jawab hai " Berlin". Iske peeche teen steps hote hain:

  1. Tokenize: input text token IDs me badalta hai — jaise [785, 6722, 315, 9856, 374].
  2. Logits: model har vocabulary token ke liye ek score deta hai — in scores ko logits kehte hain. Is model ki vocabulary 151,936 tokens ki hai, isliye logits ka shape [1, 151936] hota hai.
  3. Argmax: sabse bada score wala token chuna jata hai — yahan token ID 19846, jo " Berlin" ko decode karta hai. Ise greedy decoding kehte hain.

Logits ka range is example me lagbhag -8 se 20 tak tha, jisme " Berlin" ka logit sabse uncha (20 ke aas-paas) tha.

Temperature: logits ko rescale karna

Temperature ek number hai jisse hum logits ko divide kar dete hain, softmax se pehle. Formula simple hai: softmax(logits / T).

  • T = 1.0: koi change nahi — divide by 1 wahi number deta hai.
  • T < 1 (jaise 0.5): distribution sharper ho jati hai — top token aur zyada dominant, model zyada confident, kam diverse.
  • T > 1 (jaise 5.0): distribution flatter ho jati hai — top token aur baaki tokens ke beech ka gap kam, model zyada diverse, kam predictable.
  • T = 0: greedy decoding — hamesha sabse probable token, koi randomness nahi.
python
def scale_logits_by_temperature(logits, temperature):
    if temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Temperature must be positive")
    return logits / temperature

Temperature ka naam physics se aaya hai — wahan temperature system me randomness ya movement ko control karta hai. LLMs me bhi wahi idea hai: temperature next-token choice ki randomness ko control karta hai.

Logits se probabilities: softmax

Rescaled logits ko torch.softmax se probabilities me badla jata hai — har value 0 aur 1 ke beech, aur sabka sum 1.

  • Softmax ka formula hai: softmax(z_i) = exp(z_i) / sum(exp(z_j)) — har score ka exponential lekar total se divide kar do.
  • Probability ko model ki confidence ki tarah padha ja sakta hai: zyada probability matlab model ko us token par zyada bharosa.
  • Example: T = 5.0 par " Berlin" ki probability sirf 0.0003 thi — kyunki distribution bahut flat thi. Wahi T = 0.5 par badh kar 0.3398 ho gayi, aur T = 0.35 par lagbhag 0.42.

Probabilities se sampling: multinomial

Greedy decoding hamesha top token leta hai. Sampling me hum probability distribution se randomly ek token draw karte hain — zyada probability wale token ke aane ke chances zyada, lekin kam probability wala bhi aa sakta hai.

  • Example: probabilities Berlin 0.70, Munich 0.20, Hamburg 0.10 hon to greedy hamesha Berlin dega; sampling 1000 draws me lagbhag 700 baar Berlin, 200 baar Munich aur 100 baar Hamburg dega.
  • Book ke experiment me T = 5.0 par 1000 samples me koi bhi token 2 se zyada baar nahi aaya — aur sab nonsense tokens the. Temperature bahut zyada tha.
  • Wahi T = 0.35 par 1000 samples me " Berlin" 435 baar aaya — aur Munich aur Hamburg bhi thode-thode aaye, jo context me samajh aate hain (Germany ke bade sheher).
  • Code me ye torch.multinomial(probas, num_samples=1) se hota hai. Reproducibility ke liye random seed set kiya jata hai.

Temperature ko generation function me jodna

Ab temperature aur sampling ko text generation function me daal diya jata hai — generate_text_temp_stream_cache. Har step par ye hota hai:

  1. Model se logits lo.
  2. Temperature se rescale karo (agar T 1.0 hai ya None hai to seedha argmax).
  3. Softmax se probabilities banao.
  4. Multinomial se ek token sample karo.
python
if temperature is None or temperature == 1.0:
    next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
else:
    logits = scale_logits_by_temperature(out, temperature)
    probas = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
    next_token = torch.multinomial(probas.cpu(), num_samples=1)

Temperature chunne ke practical rules

  • T = 0.0: greedy decoding — single best answer chahiye ho to.
  • T = 0.3–0.8: thodi diversity, bina reliability khoye — aksar useful range.
  • Bahut zyada T: creative generation ya broad search ke liye, lekin factual tasks par reliability girti hai.
  • Demo me T = 1.1 par model ne galat jawab diya (x = 90/7) — temperature akele accuracy nahi badhata, ye sirf diversity ka control hai.
Yaad rakho: Temperature sampling diversity deta hai, accuracy nahi. Diversity ka fayda agle sections me milega — jab hum kai samples me se vote karenge.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Logits = har token ka raw score; argmax = greedy decoding.
  • Temperature logits ko divide karta hai: T < 1 sharp, T > 1 flat, T = 1 no change.
  • Softmax logits ko probabilities me badalta hai (sum = 1).
  • Multinomial sampling probabilities ke hisab se randomly token chunta hai.
  • T = 0.35 par " Berlin" 435/1000 baar aaya; T = 5.0 par sirf nonsense tokens.
