04.4Chapter 4 — Improving reasoning with inference-time scaling

Balancing diversity and coherence with top-p sampling

Temperature se diversity milti hai — lekin kabhi-kabhi model bahut hi unlikely, nonsense tokens bhi sample kar leta hai. Top-p sampling (jise nucleus sampling bhi kehte hain) is problem ko solve karta hai: bahut kam probability wale tokens ko pehle hi hata do, phir bache hue me se sample karo.

Top-p filter ke 4 steps

  1. Sort: token probabilities ko descending order me sort karo — sabse probable pehle.
  2. Cumulative sum: sorted probabilities ka cumulative sum nikalo — pehla token, pehle do ka sum, pehle teen ka sum, aur aise aage, jab tak total 1 na ho jaye.
  3. Cutoff: sabse chhota subset rakho jiska cumulative probability p ko paar kar jaye. Baaki sab tokens hata do.
  4. Renormalize: bache hue probabilities ko dobara scale karo taaki unka sum phir se 1 ho jaye — warna sampling sahi nahi hogi.

Toy example: 10 tokens, p = 0.8

Book me ek chhota example hai jisme vocabulary sirf 10 tokens ki hai. Toy logits hain [-0.7, -3.0, 0.1, -1.2, 2.0, -1.0, -0.5, -2.0, 0.3, 1.5]. Temperature 1.0 par inki probabilities sort karne ke baad cumulative sum ye banta hai:

python
# sorted probabilities ka cumulative sum (p = 0.8)
# [0.4538, 0.7290, 0.8119, 0.8798, 0.9170, ...]
keep_mask = cumsum <= top_p   # strict rule: sirf 2 tokens bachte hain
keep_mask = (cumsum - sorted_probas) < top_p  # common rule: 3 tokens bachte hain
  • Strict rule (cumsum <= p) se sirf 2 tokens bachte hain, kyunki teesra cumulative value 0.8119, 0.8 se zyada hai.
  • Common rule me woh token bhi rakha jata hai jo threshold ko paar karta hai — isse 3 tokens bachte hain. Isi definition ke hisab se "sabse chhota subset jiska cumulative mass kam se kam p ho" milta hai.
  • Baaki 7 tokens ko zero kar diya jata hai, phir original order wapas laya jata hai, aur bache hue 3 tokens ki probabilities renormalize hoti hain: [0.5589, 0.1021, 0.3390] (baaki sab zero).

Top-p filter ka code

python
def top_p_filter(probas, top_p):
    if top_p is None or top_p >= 1.0:
        return probas
    sorted_probas, sorted_idx = torch.sort(probas, dim=1, descending=True)
    cumprobas = torch.cumsum(sorted_probas, dim=1)
    prefix = cumprobas - sorted_probas
    keep = prefix < top_p
    keep[:, 0] = True  # top token hamesha rakho
    kept_sorted = torch.where(keep, sorted_probas, torch.zeros_like(sorted_probas))
    filtered = torch.zeros_like(probas).scatter(1, sorted_idx, kept_sorted)
    denom = torch.sum(filtered, dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
    return filtered / denom
  • keep[:, 0] = True ek safety hai — agar p bahut chhota ho to bhi top token hamesha bachta hai.
  • scatter filtered values ko wapas original vocabulary order me laata hai.
  • Last step me divide karke renormalize kiya jata hai, taaki probabilities ka sum phir 1 ho.

Asli example par asar: "The capital of Germany is"

Temperature 0.35 par bina filter ke 1000 samples me " Berlin" 435 baar, aur Munich aur Hamburg bhi 3-3 baar aaye. Top-p = 0.8 lagane ke baad:

  • " Berlin" 534 baar aaya — top token ka share badh gaya, kyunki tail hat gayi.
  • Munich aur Hamburg bilkul gayab ho gaye — low-probability options filter ho gaye.
  • Bache hue underscore tokens quiz-style placeholders hain — model ne training me "The capital of Germany is ____" jaise text dekhe hain.

Top-p ko generation function me jodna

Naya function generate_text_top_p_stream_cache temperature wale function jaisa hi hai — bas softmax ke baad aur multinomial se pehle ek extra step hai: probas = top_p_filter(probas, top_p). Experiments me temperature aur top-p dono 0.9 rakhe gaye the.

  • Pipeline ab ye hai: logits → temperature rescale → softmax → top-p filter → multinomial sampling.
  • Math problem par T = 0.5, top-p = 0.8 se model ne \boxed{18} diya — abhi bhi galat. Sampling akele answer sahi nahi karta; ye sirf diverse answers deta hai. Sahi jawab ke liye agle section ka voting chahiye.

Top-k filtering — ek aur option

Top-p ke alawa top-k filtering bhi hoti hai: cumulative probability dekhne ke bajay, sirf k sabse probable tokens rakho, baaki hata do, phir renormalize karo.

  • Top-k: fixed number — hamesha k tokens bachte hain.
  • Top-p: variable number — distribution sharp ho to kam tokens, flat ho to zyada tokens bachte hain.
  • Top-k implement karna simple hai, lekin top-p aaj kal zyada popular hai, kyunki woh distribution ke shape ke hisab se khud adjust ho jata hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baatein

  • Top-p = nucleus sampling: cumulative probability p tak ke top tokens rakho, baaki hata do.
  • Steps: sort → cumsum → cutoff → renormalize.
  • Toy example me p = 0.8 par 3 tokens bache, renormalized probabilities 0.5589, 0.1021, 0.3390.
  • Top-k fixed k tokens rakhta hai; top-p variable rakhta hai.
  • Temperature + top-p akele accuracy nahi badhate — ye diversity ke controls hain.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 4

04.5Chapter 4 — Improving reasoning with inference-time scaling

Improving response accuracy with self-consistency

Ab humare paas saare pieces hain: chain-of-thought prompting, temperature sampling aur top-p filtering. Self-consistency in sabko jod kar ek simple lekin powerful tareeka banata hai — kai jawab generate karo, aur majority vote se sabse frequent jawab chuno.

Self-consistency kya hai?

Naam fancy hai, lekin idea simple majority voting hai. Ek hi prompt ke liye model se kai alag-alag jawab sample karwate hain (temperature > 0 aur top-p ke saath), har jawab se final boxed answer nikalte hain, aur jo answer sabse zyada baar aaya, use final answer maan lete hain.

  1. Sample karo: temperature aur top-p ke saath n alag jawab generate karo.
  2. Extract karo: har jawab se boxed final answer nikalo (chapter 3 wala extraction function reuse hota hai).
  3. Vote karo: sabse frequent answer final answer hai.
python
def self_consistency_vote(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
    num_samples=10, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.9,
    max_new_tokens=2048, seed=None,
):
    short_answers = []
    for i in range(num_samples):
        answer = generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
            model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer, prompt=prompt,
            device=device, max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
            generate_func=generate_text_top_p_stream_cache,
            temperature=temperature, top_p=top_p,
        )
        short_answers.append(extract_final_candidate(answer))
    counts = Counter(short_answers)
    return counts.most_common()  # sabse frequent answer pehle

Wahi example, ab voting se sahi jawab

Ussi problem par 5 samples liye gaye (T = 0.8, top-p = 0.9): jawab aaye 83, 22, 54, 83, 61. Sabse frequent hai 83 — jo sahi jawab hai.

  • Ek single greedy answer galat tha (20). Ek single sampled answer bhi galat ho sakta tha (22, 54 ya 61).
  • Lekin 5 samples me sahi jawab 2 baar aaya — baaki har galat jawab sirf ek baar. Majority vote ne sahi ko chunn liya.
  • CoT prompt ke saath to 5 ke 5 samples sahi (83) aaye — kyunki ye problem CoT ke saath model ke liye kaafi easy ho jati hai.

Results: MATH-500 par kya mila? (Table 4.1)

Poore MATH-500 dataset par experiments ke results ye the (temperature aur top-p dono 0.9 jahan sampling use hui):

  • Baseline, greedy: base model 15.2% (10 minute) · reasoning variant 48.2% (182 minute).
  • CoT prompting: base model 40.6% (85 minute) — sirf prompt badal kar 2.5x se zyada.
  • Temperature + top-p, bina CoT: sirf 17.8% (31 minute) — sampling akele zyada fayda nahi deta.
  • Top-p + self-consistency, bina CoT: n=3 par 29.6%, n=10 par 31.6% — n=3 se n=10 tak lagbhag koi fayda nahi.
  • CoT + self-consistency: n=3 par 42.2%, n=5 par 48.0% (453 minute), n=10 par 52.0% (863 minute).
  • Reasoning variant + self-consistency (n=3): 48.2% se badh kar 55.2% — trained reasoning model ko bhi voting se fayda hota hai.
Takeaway: CoT + self-consistency base model ko 15.2% se 52.0% tak le gaya — bina ek bhi weight badle. Keemat: runtime 10 minute se 863 minute. Accuracy ke badle compute — yahi inference-time scaling ka trade-off hai.

Tie-breaking aur early stopping

  • Tie: agar do jawab barabar frequency par hon to book ka function final answer None deta hai — tie handle nahi karta. Agle chapter ka scorer tie-breaker ban sakta hai.
  • Simple tie-break: pehle aane wala jawab chuno — jaise samples 13, 15, 13, 15, 16 hon to 13 chuno.
  • Early stopping: agar aadhe se zyada answers ek hi jawab par agree kar jayein to aage sampling rok do — time bachta hai, result wahi rehta hai.
  • Parallel: samples independent hote hain, isliye alag-alag GPUs par parallel generate kiye ja sakte hain — total compute same, wall-clock time kam.

Best-of-n aur pass@k — voting ke rishtedaar

Majority vote self-consistency ka ek tareeka hai; iske do rishtedaar concepts bhi samajh lo:

  • Best-of-n: n samples generate karke majority vote ke bajay ek scorer se best sample chuno. Scorer hi decide karta hai kaun sa sample sabse achha hai — isliye best-of-n utna hi achha hai jitna uska scorer. Scorer banana chapter 5 ka topic hai.
  • Pass@k: ye ek evaluation metric hai — k samples me se kam se kam ek sahi ho to pass. Ye batata hai ki sampling se sahi jawab milne ki kitni sambhavna hai, chahe majority vote use pakad paye ya nahi. Majority-vote accuracy se alag metric hai: pass@k zyada hota hai, kyunki ek bhi sahi sample kaafi hai.
  • Self-consistency ka ek limitation: ye boxed, chhote final answer par depend karta hai — lambe, open-ended jawabon par vote karna mushkil hai. Isi liye agle chapter me self-refinement aata hai, jo vote nahi, ek jawab ko sudhaarta hai.

Temperature aur top-p ke practical starting points

  • Self-consistency ke liye temperature lagbhag 0.5–0.9 aur top-p lagbhag 0.7–0.9 reasonable starting points hain.
  • Agar saare answers lagbhag ek jaise dikhein to temperature ya top-p thoda badhao — diversity chahiye.
  • Agar answers nonsense lagne lagein to settings kam karo — pehle temperature ghatao.

Chapter 4 ka summary

  • Chain-of-thought prompting aur self-consistency — dono weights badle bina accuracy badhate hain.
  • Temperature diversity control karta hai; top-p unlikely tokens ko filter karta hai.
  • Flexible wrapper se alag-alag generation strategies plug karke compare ki ja sakti hain.
  • Central trade-off: zyada accuracy ke badle bahut zyada inference compute aur time.
  • Agla chapter: self-refinement — ek jawab ko baar-baar sudhaar kar behtar banana.

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import time

import torch

from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import get_device
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import (
    load_math500_test,
    eta_progress_message,
    extract_final_candidate,
    render_prompt,
    grade_answer,
    generate_text_stream_concat,
    load_model_and_tokenizer
)


def evaluate_math500_stream(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    device,
    math_data,
    out_path=None,
    max_new_tokens=512,
    verbose=False,
    prompt_suffix=""  # NEW
):

    if out_path is None:
        dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")
        out_path = Path(f"math500-{dev_name}.jsonl")

    num_examples = len(math_data)
    num_correct = 0
    start_time = time.time()

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for i, row in enumerate(math_data, start=1):
            prompt = render_prompt(row["problem"])
            prompt += prompt_suffix  # NEW
            gen_text = generate_text_stream_concat(
                model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
                max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
                verbose=verbose,
            )

            extracted = extract_final_candidate(
                gen_text
            )
            is_correct = grade_answer(
                extracted, row["answer"]
            )
            num_correct += int(is_correct)

            record = {
                "index": i,
                "problem": row["problem"],
                "gtruth_answer": row["answer"],
                "generated_text": gen_text,
                "extracted": extracted,
                "correct": bool(is_correct),
            }
            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

            progress_msg = eta_progress_message(
                processed=i,
                total=num_examples,
                start_time=start_time,
                show_eta=True,
                label="MATH-500",
            )
            print(progress_msg, end="\r", flush=True)
            if verbose:
                print(
                    f"\n\n{'='*50}\n{progress_msg}\n"
                    f"{'='*50}\nExtracted: {extracted}\n"
                    f"Expected:  {row['answer']}\n"
                    f"Correct so far: {num_correct}\n{'-'*50}"
                )

    seconds_elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    acc = num_correct / num_examples if num_examples else 0.0
    print(f"\nAccuracy: {acc*100:.1f}% ({num_correct}/{num_examples})")
    print(f"Total time: {seconds_elapsed/60:.1f} min")
    print(f"Logs written to: {out_path}")
    return num_correct, num_examples, acc

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Batch runner for self-consistency sweeps on MATH-500
#
# Usage:
#   bash run_batch_self_consistency_math500.sh
#

WORKDIR="${WORKDIR:-$(pwd)}"

OUTDIR="self_consistency_math500_runs"
mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"

MAIN_LOG="$OUTDIR/all_runs.txt"

echo "=== self-consistency batch start: $(date -Is)" | tee "$MAIN_LOG"
echo "=== WORKDIR: $WORKDIR" | tee -a "$MAIN_LOG"
echo "=== OUTDIR:  $OUTDIR" | tee -a "$MAIN_LOG"
echo | tee -a "$MAIN_LOG"

run_sc () {
    local row="$1"; shift
    local tag="$1"; shift

    local outfile="$OUTDIR/${row}__${tag}.txt"

    echo "=== ${row} (${tag})" | tee -a "$MAIN_LOG"
    echo "=== Output -> ${outfile}" | tee -a "$MAIN_LOG"
    echo "Command: uv run self_consistency_math500.py $*" | tee -a "$MAIN_LOG"

    pushd "$WORKDIR" >/dev/null

    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 uv run python -u self_consistency_math500.py "$@" \
        2>&1 \
    | awk 'BEGIN{RS="\r|\n"; ORS="\n"} {print; fflush()}' \
    | tee "$outfile" \
    | tee -a "$MAIN_LOG"

    popd >/dev/null

    echo | tee -a "$MAIN_LOG"
}

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import time

import torch
from collections import Counter

from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import get_device
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import (
    load_math500_test,
    eta_progress_message,
    render_prompt,
    grade_answer,
    load_model_and_tokenizer,
    extract_final_candidate,
)
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch04 import (
    generate_text_stream_concat_flex,
    generate_text_top_p_stream_cache,
)


def self_consistency_vote(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    prompt,
    device,
    num_samples=10,
    temperature=0.8,
    top_p=0.9,
    max_new_tokens=2048,
    show_progress=True,
    show_long_answer=False,
    seed=None,
    early_stop=True,   # NEW
):
    full_answers, short_answers = [], []
    counts = Counter()
    groups = {}
    majority_winners, final_answer = [], None

    for i in range(num_samples):
        if seed is not None:
            torch.manual_seed(seed + i + 1)

        answer = generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
            model=model,
            tokenizer=tokenizer,
            prompt=prompt,
            device=device,
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
            verbose=show_long_answer,
            generate_func=generate_text_top_p_stream_cache,
            temperature=temperature,
            top_p=top_p,
        )

        short = extract_final_candidate(answer, fallback="number_then_full")
        full_answers.append(answer)
        short_answers.append(short)
        counts[short] += 1
        groups.setdefault(short, []).append(i)

        if show_progress:
            print(f"[Sample {i+1}/{num_samples}] → {short!r}")

        #########################################################
        # NEW
        # Early stop if one answer already meets >= 50% majority
        if early_stop and counts[short] > num_samples / 2:
            majority_winners = [short]
            final_answer = short
            break
        #########################################################

    if final_answer is None:
        mc = counts.most_common()
        if mc:
            top_freq = mc[0][1]
            majority_winners = [s for s, f in mc if f == top_freq]
            final_answer = mc[0][0] if len(majority_winners) == 1 else None

    return {
        "full_answers": full_answers,
        "short_answers": short_answers,
        "counts": dict(counts),
        "groups": groups,
        "majority_winners": majority_winners,
        "final_answer": final_answer,
    }


def evaluate_math500_stream(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    device,
    math_data,
    out_path=None,
    max_new_tokens=2048,
    verbose=False,
    prompt_suffix="",    # NEW
    temperature=1.0,     # NEW
    top_p=1.0,           # NEW
    seed=None,           # NEW
    num_samples=10,      # NEW
    early_stop=False,    # NEW
):

    if out_path is None:
        dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")
        out_path = Path(f"math500-{dev_name}.jsonl")

    num_examples = len(math_data)
    num_correct = 0
    start_time = time.time()

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for i, row in enumerate(math_data, start=1):
            prompt = render_prompt(row["problem"])

            ###################################################################
            # NEW
            prompt += prompt_suffix
            results = self_consistency_vote(
                model=model,
                tokenizer=tokenizer,
                prompt=prompt,
                device=device,
                num_samples=num_samples,
                temperature=temperature,
                top_p=top_p,
                max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
                show_progress=False,
                show_long_answer=False,
                seed=seed,
                early_stop=early_stop,
            )

            # If final_answer was not determined (tie),
            # resolve it by first appearance
            if results["final_answer"] is None:
                extracted = results["majority_winners"][0]
            else:
                extracted = results["final_answer"]

            # extracted = extract_final_candidate(
            #     gen_text
            # )

            # Optionally, get long answer
            if extracted is not None:
                for idx, s in enumerate(results["short_answers"]):
                    if s == extracted:
                        long_answer = results["full_answers"][idx]
                        break
            gen_text = long_answer
            ###################################################################

            is_correct = grade_answer(
                extracted, row["answer"]
            )
            num_correct += int(is_correct)

            record = {
                "index": i,
                "problem": row["problem"],
                "gtruth_answer": row["answer"],
                "generated_text": gen_text,
                "extracted": extracted,
                "correct": bool(is_correct),
            }
            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

            progress_msg = eta_progress_message(
                processed=i,
                total=num_examples,
                start_time=start_time,
                show_eta=True,
                label="MATH-500",
            )
            print(progress_msg, end="\r", flush=True)
            if verbose:
                print(
                    f"\n\n{'='*50}\n{progress_msg}\n"
                    f"{'='*50}\nExtracted: {extracted}\n"
                    f"Expected:  {row['answer']}\n"
                    f"Correct so far: {num_correct}\n{'-'*50}"
                )

    seconds_elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    acc = num_correct / num_examples if num_examples else 0.0
    print(f"\nAccuracy: {acc*100:.1f}% ({num_correct}/{num_examples})")
    print(f"Total time: {seconds_elapsed/60:.1f} min")
    print(f"Logs written to: {out_path}")
    return num_correct, num_examples, acc

    parser.add_argument(

# Copyright (c) [Name] under Apache License 2.0 (see LICENSE.txt)
# Source for "Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch)": https://mng.bz/lZ5B
# Code repository: https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import time

import torch
from collections import Counter

from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import get_device
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import (
    load_math500_test,
    eta_progress_message,
    render_prompt,
    grade_answer,
    load_model_and_tokenizer,
    extract_final_candidate,
)
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch04 import (
    top_p_filter,
    scale_logits_by_temperature,
)
from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import KVCache


@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_top_p_batched(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens,
    eos_token_id=None,
    temperature=0.0,
    top_p=None,
    seed=None,
    seed_offset=0,
):
    """Batched variant of top-p sampling used for self-consistency."""

    model.eval()
    cache = KVCache(n_layers=model.cfg["n_layers"])
    model.reset_kv_cache()

    device = token_ids.device
    batch_size = token_ids.size(0)
    generated_tokens = [[] for _ in range(batch_size)]
    finished = torch.zeros(batch_size, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)

    rngs = None
    if seed is not None and temperature not in (None, 1.0):
        rngs = []
        for idx in range(batch_size):
            gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu")
            gen.manual_seed(seed + seed_offset + idx + 1)
            rngs.append(gen)

    out = model(token_ids, cache=cache)[:, -1]

    for step in range(max_new_tokens):
        if temperature is None or temperature == 0.0:
            next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
            if eos_token_id is not None and torch.any(finished):
                fill = torch.full_like(next_token, eos_token_id)
                next_token = torch.where(finished.view(-1, 1), fill, next_token)
        else:
            logits = scale_logits_by_temperature(out, temperature)
            probas = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
            probas = top_p_filter(probas, top_p)
            probas_cpu = probas.cpu()
            sampled = []
            for idx in range(batch_size):
                if finished[idx]:
                    fill_value = eos_token_id if eos_token_id is not None else 0
                    sampled.append(torch.tensor([fill_value], dtype=torch.long))
                    continue
                generator = rngs[idx] if rngs is not None else None
                sampled.append(
                    torch.multinomial(
                        probas_cpu[idx],
                        num_samples=1,
                        generator=generator,
                    )
                )
            next_token = torch.stack(sampled, dim=0).to(device)

        eos_mask = torch.zeros(batch_size, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
        if eos_token_id is not None:
            eos_mask = next_token.squeeze(1) == eos_token_id

        for idx in range(batch_size):
            if finished[idx]:
                continue
            token_val = next_token[idx, 0].item()
            if eos_token_id is not None and token_val == eos_token_id:
                finished[idx] = True
            else:
                generated_tokens[idx].append(token_val)

        if eos_token_id is not None:
            finished = finished | eos_mask

        if torch.all(finished):
            break

        if step + 1 < max_new_tokens:  # Skips the forward pass after the last token is generated
            out = model(next_token, cache=cache)[:, -1]

    return generated_tokens


def self_consistency_vote(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    prompt,
    device,
    num_samples=10,
    temperature=0.8,
    top_p=0.9,
    max_new_tokens=2048,
    show_progress=True,
    show_long_answer=False,
    seed=None,
):
    full_answers, short_answers = [], []
    counts = Counter()
    groups = {}
    majority_winners, final_answer = [], None

    batch_size = max(1, num_samples)
    prompt_ids = torch.tensor(
        tokenizer.encode(prompt), device=device, dtype=torch.long
    ).unsqueeze(0)

    while len(full_answers) < num_samples:
        remaining = num_samples - len(full_answers)
        current_batch = min(batch_size, remaining)
        token_batch = prompt_ids.repeat(current_batch, 1)

        token_lists = generate_text_top_p_batched(
            model=model,
            token_ids=token_batch,
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
            eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id,
            temperature=temperature,
            top_p=top_p,
            seed=seed,
            seed_offset=len(full_answers),
        )
        answers = [tokenizer.decode(tokens) for tokens in token_lists]

        for answer in answers:
            sample_idx = len(full_answers)
            short = extract_final_candidate(answer, fallback="number_then_full")
            full_answers.append(answer)
            short_answers.append(short)
            counts[short] += 1
            groups.setdefault(short, []).append(sample_idx)

            if show_long_answer:
                print(answer)

            if show_progress:
                print(f"[Sample {sample_idx+1}/{num_samples}] → {short!r}")

    if final_answer is None:
        mc = counts.most_common()
        if mc:
            top_freq = mc[0][1]
            majority_winners = [s for s, f in mc if f == top_freq]
            final_answer = mc[0][0] if len(majority_winners) == 1 else None

    return {
        "full_answers": full_answers,
        "short_answers": short_answers,
        "counts": dict(counts),
        "groups": groups,
        "majority_winners": majority_winners,
        "final_answer": final_answer,
    }


def evaluate_math500_stream(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    device,
    math_data,
    out_path=None,
    max_new_tokens=2048,
    verbose=False,
    prompt_suffix="",
    temperature=1.0,
    top_p=1.0,
    seed=None,
    num_samples=10,
):

    if out_path is None:
        dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")
        out_path = Path(f"math500-{dev_name}.jsonl")

    num_examples = len(math_data)
    num_correct = 0
    start_time = time.time()

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for i, row in enumerate(math_data, start=1):
            prompt = render_prompt(row["problem"])

            prompt += prompt_suffix
            results = self_consistency_vote(
                model=model,
                tokenizer=tokenizer,
                prompt=prompt,
                device=device,
                num_samples=num_samples,
                temperature=temperature,
                top_p=top_p,
                max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
                show_progress=False,
                show_long_answer=False,
                seed=seed,
            )

            # If final_answer was not determined (tie),
            # resolve it by first appearance
            if results["final_answer"] is None:
                extracted = results["majority_winners"][0]
            else:
                extracted = results["final_answer"]

            # extracted = extract_final_candidate(
            #     gen_text
            # )

            # Optionally, get long answer
            long_answer = None
            if extracted is not None:
                for idx, s in enumerate(results["short_answers"]):
                    if s == extracted:
                        long_answer = results["full_answers"][idx]
                        break
            gen_text = long_answer
            ###################################################################

            is_correct = grade_answer(
                extracted, row["answer"]
            )
            num_correct += int(is_correct)

            record = {
                "index": i,
                "problem": row["problem"],
                "gtruth_answer": row["answer"],
                "generated_text": gen_text,
                "extracted": extracted,
                "correct": bool(is_correct),
            }
            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

            progress_msg = eta_progress_message(
                processed=i,
                total=num_examples,
                start_time=start_time,
                show_eta=True,
                label="MATH-500",
            )
            print(progress_msg, end="\r", flush=True)
            if verbose:
                print(
                    f"\n\n{'='*50}\n{progress_msg}\n"
                    f"{'='*50}\nExtracted: {extracted}\n"
                    f"Expected:  {row['answer']}\n"
                    f"Correct so far: {num_correct}\n{'-'*50}"
                )

    seconds_elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    acc = num_correct / num_examples if num_examples else 0.0
    print(f"\nAccuracy: {acc*100:.1f}% ({num_correct}/{num_examples})")
    print(f"Total time: {seconds_elapsed/60:.1f} min")
    print(f"Logs written to: {out_path}")
    return num_correct, num_examples, acc


def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--device",
        type=str,
        default="auto",
        help="Device to use: 'auto', or any torch device string like 'cpu', 'cuda', 'cuda:0', 'mps'.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--which_model",
        type=str,
        default="base",
        choices=["base", "reasoning", "instruct"],
        help="Model variant to load",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dataset_size",
        type=int,
        default=10,
        help="Number of MATH-500 examples to evaluate",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max_new_tokens",
        type=int,
        default=2048,
        help="Max new tokens for generation",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--compile",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable torch.compile for the model.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        help="Print per-sample correctness while evaluating.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--prompt_suffix",
        type=str,
        default="\n\nExplain step by step.",
        help="Adds a chain-of-thought prompt",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--seed",
        type=int,
        default=42,
        help="Random seed for self-consistency sampling",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--temperature",
        type=float,
        default=1.0,
        help="Setting for temperature scaling",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--top_p",
        type=float,
        default=1.0,
        help="Threshold for top-p filtering (nucleus sampling)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--num_samples",
        type=int,
        default=3,
        help="Number of samples for self-consistency sampling",
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = parse_args()

    if args.device == "auto":
        device = get_device()
    else:
        device = torch.device(args.device)

    which_model = args.which_model
    dataset_size = args.dataset_size
    max_new_tokens = args.max_new_tokens
    use_compile = args.compile

    print("Model:", which_model)
    print("Device:", device)
    dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")

    math_data = load_math500_test()

    if args.which_model == "instruct":
        which_model = "reasoning"
    else:
        which_model = args.which_model

    model, tokenizer = load_model_and_tokenizer(
        which_model=which_model,
        device=device,
        use_compile=args.compile
    )
    if args.which_model == "instruct":
        tokenizer.add_thinking = False

    model.eval()
    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("high")

    num_correct, num_examples, acc = evaluate_math500_stream(
        model=model,
        out_path=f"math500_{which_model}-{dev_name}-evaluate-script.jsonl",
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        device=device,
        math_data=math_data[:dataset_size],
        max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
        verbose=args.verbose,
        prompt_suffix=args.prompt_suffix,
        temperature=args.temperature,
        top_p=args.top_p,
        seed=args.seed,
        num_samples=args.num_samples,
    )

from .ch02 import generate_text_basic_stream_cache
from .ch03 import extract_final_candidate
from .qwen3 import KVCache

from collections import Counter
import torch


def generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device, max_new_tokens,
    verbose=False,
    generate_func=None,  # New
    **generate_kwargs  # New
):

    if generate_func is None:  # New
        generate_func = generate_text_basic_stream_cache

    input_ids = torch.tensor(
        tokenizer.encode(prompt), device=device
        ).unsqueeze(0)

    generated_ids = []
    for token in generate_func(  # New
        model=model,
        token_ids=input_ids,
        max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
        eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id,
        **generate_kwargs,  # New
    ):
        next_token_id = token.squeeze(0)
        generated_ids.append(next_token_id.item())

        if verbose:
            print(
                tokenizer.decode(next_token_id.tolist()),
                end="",
                flush=True
            )
    return tokenizer.decode(generated_ids)


def plot_scores_bar(
    next_token_logits, start=19_800, end=19_900,
    arrow=True, ylabel="Logit value"
):

    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    # Select vocabulary subsection
    x = torch.arange(start, end)

    # .cpu() is a shortcut for to(torch.device("cpu"))
    logits_section = next_token_logits[0, start:end].float().cpu()

    # Plot logits
    plt.bar(x, logits_section)
    plt.xlabel("Vocabulary index")
    plt.ylabel(ylabel)

    # Highlight max logit
    if arrow:
        max_idx = torch.argmax(logits_section)
        plt.annotate(
            "Berlin",
            xy=(x[max_idx], logits_section[max_idx]),
            xytext=(x[max_idx] - 25, logits_section[max_idx] - 2),
            arrowprops={
                "facecolor": "black", "arrowstyle": "->", "lw": 1.5
            },
            fontsize=10,
        )

    plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def scale_logits_by_temperature(logits, temperature):
    if temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Temperature must be positive")
    return logits / temperature


def plot_logits_with_temperature(
    next_token_logits, start=19_800, end=19_900,
    temps=(0.5, 5.0),
):

    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    x = torch.arange(start, end)
    logits_orig = next_token_logits[0, start:end].float().cpu()

    # Apply temperature scaling
    logits_scaled = [
        scale_logits_by_temperature(logits_orig, T) for T in temps
    ]
    # Plot logits
    plt.plot(x, logits_orig, label="Original logits", lw=2)
    plt.plot(
        x, logits_scaled[0],
        label=f"T={temps[0]} (sharper)", ls="--", lw=1
    )
    plt.plot(
        x, logits_scaled[1],
        label=f"T={temps[1]} (flatter)", ls=":", lw=3
    )

    # Highlight max logit
    max_idx = torch.argmax(logits_orig)
    plt.annotate(
        "Berlin",
        xy=(x[max_idx], logits_orig[max_idx]),
        xytext=(x[max_idx] - 25, logits_orig[max_idx] + 2),
        arrowprops={"facecolor": "black", "arrowstyle": "->", "lw": 1.5},
        fontsize=12,
    )

    plt.xlabel("Vocabulary index")
    plt.ylabel("Logit value")
    plt.legend()
    plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def count_samples(probas, num_samples=1000, threshold=1, tokenizer=None):
    # Draw samples according to probabilities
    samples = torch.multinomial(
        probas.cpu(), num_samples=num_samples, replacement=True
    )

    # Count how often each index was selected
    counts = torch.bincount(samples.squeeze(0), minlength=1)

    # Print results
    for i, c in enumerate(counts):
        if c > threshold:
            if tokenizer is None:
                print(f"Vocab index {i}: {c.item()}x")
            else:
                print(f"'{tokenizer.decode([i])}': {c.item()}x")


@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_temp_stream_cache(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens,
    eos_token_id=None,
    temperature=0.
):
    model.eval()
    cache = KVCache(n_layers=model.cfg["n_layers"])
    model.reset_kv_cache()

    # Step 3.1: Get logits
    out = model(token_ids, cache=cache)[:, -1]
    for step in range(max_new_tokens):

        ########################################
        # NEW:
        orig_device = token_ids.device

        if temperature is None or temperature == 0.0:
            next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        else:
            # Step 3.2: Apply temperature scaling on logits
            logits = scale_logits_by_temperature(out, temperature)

            # Step 3.3: Convert to probabilities
            probas = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)

            # Step 3.4: Sample token according to probabilities
            next_token = torch.multinomial(probas.cpu(), num_samples=1)
            next_token = next_token.to(orig_device)

        #########################################
        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and torch.all(next_token == eos_token_id)):
            break

        yield next_token
        if step + 1 < max_new_tokens:  # Skips the forward pass after the last token is generated
            out = model(next_token, cache=cache)[:, -1]


def top_p_filter(probas, top_p):
    if top_p is None or top_p >= 1.0:
        return probas

    # Step 4.1: Sort by descending probability
    sorted_probas, sorted_idx = torch.sort(probas, dim=1, descending=True)

    # Step 4.2: Cumulative sum
    cumprobas = torch.cumsum(sorted_probas, dim=1)

    # Step 4.3.1: Keep tokens where prefix cumulative mass (before token) is < top_ps
    # Example: [0.5, 0.41, 0.09] with top_p=0.9 should keep the first two tokens
    prefix = cumprobas - sorted_probas   # cumulative mass before each token
    keep = prefix < top_p
    # Always keep at least one token (fallback for very small/non-positive top_p)
    keep[:, 0] = True

    # Step 4.3.2: Zero out beyond cutoff
    kept_sorted = torch.where(
        keep, sorted_probas,
        torch.zeros_like(sorted_probas)
    )
    # Step 4.3.3: Map back to original order
    filtered = torch.zeros_like(probas).scatter(1, sorted_idx, kept_sorted)

    # Step 4.4: Renormalize to sum to 1
    denom = torch.sum(filtered, dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
    # keepdim=True is technically not necessary but it makes the code work in batched cases
    return filtered / denom


@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_top_p_stream_cache(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens,
    eos_token_id=None,
    temperature=0.,
    top_p=None
):
    model.eval()
    cache = KVCache(n_layers=model.cfg["n_layers"])
    model.reset_kv_cache()

    # Step 3.1: Get logits
    out = model(token_ids, cache=cache)[:, -1]
    for step in range(max_new_tokens):

        orig_device = token_ids.device

        if temperature is None or temperature == 0.0:
            next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        else:
            # Step 3.2: Apply temperature scaling on logits
            logits = scale_logits_by_temperature(out, temperature)

            # Step 3.3: Convert to probabilities
            probas = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)

            # (New) Step 4: Apply top-p filter to probabilities
            probas = top_p_filter(probas, top_p)

            # Step 3.4: Sample token according to probabilities
            next_token = torch.multinomial(probas.cpu(), num_samples=1)
            next_token = next_token.to(orig_device)

        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and torch.all(next_token == eos_token_id)):
            break

        yield next_token
        if step + 1 < max_new_tokens:  # Skips the forward pass after the last token is generated
            out = model(next_token, cache=cache)[:, -1]


def self_consistency_vote(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
    num_samples=10, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.9, max_new_tokens=2048,
    show_progress=True, show_long_answer=False, seed=None,
):
    full_answers, short_answers = [], []

    # 1) Sample multiple answers
    for i in range(num_samples):
        if seed is not None:
            torch.manual_seed(seed + i + 1)

        answer = generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
            model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer, prompt=prompt, device=device,
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, verbose=show_long_answer,
            generate_func=generate_text_top_p_stream_cache,
            temperature=temperature, top_p=top_p,
        )

        # 2) Extract the final (short) answer from each answer
        short = extract_final_candidate(
            answer, fallback="number_then_full"
        )
        full_answers.append(answer)
        short_answers.append(short)
        if show_progress:
            print(f"[Sample {i+1}/{num_samples}] → {short!r}")

    # 3) Choose the most frequent final answer (self-consistency vote)
    counts = Counter(short_answers)
    groups = {s: [] for s in counts}
    for idx, s in enumerate(short_answers):
        groups[s].append(idx)

    mc = counts.most_common()
    if not mc:
        majority_winners, final_answer = [], None
    else:
        top_freq = mc[0][1]
        majority_winners = [s for s, f in mc if f == top_freq]
        final_answer = mc[0][0] if len(majority_winners) == 1 else None

    return {
        "full_answers": full_answers,
        "short_answers": short_answers,
        "counts": dict(counts),
        "groups": groups,
        "majority_winners": majority_winners,
        "final_answer": final_answer,
    }

from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import KVCache

@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_temp_stream_cache(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens,
    eos_token_id=None,
    temperature=0.
):
    model.eval()
    cache = KVCache(n_layers=model.cfg["n_layers"])
    model.reset_kv_cache()

    # Step 3.1: Get logits
    out = model(token_ids, cache=cache)[:, -1]
    for step in range(max_new_tokens):

        ########################################
        # NEW:
        orig_device = token_ids.device

        if temperature is None or temperature == 0.0:
            next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        else:
            # Step 3.2: Apply temperature scaling on logits
            logits = scale_logits_by_temperature(out, temperature)

            # Step 3.3: Convert to probabilities
            probas = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)

            # Step 3.4: Sample token according to probabilities
            next_token = torch.multinomial(probas.cpu(), num_samples=1)
            next_token = next_token.to(orig_device)
            
        #########################################
        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and torch.all(next_token == eos_token_id)):
            break

        yield next_token
        if step + 1 < max_new_tokens:  # Skips the forward pass after the last token is generated
            out = model(next_token, cache=cache)[:, -1]

# ---- notebook cell 71 ----
def top_p_filter(probas, top_p):
    if top_p is None or top_p >= 1.0:
        return probas

    # Step 4.1: Sort by descending probability
    sorted_probas, sorted_idx = torch.sort(probas, dim=1, descending=True)

    # Step 4.2: Cumulative sum
    cumprobas = torch.cumsum(sorted_probas, dim=1)

    # Step 4.3.1: Keep tokens where prefix cumulative mass (before token) is < top_p
    # Example: [0.5, 0.41, 0.09] with top_p=0.9 should keep the first two tokens
    prefix = cumprobas - sorted_probas   # cumulative mass before each token
    keep = prefix < top_p
    # Always keep at least one token (fallback for very small/non-positive top_p)
    keep[:, 0] = True    

    # Step 4.3.2: Zero out beyond cutoff
    kept_sorted = torch.where(
        keep, sorted_probas,
        torch.zeros_like(sorted_probas)
    )
    # Step 4.3.3: Map back to original order
    filtered = torch.zeros_like(probas).scatter(1, sorted_idx, kept_sorted)

    # Step 4.4: Renormalize to sum to 1
    denom = torch.sum(filtered, dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
    return filtered / denom

@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_top_p_stream_cache(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens,
    eos_token_id=None,
    temperature=0.,
    top_p=None
):
    model.eval()
    cache = KVCache(n_layers=model.cfg["n_layers"])
    model.reset_kv_cache()

    # Step 3.1: Get logits
    out = model(token_ids, cache=cache)[:, -1]
    for step in range(max_new_tokens):

        orig_device = token_ids.device

        if temperature is None or temperature == 0.0:
            next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        else:
            # Step 3.2: Apply temperature scaling on logits
            logits = scale_logits_by_temperature(out, temperature)

            # Step 3.3: Convert to probabilities
            probas = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)

            # (New) Step 4: Apply top-p filter to probabilities
            probas = top_p_filter(probas, top_p)            

            # Step 3.4: Sample token according to probabilities
            next_token = torch.multinomial(probas.cpu(), num_samples=1)
            next_token = next_token.to(orig_device)

        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and torch.all(next_token == eos_token_id)):
            break

        yield next_token
        if step + 1 < max_new_tokens:  # Skips the forward pass after the last token is generated
            out = model(next_token, cache=cache)[:, -1]

# ---- notebook cell 82 ----
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import extract_final_candidate
from collections import Counter

def self_consistency_vote(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
    num_samples=10, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.9, max_new_tokens=2048,
    show_progress=True, show_long_answer=False, seed=None,
):
    full_answers, short_answers = [], []

    # 1) Sample multiple answers
    for i in range(num_samples):
        if seed is not None:
            torch.manual_seed(seed + i + 1)

        answer = generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
            model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer, prompt=prompt, device=device,
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, verbose=show_long_answer,
            generate_func=generate_text_top_p_stream_cache,
            temperature=temperature, top_p=top_p,
        )

        # 2) Extract the final (short) answer from each answer
        short = extract_final_candidate(
            answer, fallback="number_then_full"
        )
        full_answers.append(answer)
        short_answers.append(short)
        if show_progress:
            print(f"[Sample {i+1}/{num_samples}] → {short!r}")

    # 3) Choose the most frequent final answer (self-consistency vote)
    counts = Counter(short_answers)
    groups = {s: [] for s in counts}
    for idx, s in enumerate(short_answers):
        groups[s].append(idx)

    mc = counts.most_common()
    if not mc:
        majority_winners, final_answer = [], None
    else:
        top_freq = mc[0][1]
        majority_winners = [s for s, f in mc if f == top_freq]
        final_answer = mc[0][0] if len(majority_winners) == 1 else None

    return {
        "full_answers": full_answers,
        "short_answers": short_answers,
        "counts": dict(counts),
        "groups": groups,
        "majority_winners": majority_winners,
        "final_answer": final_answer,
    }

05.1Chapter 5 — Inference-time scaling via self-refinement

Scoring and iteratively improving model responses

Chapter 4 me humne inference-time scaling seekha tha — model ko dobara train kiye bina, zyada compute kharch karke behtar jawab paana. Is chapter me hum usi idea ko ek kadam aage le jaate hain: self-refinement, jisme model apna hi jawab baar-baar sudhaarta hai.

Teen inference-time tareeke — ek nazar me

  • Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting: prompt me "Explain step by step" jod do — base model lambi reasoning likhta hai aur accuracy badh jaati hai. Reasoning model ko isse zyada fayda nahi hota, kyunki woh pehle se hi reasoning likhta hai.
  • Self-consistency: model se kai jawab generate karwao aur majority vote se final jawab chuno. Simple hai, lekin accuracy me bada fayda deta hai — isliye accuracy latency se zyada important ho to ye common choice hai.
  • Self-refinement (is chapter ka topic): kai jawab generate karne ke bajay ek hi jawab ko baar-baar critique karke sudhaaro.

Self-consistency ki ek kami

Majority vote ke liye chhote, compare karne layak jawab chahiye hote hain — jaise ek boxed number. Lambe, open-ended jawabon pe vote karna mushkil hai. Self-refinement is mamle me zyada versatile hai, kyunki woh ek hi jawab ko sudhaarta hai, vote nahi maangta.

Is chapter ka roadmap

  • Pehle scoring: jawabon ko rank karne ke liye scoring functions banayenge — pehle ek simple rule-based scorer, phir token probability aur log-probability par based scorer.
  • Phir self-refinement: in scorers ko ek loop me use karenge jo draft jawab likhta hai, uski critique karta hai, aur revised jawab banata hai.
  • Log-probability kyun important hai: ye concept chapter 6 me dobara aayega — wahan ye sirf scoring ke liye nahi, training objective ke andar use hoga.
Yaad rakho: Inference-time scaling ka matlab hai — training ke bina, inference par zyada compute kharch karke accuracy badhana. Self-refinement usi ka teesra tareeka hai: ek jawab, kai sudhaar.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 5

05.2Chapter 5 — Inference-time scaling via self-refinement

Scoring LLM responses with a rule-based score

Kisi bhi jawab ko sudhaarne se pehle ye jaanna zaroori hai ki kaunsa jawab behtar hai. Iske liye ek scorer chahiye — ek function jo har jawab ko number de. Sabse pehle hum sabse simple scorer banate hain: rule-based scorer.

Model load karna

Chapter ki shuruaat pehle jaise hi hoti hai — Qwen3 base model aur tokenizer load karte hain. Book CPU par chalane ki salah deti hai, kyunki is chapter me bahut chhoti decimal values ke saath kaam hota hai aur CPU par results zyada consistent rehte hain. GPU par chhote numerical farak aa sakte hain, jo pehli baar padhne par confuse kar sakte hain.

Scorer ke teen tareeke

  • Heuristic (rule-based): simple niyam — jaise final answer boxed hai ya nahi, jawab kitna chhota hai.
  • LLM-as-a-judge: ek aur LLM jawab ko rate kare. Ye appendix F me detail me hai.
  • Probability-based: model khud apne jawab ko kitni probability deta hai — ye aage ke sections me hai.

Heuristic scorer kaise kaam karta hai

Book ka heuristic_score function teen cheezein dekhta hai. Pehle, kya jawab me \boxed{} format me final answer hai — is par sabse bada bonus (2.0 points). Agar boxed nahi hai lekin number nikaala ja sakta hai, to chhota bonus (1.0). Aur aakhir me brevity bonus — chhota jawab, zyada score — jo 1.5 * exp(-length / 500) formula se milta hai.

python
def heuristic_score(answer, brevity_bonus=500.0,
                    boxed_bonus=2.0, extract_bonus=1.0):
    score = 0.0
    cand = extract_final_candidate(answer, fallback="none")
    if cand:
        score += boxed_bonus          # boxed final answer
    else:
        cand = extract_final_candidate(answer, fallback="number_only")
        if cand:
            score += extract_bonus    # sirf number mila
    score += 1.5 * math.exp(-len(answer) / brevity_bonus)
    return score

Example: lamba vs chhota jawab

Dono jawab sahi the (83), lekin ek lamba tha aur ek chhota. Lamba jawab ka score 2.088 aur chhote ka 2.517 aaya — matlab scorer ne chhote, saaf jawab ko prefer kiya. Yahan "behtar" ka matlab correctness nahi, format aur brevity hai.

Scorer ko tune kaise karein

  • Agar scorer aise jawab chun raha hai jinka final answer nikaalna mushkil hai, to extraction bonus badhao.
  • Agar scorer lambe, ghumaane wale jawab chun raha hai, to brevity pressure badhao.
  • Agar scorer bahut chhote, adhoore jawab chunne lage, to brevity penalty kam karo ya extraction bonus badhao.
  • Exact numbers se zyada unke relative scale matter karte hain — boxed bonus (2.0) extract bonus (1.0) se bada hai, isliye boxed jawab hamesha jeetega.

Is scorer ke do aur use

Ye scorer sirf self-refinement ke liye nahi hai. Ise self-consistency me tie-breaker ki tarah bhi use kar sakte ho — jab do jawabon ko barabar vote milein, to scorer wala jeetega. Aur Best-of-N setup me majority vote ki jagah scorer se best jawab chuna ja sakta hai.

Yaad rakho: Is section me chapter 3 wala verifier use nahi hota, kyunki verifier ko sahi jawab pehle se pata hona chahiye. Scorer tab kaam aata hai jab sahi jawab pata nahi hai — woh sirf jawab ki quality ko rank karta hai.

05.3Chapter 5 — Inference-time scaling via self-refinement

Understanding token probability scores

Rule-based scorer sirf format dekhta hai — model ke andar kya chal raha hai, ye nahi. Ab hum model ke apne confidence ko measure karte hain: token probability. Matlab, model khud apne jawab ke har token ko kitni probability deta hai.

Logits se probability tak

Har step par model vocabulary ke har token ko ek score deta hai — isse logit kehte hain. Softmax se ye logits probabilities me badal jaate hain, jinka total 1 hota hai. Text generate karte time model sabse zyada probability wala token chunta hai. Yahan hum generate nahi kar rahe — hum sirf scores ko dekh rahe hain.

Example: Berlin vs Bridge

Prompt hai "The capital of Germany is" — model ko do candidate next tokens compare karne hain: "Berlin" aur "Bridge". "Berlin" ko bahut zyada probability milti hai, "Bridge" ko bahut kam. Isse pata chalta hai ki model ko pehla jawab zyada "natural" lagta hai.

Sequence likelihood kya hai

  • Ek jawab ke saare tokens ki probabilities ko multiply kar do — ye joint probability ya sequence likelihood hoti hai.
  • Agar jawab ke tokens ko model consistently high probability deta hai, to jawab model ki apni pasand ke zyada kareeb hai.
  • Agar kai tokens ko bahut kam probability mili, to model khud us jawab ko strongly support nahi karta.

Confidence matlab correctness nahi

Ye sabse important warning hai: high confidence ka matlab sahi jawab nahi hota. Model galat jawab ko bhi high probability de sakta hai, sirf isliye kyunki woh pattern usne training me bahut dekha hai. Isliye confidently galat jawab pakadne ke liye verifier, self-consistency, ya external tools chahiye hote hain.

Ye concept aage kyun kaam aayega

Token probability sirf scoring ke liye nahi hai. Chapter 6 me yehi log-probability training objective ke andar aayegi — GRPO loss ka core hissa banegi. Isliye is chapter me is par itna time diya gaya hai.

Yaad rakho: Probability model ka confidence batati hai, correctness nahi. Ek fluent, confident jawab bhi galat ho sakta hai — scoring ko hamesha verifier ya vote ke saath combine karo.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 5
← Previous05.2 · Scoring LLM responses with a rule-based score→ Next05.4 · From token probability scores to log-probabilities
05.4Chapter 5 — Inference-time scaling via self-refinement

From token probability scores to log-probabilities

Probabilities ko multiply karne me ek practical problem hai: bahut chhoti values ko multiply karte-karte result zero ke itna kareeb aa jata hai ki computer use zero round kar de — isse numerical underflow kehte hain. Iska solution hai log-probability (logprob).

Logprob kya hai

Probability ka natural logarithm lo — bas. torch.log_softmax ek hi step me softmax aur log dono kar deta hai. Example: logits [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2] par probabilities [0.009, 0.017, 0.034, 0.066, 0.129, 0.252, 0.491] milti hain, aur logprobs [-4.71, -4.04, -3.38, -2.71, -2.04, -1.38, -0.71].

Logprob ke do bade fayde

  • Ordering same rehti hai: bada logit = badi probability = kam negative logprob. Log lene se ranking nahi badalti, sirf scale badalta hai.
  • Multiply, add ban jata hai: log ka niyam hai — log(a × b) = log(a) + log(b). Pure sequence ki joint probability nikaalne ke liye bahut chhoti values multiply karne ke bajay, unke logprobs ko add kar do. Ye numerically stable hai.

Zero ke kareeb matlab behtar

Logprob me 0 sabse achha hai (probability 1 ke barabar), aur bahut negative value sabse bura. "Berlin" wale sequence ka total logprob -16.6 aaya, "Bridge" wale ka -29.9 — ek token badalne se bhi farak saaf dikh gaya, jabki raw probability me dono hi zero ke kareeb dikhte.

Average logprob scorer (Section 5.6)

Scorer banane ke liye do badlaav karte hain. Pehle, prompt ke tokens ko score se bahar rakho — sirf answer ke tokens ginon. Doosra, sum ke bajay average lo, taaki alag-alag length ke jawabon ki fair comparison ho sake. Isse avg_logprob_answer function banta hai — jo aage self-refinement loop me scorer ki tarah use hoga.

python
# token logprobs nikaalo, phir answer tokens ka average lo
logprobs = torch.log_softmax(logits, dim=-1)
next_token_logps = logprobs[t_idx, next_tokens]
return torch.mean(next_token_logps).item()  # sum nahi, mean

Sum vs average — kab kaunsa

  • Sum (sequence logprob): pure sequence ki likelihood — chapter 6 ke GRPO me use hoga, kyunki wahan ek rollout ko ek hi signal milta hai.
  • Average: length-normalized score — scoring aur comparison ke liye behtar, kyunki lamba jawab sirf lamba hone ki wajah se penalize nahi hota.
Yaad rakho: Logprob me kam negative = zyada confident. Aur jab bhi bahut saari probabilities multiply karni hon, log space me kaam karo — add karna multiply karne se hamesha stable hota hai.
SOURCESource: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch), Manning, Chapter 5
← Previous05.3 · Understanding token probability scores→ Next05.5 · Self-refinement through iterative feedback
05.5Chapter 5 — Inference-time scaling via self-refinement

Self-refinement through iterative feedback

Ab chapter ka core technique: self-refinement. Model pehle ek draft jawab likhta hai, phir khud uski critique karta hai, aur phir critique ke hisaab se revised jawab banata hai. Teen steps, ek loop.

Teen steps, ek example ke saath

  • Step 1 — Draft: Sawaal tha "Half the value of 3x-9 is x+37, x kya hai?" Model ne pehle galat jawab diya: \boxed{18} (sahi jawab 83 hai).
  • Step 2 — Critique: Critique prompt me original sawaal aur draft dono diye jaate hain, aur model se kaha jata hai ki logical error, missing step ya arithmetic mistake dhoondhe aur fix plan likhe. Model ne sahi equation (3x-9)/2 = x + 37 pehchaan li aur 5-step fix plan likha — critique me ek chhoti galti bhi thi, phir bhi fix plan sahi tha.
  • Step 3 — Refine: Refine prompt me sawaal, purana jawab aur critique teeno diye jaate hain. Model ne revised jawab me sahi answer diya: \boxed{83}.

Critique galat bhi ho to bhi kaam karta hai

Book me ek important observation hai: critique ke kuch hisse galat bhi ho sakte hain, phir bhi woh useful hoti hai — bas woh model ko behtar revision ki taraf dhakel de. Critique ka har shabd sahi hona zaroori nahi hai.

Loop ko automate karna (Section 5.8)

self_refinement_loop function ye teen steps iterations baar chalata hai. Har iteration ke baad scorer se pehle aur baad ka score compare karta hai — revised jawab tabhi accept hota hai jab uska score pehle se kam na ho (revised_score >= current_score). Agar score_fn=None ho, to score hamesha 0.0 hota hai aur har revision accept ho jata hai.

python
results = self_refinement_loop(
    model, tokenizer, raw_prompt, device,
    iterations=2, score_fn=avg_logprob_score,
    temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, verbose=True)
# [Refinement 1/2] Current: 10  Revised: 83
#   Score before: -0.855  Score after: -0.226
# [Refinement 2/2] Current: 83  Revised: 83
#   Score before: -0.226  Score after: -1.320

MATH-500 par results — sachai kya hai

Book ne MATH-500 par test kiya. Base model ki accuracy 15.2% thi. Self-refinement bina scorer ke, 1 iteration me 25.0% tak gayi — lekin 2 iterations me gir ke 22.0% ho gayi. Reasoning model par heuristic scorer ke saath 48.2% se 57.8% tak improvement mila. Lekin average logprob scorer aksar behtar nahi tha — woh fluent aur familiar jawabon ko prefer karta hai, chahe woh galat hon.

Self-refinement vs self-consistency

  • Is model aur is task par self-consistency, self-refinement se zyada effective thi — simple hone ke bawjood self-consistency widely use hoti hai.
  • Self-refinement bahut mehenga hai: base model par 1 iteration me hi time 10 minute se 85 minute ho gaya.
  • Ek aur option hai jo book me cover nahi hua: doosre LLM se critique karwana (LLM-as-a-judge) — ek badi research team ne isi tareeke se maths competitions me gold-level performance haasil ki thi.
Yaad rakho: Scorer hamesha madad nahi karta — kabhi-kabhi woh sahi jawab ko galat se badal deta hai. Kaunsa scorer use karna hai, ye experiment karke benchmark par decide karo, assumption se nahi.

import argparse

import time

import torch
from collections import Counter

from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import get_device
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import (
    load_math500_test,
    eta_progress_message,
    render_prompt,
    grade_answer,
    load_model_and_tokenizer,
    extract_final_candidate,
)
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch04 import (
    generate_text_stream_concat_flex,

)

    avg_logprob_answer

def self_consistency_vote(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    prompt,
    device,
    num_samples=10,
    temperature=0.8,
    top_p=0.9,
    max_new_tokens=2048,
    show_progress=True,
    show_long_answer=False,
    seed=None,
    scoring="heuristic",  # NEW (Best-of-N)
):
    full_answers, short_answers = [], []
    counts = Counter()
    groups = {}
    majority_winners, final_answer = [], None
    best_score, best_idx = float("-inf"), None  # NEW (Best-of-N)

    for i in range(num_samples):
        if seed is not None:
            torch.manual_seed(seed + i + 1)

        answer = generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
            model=model,
            tokenizer=tokenizer,
            prompt=prompt,
            device=device,
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
            verbose=show_long_answer,
            generate_func=generate_text_top_p_stream_cache,
            temperature=temperature,
            top_p=top_p,
        )

        short = extract_final_candidate(answer, fallback="number_then_full")
        full_answers.append(answer)
        short_answers.append(short)
        counts[short] += 1
        if short in groups:  # NEW (Best-of-N)
            groups[short].append(i)  # NEW (Best-of-N)
        else:  # NEW (Best-of-N)
            groups[short] = [i]  # NEW (Best-of-N)
        if scoring == "heuristic":  # NEW (Best-of-N)
            score = heuristic_score(answer, prompt=prompt)  # NEW (Best-of-N)
        elif scoring == "logprob":  # NEW (Best-of-N)
            score = avg_logprob_answer(  # NEW (Best-of-N)
                model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer, prompt=prompt, answer=answer, device=device  # NEW (Best-of-N)
            )  # NEW (Best-of-N)
        else:  # NEW (Best-of-N)
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown scoring method: {scoring}")  # NEW (Best-of-N)
        if score > best_score:  # NEW (Best-of-N)
            best_score, best_idx = score, i  # NEW (Best-of-N)

        if show_progress:
            print(f"[Sample {i+1}/{num_samples}] → {short!r}")

        #########################################################
        # Track best candidate; no early stopping to allow best-of-n scoring
        #########################################################

    if best_idx is not None:  # NEW (Best-of-N)
        final_answer = short_answers[best_idx]  # NEW (Best-of-N)
        majority_winners = [final_answer]  # NEW (Best-of-N)

    return {
        "full_answers": full_answers,
        "short_answers": short_answers,
        "counts": dict(counts),
        "groups": groups,
        "majority_winners": majority_winners,
        "final_answer": final_answer,
    }


def evaluate_math500_stream(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    device,
    math_data,
    out_path=None,
    max_new_tokens=2048,
    verbose=False,
    prompt_suffix="",
    temperature=1.0,
    top_p=1.0,
    seed=None,
    num_samples=10,
    scoring="heuristic",  # NEW (Best-of-N)
):

    if out_path is None:
        dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")
        out_path = Path(f"math500-{dev_name}.jsonl")

    num_examples = len(math_data)
    num_correct = 0
    start_time = time.time()

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for i, row in enumerate(math_data, start=1):
            prompt = render_prompt(row["problem"])

            ###################################################################
            prompt += prompt_suffix
            results = self_consistency_vote(
                model=model,
                tokenizer=tokenizer,
                prompt=prompt,
                device=device,
                num_samples=num_samples,
                temperature=temperature,
                top_p=top_p,
                max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
                show_progress=False,
                show_long_answer=False,
                seed=seed,
                scoring=scoring,  # NEW (Best-of-N)
            )

            extracted = results["final_answer"]  # NEW (Best-of-N)

            # extracted = extract_final_candidate(
            #     gen_text
            # )

            # Optionally, get long answer
            long_answer = None  # NEW (Best-of-N)
            if extracted is not None:
                for idx, s in enumerate(results["short_answers"]):
                    if s == extracted:
                        long_answer = results["full_answers"][idx]
                        break
            gen_text = long_answer
            ###################################################################

            is_correct = grade_answer(
                extracted, row["answer"]
            )
            num_correct += int(is_correct)

            record = {
                "index": i,
                "problem": row["problem"],
                "gtruth_answer": row["answer"],
                "generated_text": gen_text,
                "extracted": extracted,
                "correct": bool(is_correct),
            }
            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

            progress_msg = eta_progress_message(
                processed=i,
                total=num_examples,
                start_time=start_time,
                show_eta=True,
                label="MATH-500",
            )
            print(progress_msg, end="\r", flush=True)
            if verbose:
                print(
                    f"\n\n{'='*50}\n{progress_msg}\n"
                    f"{'='*50}\nExtracted: {extracted}\n"
                    f"Expected:  {row['answer']}\n"
                    f"Correct so far: {num_correct}\n{'-'*50}"
                )

    seconds_elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    acc = num_correct / num_examples if num_examples else 0.0
    print(f"\nAccuracy: {acc*100:.1f}% ({num_correct}/{num_examples})")
    print(f"Total time: {seconds_elapsed/60:.1f} min")
    print(f"Logs written to: {out_path}")
    return num_correct, num_examples, acc

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter)

import argparse

from pathlib import Path

import torch
from collections import Counter

from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import get_device
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import (
    eta_progress_message,
    render_prompt,
    grade_answer,
    load_model_and_tokenizer,
    extract_final_candidate,
)
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch04 import (
    generate_text_stream_concat_flex,
    generate_text_top_p_stream_cache,
)

def self_consistency_vote(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    prompt,
    device,
    num_samples=10,
    temperature=0.8,
    top_p=0.9,
    max_new_tokens=2048,
    show_progress=True,
    show_long_answer=False,
    seed=None,
    early_stop=True,   # NEW
):
    full_answers, short_answers = [], []
    counts = Counter()
    groups = {}
    majority_winners, final_answer = [], None

    for i in range(num_samples):
        if seed is not None:
            torch.manual_seed(seed + i + 1)

        answer = generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
            model=model,
            tokenizer=tokenizer,
            prompt=prompt,
            device=device,
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
            verbose=show_long_answer,
            generate_func=generate_text_top_p_stream_cache,
            temperature=temperature,
            top_p=top_p,
        )

        short = extract_final_candidate(answer, fallback="number_then_full")
        full_answers.append(answer)
        short_answers.append(short)
        counts[short] += 1
        groups.setdefault(short, []).append(i)

        if show_progress:
            print(f"[Sample {i+1}/{num_samples}] → {short!r}")

        #########################################################
        # NEW
        # Early stop if one answer already meets >= 50% majority
        if early_stop and counts[short] > num_samples / 2:
            majority_winners = [short]
            final_answer = short
            break
        #########################################################

    if final_answer is None:
        mc = counts.most_common()
        if mc:
            top_freq = mc[0][1]
            majority_winners = [s for s, f in mc if f == top_freq]
            final_answer = mc[0][0] if len(majority_winners) == 1 else None

    return {
        "full_answers": full_answers,
        "short_answers": short_answers,
        "counts": dict(counts),
        "groups": groups,
        "majority_winners": majority_winners,
        "final_answer": final_answer,
    }


def evaluate_math500_stream(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    device,
    math_data,
    out_path=None,
    max_new_tokens=2048,
    verbose=False,
    prompt_suffix="",    # NEW
    temperature=1.0,     # NEW
    top_p=1.0,           # NEW
    seed=None,           # NEW
    num_samples=10,      # NEW
    early_stop=False,    # NEW
    scoring="none",      # NEW2
):

    if out_path is None:
        dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")
        out_path = Path(f"math500-{dev_name}.jsonl")

    num_examples = len(math_data)
    num_correct = 0
    start_time = time.time()

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for i, row in enumerate(math_data, start=1):
            prompt = render_prompt(row["problem"])

            ###################################################################
            # NEW
            prompt += prompt_suffix
            results = self_consistency_vote(
                model=model,
                tokenizer=tokenizer,
                prompt=prompt,
                device=device,
                num_samples=num_samples,
                temperature=temperature,
                top_p=top_p,
                max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
                show_progress=False,
                show_long_answer=False,
                seed=seed,
                early_stop=early_stop,
            )

            # If final_answer was not determined (tie),
            # resolve it via scoring (or first appearance if scoring is none)  # NEW2
            if results["final_answer"] is None:  # NEW2
                if scoring == "none":  # NEW2
                    extracted = results["majority_winners"][0]  # NEW2
                else:  # NEW2
                    best = None  # NEW2
                    best_score = float("-inf")  # NEW2
                    for cand in results["majority_winners"]:  # NEW2
                        scores = []  # NEW2
                        for idx in results["groups"][cand]:  # NEW2
                            candidate_full = results["full_answers"][idx]  # NEW2
                            if scoring == "heuristic":  # NEW2
                                score = heuristic_score(candidate_full, prompt=prompt)  # NEW2
                            elif scoring == "logprob":  # NEW2
                                score = avg_logprob_answer(  # NEW2
                                    model=model,  # NEW2
                                    tokenizer=tokenizer,  # NEW2
                                    prompt=prompt,  # NEW2
                                    answer=candidate_full,  # NEW2
                                    device=device,  # NEW2
                                )  # NEW2
                            else:  # NEW2
                                score = 0.0  # NEW2
                            scores.append(float(score))  # NEW2
                        cand_score = max(scores)  # NEW2
                        if cand_score > best_score:  # NEW2
                            best_score = cand_score  # NEW2
                            best = cand  # NEW2
                    extracted = best  # NEW2
            else:  # NEW2
                extracted = results["final_answer"]  # NEW2

            # extracted = extract_final_candidate(
            #     gen_text
            # )

            # Optionally, get long answer
            if extracted is not None:
                for idx, s in enumerate(results["short_answers"]):
                    if s == extracted:
                        long_answer = results["full_answers"][idx]
                        break
            gen_text = long_answer
            ###################################################################

            is_correct = grade_answer(
                extracted, row["answer"]
            )
            num_correct += int(is_correct)

            record = {
                "index": i,
                "problem": row["problem"],
                "gtruth_answer": row["answer"],
                "generated_text": gen_text,
                "extracted": extracted,
                "correct": bool(is_correct),
            }
            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

            progress_msg = eta_progress_message(
                processed=i,
                total=num_examples,
                start_time=start_time,
                show_eta=True,
                label="MATH-500",
            )
            print(progress_msg, end="\r", flush=True)
            if verbose:
                print(
                    f"\n\n{'='*50}\n{progress_msg}\n"
                    f"{'='*50}\nExtracted: {extracted}\n"
                    f"Expected:  {row['answer']}\n"
                    f"Correct so far: {num_correct}\n{'-'*50}"
                )

    seconds_elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    acc = num_correct / num_examples if num_examples else 0.0
    print(f"\nAccuracy: {acc*100:.1f}% ({num_correct}/{num_examples})")
    print(f"Total time: {seconds_elapsed/60:.1f} min")
    print(f"Logs written to: {out_path}")
    return num_correct, num_examples, acc


def get_data():
    local_path = Path("math500_test.json")
    url = (
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/"
        "main/ch03/01_main-chapter-code/math500_test.json"
    )

    if local_path.exists():
        with local_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            math_data = json.load(f)
    else:
        r = requests.get(url, timeout=30)
        r.raise_for_status()
        math_data = r.json()

    return math_data

import argparse
import json
import time
from functools import partial
from pathlib import Path

import requests
import torch

from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import get_device
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import (
    render_prompt,
